*Review contains spoilers* Story 9/10 The story is original, well written and with a good pace. It was very interesting to see stories and events interconnect, meaning, things that happened during first episodes are brought back way later in the show at times when you don't even remember this or that happened. The anime does use comedy as a relief from tragic/tense moments, but it didn't feel overdone or like it took away from the story...tragedy and comedy usually go hand by hand and don't necessary have to compete between each other. I really liked the fighting sequences and how most of the times battles were a"free for all" kind of scenario, where X person was fighting Y person but then Z person arrived and then X and Y started fighting Z together, but when Z was gone, X and Y started fighting again. I also liked the alliances people formed for a greater objective. I must say I found this anime a lot deeper and more emotional than I thought it would be!

The are only a few weakness that prevent me from giving this section a 10. First, I did not like how Edward seemed to be more highly regarded than Alphonse, when Alphonse thought, researched, struggled, helped and sacrificed himself just as much as Edward did. I felt Al was often forgotten about while Edward was given all the spotlight and merit for things they had both done, and in fact, some of which Ed would have not been able to accomplish without Al. Second, I felt there were many things not quite explained and left me wondering. For example, how/why was the first homunculus (Father) created? In the anime, all we get to know is that Hohenheim's blood was used for it. Why were the Homunculus chasing Scar initially? Also, why was Mustang chosen as a sacrifice? Because the explanation for the other 4 was that they had already transmuted with human beings but he was forced to do it, so why him? it seemed any other alchemist would have worked. And like this, there are some details of events or characters that could have been explored a bit more so they could have made more sense for the story. Third, many characters were alchemist but at times, to solve simple issues or offer simple solutions to complex issues, they completely forgot about their powers for no apparent reason (ex: when the car in which Yoki, Heinkel, Dr. Marcoh and Al were travelling got a stuck tire, they were trying to pull it out and eventually left the car when Al could have done some alchemy to get the car moving...in fact, I kept thinking why didn't he use his powers to find a quicker way to arrive at Central instead or running?...and like this, there are plenty of examples through the anime). 

The ending is very satisfactory, although I was surprised to see almost all characters getting happy endings because of the dark and somber nature of the anime. I was ready to have either Mustang, Hawkeye or Al die. Also, ready to see Al not being able to get his body back. Don't get me wrong, I am very pleased with the ending, just a bit surprised as I was prepared for the worst. I think the best that happened was Hohenheim dying because I couldn't completely forgive or justify him leaving his children and wife behind and I don't think it would have been believable that him, Ed and Al became just one happy family after everything that happened. It would have taken a lot of time for those wounds to heal.

On a side note: am I the only one surprised that they had such high tech as Automail and could do alchemy, but they didn't even have cellphones? Very archaic communication and means of transportations...also, was I the only one worried that Ed and Al were not going to school? I mean, Edward already had a job and I guess nobody expected him to continue school, but what about Al? 

Art 9/10
I imagine a lot of money must have been invested into making this anime because the drawings look very fresh and modern, even though this is from 2009. Colors were vibrant and a lot of attention to details was made (ex: Mustang's hand wound healing slowly over the episodes, Winry's earrings holes were visible when she was not wearing her earrings, etc). I really enjoyed the art of this anime.

Sound 10/10
Voice acting was completely on point (just thinking about the desperation on Envy's voice during his last moments gives me goosebumps!!). Openings and endings were also on point, with me actually putting at least half of them in my playlist. The only thing I really hated was the voiceover of the anime's name when the show is supposed to go on commercial break!

Characters 10/10
Jesus Christ!! I find so remarkable the fact that a show can have so many characters, each of them so interesting, that it felt none of them got enough screen time. I can honestly say that no character was irrelevant and I wanted to know more about all of them. My absolute favorites are Mustang, Scar and Ling.
I liked Mustang because the guy was a mastermind! He was able to think one step ahead and make a plan involving so many people without failure. I loved the scene where he almost loses his mind while finishing off Envy and how he had to be brought back to his senses by others. I found it very realistic and human like. With Scar, as soon as he was introduced I knew he wasn't a villain at all, but an anti-hero. Although unjustified, I felt his initial motives were understandable and I loved to see him slowly changing his perceptions about Amestrians and his behavior towards people in general. I liked Ling because he was introduced as this goofy and careless character, when all of that in fact seemed to just be a charade to hide his true power. Obviously, he is powerful because he could share his body with Greed and engage in direct combat with the homunculus without major loses or wounds. Many things were accomplished because of Ling's/Greed help and I wish he had gotten more screen time than he did.

Edward was a very stubborn child, but I believe precisely for that reason he was able to go as far as he did. I liked his perseverance and tenacity. I felt Al was more mature than Ed, but sometimes could be a bit too naive for his own good. Al is a kind and noble soul, that got exactly the ending he deserved. I loved to see how Ed and Al remained completely true to their character through the whole anime. I enjoyed to see these kids being able to preserve joy, a lightness of heart and joke around in an age appropriate manner despite all the horrors and pain they went through. 

I can't finish this section without pointing out how most of the villains were so amazingly written that you couldn't help being interested or feeling bad for them. Honestly I didn't care much about Gluttony, Lust, Sloth, Pride and Wrath, although I understand they were there for a reason. I really believe each character's design contributed to their personality a lot more than one might think. For example, King Bradley (Wrath) was cool and under control most of the time (oposite to what that emotion means). Pride, a young boy and the most faithful son, who would even put himself in danger to fulfil his father's wishes, to me represented how much he 
was willing to put at stake to be praised by his father. Yet, my absolutely favorite villians were Greed and Envy. I liked Greed because he acted very accordingly to his name, doing what would better suit his interests, regardless of whether his actions would put him with the bad or the good team. I liked how by the end Greed realized what he truly wanted the most. I think his pairing with Ling was smartly done because Ling in some ways was greedy himself. I liked Envy because he was a consistent villain throughout the anime, not easy to get rid of, and also showed some character development, at least by the end of his life. His last speech was very powerful and made for my favorite episode (54). I can't help to wonder whether Envy was given the transforming power so he could "become" whoever he felt envious of?
Side note: wasn't Kimble the craziest guy alive? His logic was so off that I found it too funny (never forget when Pride swallowed him and then wondered how Kimble was still alive with all those souls in sorrow and Kimble's answer was "this is like music to my ears!!).

Enjoyment 10/10
A few people had been recommending this anime for ages now, but I kind of stayed away from it because I felt the synopsis was not appealing enough...man, was I wrong! I binged-watched this in a span of 3-4 days because I could not stop watching...It seems like every single episode ends in this cliffhanger that makes it almost imposible not knowing the outcome right away. 

Overall 10/10
I know many people see this anime as a masterpiece and a must watch...I am not a 100% sure I feel this way but I would totally recommend it.

I would not recommend people watch Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood (FMAB) as their first show unless they want every other show out there (aside from a few notable exceptions) to leave a painfully average taste. The Plot: FMAB has a plot that at first seems pretty generic albeit interesting. The concept of alchemy is introduced very well and continuously explained well throughout the show. At no point during the show was I confused about the weird magic sorcery they were doing. The entire concept of alchemy is also very elegant and easy to comprehend. FMAB sets rules and the world abides by those rules. However throughout the showthe plot develops from the brothers simple journey to a conflict that puts at stake the population of an entire country and the potential creation of a god. The way the story develops is wonderful and watching it put the main brothers in morally conflicting situations really helps you to create a bond with the protagonists and enjoy watching them grow.

The Characters:

The FMAB characters are extremely solid and well rounded with some incredible examples like Hohenheim and Greed. There are very few main characters that feel bland or boring with each addition being somewhat unique and having their own additional quirks, personalities, morals and problems. The homunculi vary in quality from some absolute masterpieces such as envy and greed to some questionable characters such as lust and sloth. In total the characters of FMAB won't be on the same level as Lelouch from Code Geass but won't disappoint either.

Sound and Animation:

Bones put a lot of effort and money into making the animation good and it really stands out. The entire show comes to life and fight scenes never disappoint. The openings and endings are also all of a high quality with certain tracks such as Uso, Rain and Again being some of the best themes in anime. The OST's are also incredibly memorable and really bring the show to life and help elicit emotional responses from the viewer, whether that be hype at an awesome battle or tears at an emotional moment. The music and animation in this show is stellar.

Enjoyment:

FMAB is (to date) my second favorite anime of all time, only beaten out by Steins Gate and closely followed by Code Geass. Its incredibly enjoyable and I was never bored whilst watching. If anything the only problem with the show is that due to the lack of low points the high points feel less high which is hardly the shows fault. I believe this anime to be one of the best out there and if you watch I'm sure you'd be of similar opinion.

Problems:

There really aren't that many issues with the show. Since its so solid its hard to point out any consistent because quite frankly they aren't there. I've watched the show twice (I don't rewatch shows regularly) and even on my second run through I didn't notice any ground breaking flaws in logic, plot animation or character design. If anything the only issue with the show is that it can take a while to pick up steam but that's part of the deal when you begin watching a 60+ episode show and the wait is definitely worth it. The only this stopping FMAB from being a 10 is that it doesn't do enough extra. That may sound contradictory to everything I've said in this review so allow me to explain. Everything FMAB does is done to near perfection however what it lacks is that extra level of depth. Its a good show, but that's all it is, a show. Unlike something such as the ending of Code Geass which really made me reconsider certain aspects of life. But then again this final point will come down to opinion as people connect to different things differently. 

Conclusion:

Watch this show. Don't push it back. Watch it. You won't regret it.

I have watched the 2003 version years ago, so I remember a bit of the plot. However, FMAB still brought many surprises. It has a masterpiece soundtrack that sets the tone for many scenes. The orchestra behind the soundtrack does an amazing job in complementing the emotions during important scenes. The voice actors does an exceptional job in making the characters feel more alive. Every voice I heard in the Dub version perfectly fit every character. The story does an amazing job in connecting many sub-themes and still follow under one big theme. All the characters are very impactful to the story. There arebarely any fillers and all the episodes are like puzzle pieces that form together to show you the bigger picture. After watching the 2003 adaptation I then watched Brotherhood right after. Before watching I actually thought Brotherhood was a sequel for some reason. Instead it's actually a more faithful adaptation to the manga. Because of this, the first 13-15 episodes had the same events as the 2003 version, but after that it was completely different. I decided to watch this in English because the first version's dub was great. So which version was the superior one? Most importantly was it good in general? Here are my thoughts.***contains MINOR spoilers*** Story:10/10 Incredibly well written. It follows the same journey as the original but with different plotlines. While stillmaintaining the same amount of humor and darkness form the original, this version has better action, more nail biting moments, and better backstory. What I really loved about both of the FMA series' is their exploration on serious topics like war, redemption, death, human sacrifice, and humanity. This is what makes this shonen franchise so special becuz it touches important topics that no other shonens would explore as FMA focuses more on being serious. Ed and Winry's relationship is deeper here so it adds a bit of a romance. Brotherhood also had a better atmosphere as it had lots of scenes that would suck you right into the story. As for pacing, it starts off fast due to the first 13-15 episodes but after that the pacing was perfect. Not once did I feel that it started to slow down. Another huge advantage is that the ending here is far superior. It was way more satisfying and it left giving us everything it had to offer. After a long dramatic journey, the Elric brothers did everything they needed to do and all the other characters lived up to their potential. A lot of sacrifice, a lot of emotional scenes, Brotherhood ended the best way it could've.


Art:10/10
This is unfair to compare because this version is more recent but in general the animation is gorgeous. It focused more on animating things in the background, making the action sequences flawlessly smooth, with lots of movement. Most of the settings such as Amestris and the civilians look more realistic due to them being nicely detailed and with great amount of fluidity. The visual and special effects were far better making alchemical powers such as fire to look more realistic. And plus every character looks better here with all their features given more depth.

Sound:10/10
Like the 2003 series, this is an area where Brotherhood truly shines. An awesome soundtrack that I heavily enjoyed. While 2003's OST had more of a sad tone Brotherhood's OST was more epic that helped give the action that extra intensity. The first ending theme, "Uso" is one of my favorite themes in all of anime as well as the first opening theme, "Again." The voice acting was once again terrific with majority of the characters given their same VA although this time Al was given a female to do his voice. His VA however, did a great job and sounded a lot like the one from the original.

Character:10/10
Brotherhood did what was almost impossible; it made the cast BETTER. This version gave us some new characters that played key roles and made the series very enjoyable. The homunculi were also handled better and given different origins from the original that made more sense. They were likeable in the 2003 series due to their origins making them a lil more human, while in Brotherhood they were mainly evil and sadistic and made their deaths more satisfying to watch. What this also did however  was make them more of a villainous threat and added more conflict to the series. Hohenheim was also more relevant and given more of a backstory compared to the 2003 series. The biggest advantage was the main villain, Father. For one he's the most powerful character of the franchise, he has a stronger backstory with Hohenheim, his motives are more clear and understandable, and he had a bigger impact. Not only was he great, but I would put him among anime's best villains.


Final Verdict

Simply a masterpiece, Brotherhood imo was hands down the better adaptation. Better villains, better action, and waaaaay better ending, this was everything I wanted the original to be. It's hard to get two adaptions from the same franchise and not compare which is why I made a few comparisons. But in general this series blew me away. FMA: Brotherhood was not only great it's to me the greatest anime OF ALL TIME.  Ever since I got into this legendary franchise Ive become a huge fan of it. I do recommend watching both becuz although the original wasn't as great as Brotherhood, it still had emotional depth and in general it was very good. This is one anime that all fans must see.

Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood: A spoiler free review. I have two sisters. One three years older, the other three years younger. I don't know what it's like to have a brother. I have friends I call brothers, but at the end of the day, they are just guy friends I can trust to be in my apartment when I'm not there. But I do know what it's like to be a brother. I know what it feels like to be responsible for another's safety and well-being. My younger sister is my best friend. She is the most important person in my life. Andlike Ed to Al, I would give anything to ensure her safety. I understood Ed immediately. And that is the true strength of Fullmetal.

   Don't get me wrong, there is a lot to love about this show. The pacing, the world building, the interesting use of not only alchemy but how some use it different than others depending on their personalities. The music is on point, the villains are interesting and the heroes are not heroes but heroic people. So I can safely say this show is a solid 7-8 out of ten. But it gets the solid 9 for its representation of sibling relationships. 

   This is a person you grew up with. Shared a home with, made a bond with. A promise, a rise to arms if the duty calls. You would give your blood, your life, your very existence to make sure this person you are closest to is safe. Is happy. We all like to think we would jump at the call to fight for what's right like Ed and Al. We all like to think we would take the chance and save the world. But not all of us would. Not all of us are heroes. And that's okay. But if you have siblings, especially if you are an older sibling, I think you will really see the strength in this series. Because it sold me in the very first moments of the show what it means to be an older brother. To feel responsible for this helpless youth. You would walk the edges of the world for them. And even though we may not all jump to arms to save the world, I think almost everyone would jump into hell to protect their sibling.

 I know I would.

This is the first time I actually feel like writing a review, and I’m very much aware that I won’t be saying anything that it hasn’t been said before. But I just had to. Why? well, I have been avoiding to watch this anime for years, mainly because I don't really like the design of the characters and when it comes to manga/anime, I tend to chose stories with Japanese settings. But recently I decided to give it a chance, since it’s usually a very well positioned show in all the rankings. I guess I wanted to know why… So now that I’ve finallywatched Full Metal Alchemist Brotherhood, I can openly say that it is one of the most overrated shows of all times.  Please don’t get me wrong, I liked it, I really did. It’s not a bad show, it’s actually pretty good one, but I just can’t understand how it is so high on the list.  The story is good, the plot develops very skillfully. It’s a very epic show if “epicness” is what you’re looking for. However, for people like me, who may be more attracted by getting emotionally involved with the story and characters…. It just doesn’t feel enough.  This show could have been much more awesome if it had been given the time to deepen into the background of the characters. I just felt that most of the characters were plain and barely half developed. There are very nice characters with a lot of potential, but their personality just seems incomplete. This is very frustrating especially in the case of the “villains”. There you have a bunch of characters that could have been really badass but they are just purposeless. Their background, their psychological basis, their ulterior motives were almost inexistent. I really don’t know if it was a failure of the plot or if it was a failure of the adaptation that failed to embody their means and motivations.… Which, by the way, was way better constructed in the previous anime adaptation of Full Metal Alchemist.  In the previous adaptation, the homunculi had a more complex origin and a very contradicting nature, which made them way more interesting than they are in Botherhood. For instance, characters as Lust or Izumi, which were very charismatic in FMA due to their background story, are just empty shells in Brotherhood.  That’s pretty sad, because at the end you see the characters suffering and you get like “who are you again?”. At the end of the show I just felt I had not really been given the chance to truly get to know any of these characters, so I didn’t really care that much of what would happen to them.  In FMA I was really moved by most of the characters’ circumstances, but in Brotherhood it was like… yep, ok, this fight is sooo epic, but who was fighting again? What for?...
In addition FMA had those twisted scenes… kind of dark situations that came out of nowhere (let’s call them “small and subtle creepy Nina-like scenes” if you know what I mean) that would leave us all wondering what the heck did just happened and how such a nice show can become so creepy in just a second and immediately turn back to normal as if nothing had happened. That was pretty awesome in FMA, and there was no trace of that awesomeness in Brotherhood. 
Maybe I’m comparing the two animes a little too much, but I actually watched FMA after watching FMAB, and I just can’t help to think that there should be a third adaptation mixing the two previous shows. THAT could be the best show ever if they do it right.
So yep, leaving FMA aside for now, about Brotherhood I can say: yes, it’s a good story. Yes, it’s worth watching. Yes, after watching it you will look back and think “it was a good anime” . Plus it has a cool soundtrack, with very cool openings and endings, which is always appreciated.  But, if you watch it, do not expect it to be the best anime ever, because it is not.

I guess people on MAL need to go through this step when watching anime. Watching the top rated anime on the website. I think it's been this way for 8 years now, and definitely not deserved. But that's a community matter, let's talk about the damn show. From what I've seen, FMAB is an anime that has been overwhelmingly praised, with very little hate. My stance on it? A good story, although it fell off pretty bad at the end of it. Might have spoilers, might not, I write these on the fly. Through the first half of the show, it pretty much follows what I considerto be "perfect storytelling" which is, a series of fairly meaningless arcs to give the viewer an understanding of the world before the threads of the plot form a more coherent main story. And then comes the second half, which I put somewhere during the whole Briggs fortress visit, which is honestly my favorite part of the show. This second part is basically a massive build-up for the final fight, while still keeping bits of the mystery solving from the first part.

And then comes the real problem, the final fight in question. On its own, it would probably be a 4/10, everything before was rendered useless, since the major hindrance the bad guys faced was something that, while slightly foreshadowed, happened off-camera.

Also, the main character, or even the main cast for that matter was utterly useless in the fight against Homonculus. Just because Ed threw some punches and dealt "the finishing blow" doesn't mean that the whole battle wasn't carried by someone who appeared in the latter half of the anime. Sure it's realistic, but that's the problem. Realism shouldn't get in the way of a good story. Also, almost every death was stupid and easy to avoid, almost feels like the goal was only shock value.

Of course, the rest of the show was praise-worthy. I really enjoyed the world building and basically everything that revolved around combat. The fighting moments looked good, the power system, while simple, did a very good job and the internal political intrigue -which plays the main role in the show, even more so than the actual battling- was the best aspect of the anime.

And of course through the political intrigue in this military dictatorship, the characters really shone. Honestly, there hasn't been a single bad character, although my preference goes to Scar. Speaking about Scar, he's the most minor criminal in a pretty big offense from the show. Along with the whole Xing cast, he's part of those characters who had no business in the grand scheme of things. And while the author did a decent job explaining what Scar was doing, tf were the Xing guys doing? Ling gang and May were both self contained stories in the greater narrative.

The Elrics, Mustang and the Armstrongs all have some sort of stake in the story. But the Xing gang only cared about immortality and just happened to be strung along the whole thing and just happened to fill a few important roles, regardless of how desperately the author tried to string them with certain characters. Maybe it seems too harsh, but I couldn't help but think: "What are these guys doing here?" My theory is that the author wanted to expand upon the world with spin-offs and the likes but never got around to doing it.

Also, mind if I use this paragraph to congratulate Armstrong (Alex) for being the only big guy who's purpose wasn't to show how much stronger another character is? That's it thanks.

With all that being said, this remains a real solid anime, and while the top position isn't really deserved to me, it remains a really good shonen. Even more so when there's more political intrigue than there is battling. This is how I enjoy an anime. Very grateful to the creator for that. But a bit less for the fact that it's still not canon that Scar's name is Jugenmujugenmugokonosurike kaiaiusugesugematsufunfaimatsufunraimatsukurune tokoronisumiyapparikojiyappankoji baibobaibobaiboshuringashuringanugurindai guindainobomboribombonanojoukyuumechousuke

Fullmetal Alchemist is, in a way, unique. It is very much a mainstream series, with the appeal of a huge cast of unique characters, action that commonly involves special powers, a fairly straight forward story with some mostly obvious symbolism, and a mix of comedy, action, drama, and even some romance. These are all common staples of long running anime series that lean towards a more commercial and public appeal. And yet, for a mainstream series, it manages to continually surprise with a very mature and serious tone. There is a great deal of tragedy and some moments are even frightening and memorable. Few seriesachieve such a perfect balance of mainstream entertainment and gut wrenching drama and tragedy.

Such was what I discovered when I first laid my eyes on the original FMA series. And yet, for all it's greatness, it began to flounder in it's second season. As many series do, it took on its own form and story, and it was at that point that it started to lose its charm. So, Bones did the smart thing. They remade it. For most series, this would be pointless, but for FMA, it's very much welcome. Five years after the original series ended and the manga has had time to grow, this new FMA is better looking, paced better, and follows the manga, expanding the plot in a better direction.

It's hard not to like anything about this new FMA. The action is fantastic and looks great, as it always did. We aren't subjected to single shots or poorly edited sequences. All the action is displayed and wonderfully animated. Likewise, all the charm is here as well, from the more serious scenes that fans will remember to the humor which is consistent and still funny. Bones took everything good about the original series and threw out all the bad, replacing those particulars with higher quality details. In a sense, it even feels like a new anime, and by episode 13, it has gone in a completely new direction.

A better developed story and characters, superior animation, and fantastic details. These are what make the new FMA an instant new-age classic. Like FMA was the first time around, the new FMA will be one of the top anime to watch out for in the states.

Possibly the greatest anime I've ever seen. No exaggeration, no joke about it. In an anime what should be the measuring stick for manga adaptations, FullMetal Alchemist Brotherhood left me speechless by the end of episode 63 and also a little downcast when it wrapped up with 64. My favorite thing about Brotherhood is simply its plot. I can't go into too much detail here, but the way everything comes together by the final season and how it ties back to most of the characters makes it one of the most complex and wondrous plots I've seen to date. So complex in fact, I'd recommendkeeping a notepad with you as you marathon the series (because believe me, you won't be able to just watch one episode and then walk away) and jot down the questions that float to mind because while they will claw at your mind and demand answers, they will all be answered within time. And it's jaw-dropping when some of them do!

As opposed to other animes, Brotherhood introduces over thirty well-rounded and developed faces that stick in your mind and hold traits/personalities that make them both easy to remember and to identify with. From the state military, to the homunculi, to the foreign faces that accompany the Elric brothers on their journey, most of these characters, much like the ones from Fairy Tail, each have their own in-depth backstories, most of which come together in the end, and overall prove that even the supporting cast doesn't always have to be boring. 

I'm not too observant on OST's, but Brotherhood's is not one to be easily discarded. If you have a good memory for background music, more then likely a few of these pieces will be left stuck in your head. Some of its more recurring pieces like "The 5th Lab" and "Dissident's Creed" are among my favorites and add the ominous tone the scenes paired with them are going for. Not to mention the five openings and closing songs, op 1 "Again" makes it as one of the catchiest and most detailed of anime openings I've seen. 

Whether you prefer dub or sub, you can't say that all dubs are bad without giving Brotherhood's a chance. It's Funimation's best work as far as I'm concerned, and each voice actor/actress pours each line from their mouth with the emotion and tone their respective character deserves. Specifically Vic Mignogna, Travis Willingham, Troy Baker and Ed Blaylock knock their respective roles out of the park! 

Compared to the 2003 series, I simply believe Brotherhood surpasses it in every way, due to the fact that for me, an anime is more enjoyable when the anime is traced right from the manga, due to it being the author's intended beginning, middle and end. 

Needless to say again, Brotherhood just blew me away! It's now a huge favorite of mine, and it's a must-see for any anime fan!

Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is considered by many to be one of if not the best anime ever made. With its great animation, stirring music, and unique story there is reason for this. However after watching the show I felt like I could never feel the story. I never truly felt for any of the characters or their story arcs. When a character died I never felt any sense of loss. The reason for this in my eyes was length. Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is not a very long show in context. Only around 21 hours to watch which is nothing compared to behemoths like One Piece orNaruto. However with Naruto for example the scale is relatively small. Sure their are aliens and giant foxes but in the end those things don't matter. It's really just a container for fights. Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood however packs in even more scale and story in a much shorter run time and makes it the central focus of the show. At parts this scale showed, for example: a character has an internal dialogue which reveals them to be evil and then is never brought up again or when a central villain is killed and the characters go on with little fan fare.

While Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is by no means a be a bad show, I consider it above average, it simply did not meet my tastes. It felt bloated, and needed to either have a much longer or shorter runtime. If you like shows that are exposition heavy slow burn with dozens of characters you will probably enjoy this show. However if you like tighter more concise shows I would recommend skipping over this one or watch it on 2x speed.

Honestly, I only watched this at first because it was the highest rated. I thought to myself, why not just see the best since I wanna watch some anime? And knowing myself, I'm pretty new to anime. I've only seen the big name anime, so in no way is my opinion biased. I've never seen or heard much about this anime besides that it is "the best" according to many. Naturally, I came into this anime expecting something great, and it didn't fail to deliver in the slightest. At first, I was worried that this anime was a little too long for me to finish, and thatI would get bored and drop it halfway. However, as I went deeper and deeper into the series, the thought of dropping completely left my head.

I think what really makes this anime shine is the characters. You really grow to care for them, and you get to learn all of their quirks. I personally found the jokes that the writer took to put in there hilarious- for instance, every time someone called Ed short he would turn into a live landmine- that was great. I especially liked it when the people he was fighting would point out his height. It just made everything so lighthearted, and often times I feel anime can be overly serious, to the point that you can't watch too many episodes in a day because otherwise you'll feel overloaded. FMAB did a great job of balancing serious episodes with lighthearted ones.

In addition, the moments when the animator purposefully drew Ed or Al in weird ways to convey emotion, for instance when they were embarrassed Al would be drawn with 2 dots for eyes and a gray frame, making him look meek. Its just these little details that make it so much more enjoyable.

And of course, since you grow to like these characters so much, it adds extra oomph to the plot, when one dies or when another feels joy. There is also so much variety. You have the hotheaded, impulsive Ed. You have the jealous, and yet caring Alphonse. You also have the calm Roy Mustang, and his faithful companion Hawkeye. And of course, you have all the homunculi, of which I thought Greed was the most interesting. There are so many characters, I would really doubt that a viewer couldn't resonate with at least one, if not more.

All in all I highly recommend this anime to someone who is looking for something to commit to. It is long, but those hours fly by when you are watching some quality work, from one of the best anime that the genre has to offer. And previously if you told me this anime was the best, I would doubt that any anime could be better than the first anime I ever saw (One punch man). But now, I believe that this anime may just be good competition. It definitely deserves the 10 in my book. 

And I'd just like to point out that Roy Mustang says "Hagane no Renkinjutsu" the best :P

I went into FMA: Brotherhood without watching the manga or the original 2003 anime, so this review is from the standpoint of someone who really knew nothing about the series or source material. I'm going to start with what I believe the series' main weak point is: I found the first quarter of the show to be somewhat of a confusing slog. The problem, in my opinion, is that the show introduces a large number of characters and threads at once, and bouncing back and forth between them hinders the development of any one of these threads. The advice many will lend regarding this is towatch the first part of the original anime before jumping into Brotherhood. I can't comment on that approach, so my advice is to stick it through the first part of the show, even if the thought of "where is this all going?" comes to mind.

Once these threads come together a bit, the story is really fantastic and intriguing. I found myself constantly wondering how the Homonculi were going to hatch their master plan, and how the alchemists were going to attempt to thwart. The show has a knack for teasing some very intense, epic twists. Additionally, the show looks and sounds amazing and really sets the bar for other shonens. It has a really amazing art style throughout, especially when it comes to the dark, supernatural aspects.

I found the cast of characters on FMA:B''s journey to be enjoyable and interesting. Learning about everyone's backstory's was compelling and very much important to the overall story. Ironically, the two characters with the most boring/plain backstory were probably the two main protagonists. I initially was somewhat annoyed by Edward being little more than a cheesy caricature at first, but he does develop quite well and become likable.

The final quarter of the show was not quite as exciting as the middle portions, mainly because a lot of the mystery was wrapped up at this point, and what remained was for our heroes to defeat evil once and for all. I definitely enjoyed the ending of the show, but the show still really shines in its middle, and the thrilling intrigue of that portion is what makes FMA:B such a fantastically rewarding show.

- English Review (Translated version) At this point I am not going to be the one to discover anything to anyone about "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood". Years ago I read the original manga version of Arakawa's work. In fact, I have it complete in physical format and I keep it as gold in cloth. By this I mean that I no longer had the surprise factor of the script, characters and other elements at the time I started to see this adaptation, but even so I must say that I was amazed as if it had been the first time that I was immersed in the adventuresof Ed and Al. Partly because "Fullmetal Alchemist" is already a wonder in itself, partly because I can't think of a better way to bring to anime the great work of the, also great, Hiromu Arakawa.

One of the strong points (if any) of "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood" is, without any doubt, its plot. From the very beginning it is intuited that the story will be colossal, epic, of those that marks... and hell if it is. Throughout the 64 episodes of the anime, Arakawa gradually spins each character's background, each new situation, each detail and each nook and cranny. In this way he manages to weave a completely solid net, entertaining, impactful at times and that makes you stuck to the screen from the first minute to the last. Along the way he is able to perfectly combine really hard moments with other very emotional ones, without forgetting that funny white humor, which is also one of its great signs of identity. To name something negative (but I insist that it is basically to make a little counterweight to the amount of positive aspects it has), perhaps the main plot, especially towards the end, has moments in which a little entangled entering into metaphysical and philosophical aspects, which generates a little confusion at some point. Nothing important, of course.

From "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood" I am very clear that its greatest value are its characters. In fact, I can state categorically that its character squad is the best I have ever seen in an anime. Just like that. For variety, charisma and ability to create empathy. It has a lot of merit that in a story with such a large number of characters, all of them border on such a high level. It's just spectacular. There are other animes with very good characters (I think "Steins;Gate" or "Shokugeki no Soma"), but they have a smaller quantity of them or they don't have such a high quality in the overall, but in specific characters. I think Arakawa's ability to create so many different and charismatic characters can only be compared to Eiichiro Oda's genius in that sense. Big words, yes, but totally deserved. To name a few, without forgetting the brilliant protagonists Edward and Alphonse Elric, there would be room for characters such as Winry, Roy Mustang (and his inseparable Hawkeye), Scar, May Chang, the Armstrong brothers (especially Olivier), Ling and Lan Fan, Hohenheim... All with their role, with their importance, with their background, and even with their own sub-plots. And the villains, of course: Lust, Envy, Greed... In short, a list that would be endless if I had to name all the great characters of "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood".

Finally, I'd like to talk about the technical sections. So in short, I think that the visual section meets without emphasizing too much and on the contrary the musical section is outstanding. I will explain something more in detail. When I talk about the visual section I am not referring to the artistic style. Not at all. Arakawa's style, so characteristic, I like. It's relaxed yet detailed. She is also able to create a relative variety within the, also relative, visual realism of his works. But I think that technically this adaptation could have done a better job. Nothing serious, eh. Sometimes the drawing is not as good as it should be, especially in certain character animations or in the excessive blurring/simplification of scenarios. I'm not saying it's bad, but I'm saying that maybe sometimes it's not up to all the other great sections of "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood". As is the musical section, which is a real marvel. Probably one of the best global OST of the anime, with some pieces that are directly masterpieces. There are so many that are worthwhile, but I personally get "Lullaby of Resembool" if I have to name just one of them. As for openings/endings, I won't tire of repeating that I prefer a small number of them, as this creates a strong relationship between melody and anime that helps to create a greater self-identity in our mind. In "FMA: Brotherhood" there are too many. Five openings and five different endings in 64 episodes. Excessive. It's a detail I can forgive such a good series, but it's reality and I want to comment it. At least most of them are quite good. If I have to choose, I keep OP1 and ED3.

A estas alturas no voy a ser yo quien descubra nada a nadie sobre "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood". Hace años que leí la versión original en manga de la obra de Arakawa. De hecho, la tengo completa en formato físico y la guardo como oro en paño. Con esto quiero decir que ya no contaba con el factor sorpresa del guion, personajes y demás elementos en el momento que me puse a ver esta adaptación, pero aun así debo decir que me ha maravillado como si hubiera sido la primera vez que me sumergía en las aventuras de Ed y Al. En parte porque "Fullmetal Alchemist" ya es una maravilla de por sí, en parte porque no se me ocurre una mejor forma de llevar al anime la grandísima obra de la, también grandísima, Hiromu Arakawa.

Uno de los puntos fuertes (si es que tiene alguno flojo) de "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood" es, sin ningún tipo de duda, su trama. Desde el principio ya se intuye que la historia será colosal, épica, de las que marcan... y vaya si es así. A lo largo de los 64 capítulos que dura el anime, Arakawa va hilando poco a poco cada trasfondo de personaje, cada nueva situación, cada detalle y cada recoveco. De esta forma logra tejer una red completamente sólida, entretenida, impactante por momentos y que te hace estar pegado a la pantalla desde el primer minuto hasta el último. Por el camino es capaz de conjugar perfectamente momentos verdaderamente duros con otros muy emotivos, sin olvidar ese humor blanco tan divertido, que es también una de sus grandes señas de identidad. Por nombrar algo negativo (pero insisto en que es básicamente por hacer un poco de contrapeso a la cantidad de aspectos positivos que tiene), quizá la trama principal, especialmente hacia el final, tiene momentos en las que se enmaraña un poco entrando en aspectos metafísicos y filosóficos, lo que genera un poco de confusión en algún momento puntual. Nada importante, eso sí.

De "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood" tengo muy claro que su mayor valor son sus personajes. De hecho, puedo afirmar con rotundidad que su plantilla de personajes es la mejor que he visto nunca en un anime. Tal cual. Por variedad, carisma y capacidad de crear empatía. Tiene muchísimo mérito que en una historia con una cantidad tan grande de personajes, todos rayen a un nivel tan alto. Es algo simplemente espectacular. Hay otros animes con muy buenos personajes (se me vienen a la mente "Steins;Gate" o "Shokugeki no Soma"), pero tienen una cantidad menor de ellos o no tienen una calidad tan alta en el global, sino en personajes concretos. Creo que la capacidad de Arakawa para crear tantísimos personajes carismáticos y diferentes entre sí solo se puede comparar con la genialidad de Eiichiro Oda en ese sentido. Palabras mayores, sí, pero totalmente merecidas. Por nombrar a algunos, sin olvidar a los geniales protagonistas Edward y Alphonse Elric, tendrían cabida personajazos como Winry, Roy Mustang (y su inseparable Hawkeye), Scar, May Chang, los hermanos Armstrong (en especial Olivier), Ling y Lan Fan, Hohenheim... Todos con su papel, con su importancia, con su trasfondo, e incluso con sus subtramas propias. Y los villanos, por supuesto: Lust, Envy, Greed... En fin, una lista que sería interminable si tuviera que nombrar a todos los grandes personajes de "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood".

Para terminar quiero hablar de los apartados técnicos. Aquí veo claroscuros. Así de forma resumida, creo que el apartado visual cumple sin destacar demasiado y por el contrario el apartado musical es de sobresaliente. Paso a explicarme algo más en detalle. Cuando hablo del apartado visual no me estoy refiriendo al estilo artístico. Para nada. El estilo de Arakawa, tan característico, me gusta. Es desenfadado a la vez que detallado. También es capaz de crear una relativa variedad dentro del, también relativo, realismo visual de sus obras. Pero considero que técnicamente en esta adaptación se podría haber hecho un mejor trabajo. Nada grave, eh. A veces el dibujado no es todo lo bueno que debería, especialmente en ciertas animaciones de personajes o en el difuminado/simplificación excesivo de escenarios. No estoy diciendo que sea malo, pero sí que quizá en ocasiones no está a la altura de todos los demás magníficos apartados de "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood". Como sí lo está el apartado musical, que es una auténtica maravilla. Probablemente una de las mejores OST globales del anime, con algunas piezas que directamente son obras maestras. Hay muchísimas que merecen la pena, pero yo personalmente me quedo con "Lullaby of Resembool" si tengo que nombrar solo una de ellas. En cuanto a los openings/endings, no me cansaré de repetir que prefiero poca cantidad de ellos, ya que así se crea una relación fuerte entre melodía y anime que ayuda a crear una identidad propia mayor en nuestra mente. En "FMA: Brotherhood" hay demasiados. Cinco openings y cinco endings diferentes en 64 capítulos. Excesivo. Es un detalle que puedo perdonarle a una serie tan buena, pero es la realidad y quiero comentarla. Al menos en su mayoría son bastante buenos. Si tengo que elegir, me quedo con el OP1 y con el ED3.

One of the things that defines a good anime to me is when it both stands the test of time and how it is when compared to other anime I watch. With those things in mind, I can't say enough how much I thoroughly enjoyed this series. I have watched ALOT series since watching it, and this one still ranks up very high for me, even almost 10 years later. It's funny, I enjoyed the original FMA series so much back when this came out that I avoided this series, in fear that it would somehow make me upset at the mishandlingof this series when compared to the original.  I waited until the series was almost over before starting it, and in the end I kicked myself for denying myself this series.  The story does get slightly weird at the end, but it cleans up nicely.  The characters are great, and you get alot of new characters to follow and like to really set it apart from FMA.  Art is good, this one has more comedy than the first series, and it is pretty well done.  This is a great series for new or seasoned anime watchers, and for me serves as one of the series I use as a ruler on how other series measures up.

Story - I'm honestly not a huge fan of the actual story. I can look passed potholes but some things seem sloppy or only halfway thought out (example, the gold toothed doctor). I don't hate the story but the fact the last fight because Edward punching shit in your typical Shounen fashion kind of really devalues the more interesting Team dynamic between Alphonse and Edward that they had in the beginning of the series. It's far from terrible and I kind of wish it gave more of an idea of what every character did after the events (it doesn't tell you what Olivier Armstrong orIzumi Curtis is doing at the end) because the show felt like such an ensemble but instead it only focused on Edward and Alphonse and I find that to be a weakness. 

Art  - Gets an 8 because while I like the style and the visuals are great, it still suffers from the fact it spans 64 episodes and therefore there is a lot of people laying still in the frame with only mouth movement and the camera pans slightly. Otherwise, I like the style and some sequences look stellar. Very solid.

Sound - Some of the music is great, some of the music is very forgettable and serviceable at best. It was never distractedly bad and some tracks really elevated the scenes. The sound effects were fine, no complaints. The english dub is way quieter than the Japanese dub for some reason so switching between them was kind of a pain but this is a minor problem. Overall the sound was alright. I wanted to give a 7 for the sound but it gets an 8 because of those few tracks that really pushed a scene from being typical into fascinating.

Characters - The best part of this anime. I have heard arguments that the 2003 anime has better character development and that may be true. But the reason this show kept me at all was due to some of the really strong characters that I liked. So many very strong female leads which surprised me like Hawkeye, Olivier, Ross, etc. It wasn't perfect but it was by far the biggest reason I kept going with this show and the story is very much secondary to the characters and I'm fine with that.

Enjoyment - I only gave it a 7 because Story is such a huge deal for me. I know this show could have an even better story if the manga hadn't been written as it went and was planned a bit better in advance. I can't say I want to watch it all again anytime soon, I just wasn't that enamored with it and I think it's highly overrated for being ranked so highly... I just don't see why. It was alright though.

Overall - A solid 7. Definitely above your average anime, still don't understand the overwhelmingly positive reviews. It's elevated above most Shounen so maybe that's enough. I still prefer the HxH manga to something like this.

If you plan to see Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood for the first time, be prepared to be horrified by the first episodes! It took me a long time to get used to the way things work. Many lives are taken, many shadows lurking and many sacrifices are made. Between being immortal and having all the knowledge of God or being human, most people would choose the first option. But with Fullmetal, you'll find that even immortal beings would want to be human. Because there is nothing more precious than that, human being. Every human life is extremely important, which is why human transmutation is impossible. What's more, oneof the basic things you'll learn about alchemy is that to have one thing, you have to sacrifice another. This is the equivalent exchange, and if you are smug you may lose your most precious possession.

Funny how I identified so much with the homunculi, human means representing the seven deadly sins, and I was so moved by them. Each farewell hurt my heart a lot. Even though they were horrible while alive, they also had feelings and suffered in silence.

I can't help but say that this anime filled with Plot Twists, with characters that initially make you angry, and then you will have an inexplicable affection for them - as well as vice versa. The fact is that some have the opportunity to start over, but not everyone is so lucky.

I confess that at first the atheistic thought of Edward Elric the protagonist bothered me a great deal. It seems that he thought himself on the same level as God. But over time, his maturity surprised me too much!

One is all, and all is one. This is the flow of life, this is the universe. Edward, whether alchemist or not, always was only a mere human being in this stream. No more than the others, but also with a significant existence for the universe.

Everything I may be saying may seem a little confusing. But the fact is, even you go out with a slightly different head after watching. There are so many things that make you reflect on the importance of life, feelings, compassion.

It also urges us to think about what "Truth" is. There are characters from many different cultures in Fullmetal, each with their own beliefs - or religion, their own culture. That's why I believe the truth was different for each one.

The Ishvalians, for example, believed in God Ishvalia. But Edward in the laws of the universe. We shape our reality, which is why it is different for everyone. The truth is in you. The truth IS you.

An anime that at first seemed so dark and violent actually has an immeasurable depth with good, sentimental teachings. Still being horrifying in many parts, of course. So much so that characters really die in this anime! It's all very unpredictable and you really get scared if someone is going to die.

Not like the other shounens where the protagonist is the strongest of them all, the good guys remain firm and strong and there are no big losses down the road. On the contrary, it is just the opposite. Although Ed and Al are strong, most of the battles are fought by other incredibly talented characters, mostly adults, not children. Precisely because everything is so unpredictable, the battles, which already had everything to be great, become even better!

Regarding art, I find the appearance of the protagonists basic, but of many other characters is beautiful. Nothing exaggerated, but nothing ugly. I liked very much. The soundtrack is also very good. It fits perfectly with every situation, and will no doubt leave a trademark in your heart.

Finally, the last episode showed us that there are new beginnings even after the end. This is the life. This is the universe. This is the flow in which we live. Yes, this is alchemy!

Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood, is quite an amazing watch. It nails its interesting setting, featuring tonnes of world building and fitting characters with individual values, cultures and reasons to fight. And therefore following the Elric brothers on their difficult journey to get back what they lost. Truly feels like 2 kids crossing paths with the worlds powerplayers and getting entangled in the nations larger conflicts. To repeat myself, then it's an amazing watch, that at least partly deserves the praise it's recieving. However its really broad appeal may have hindered it's potential. At times it feels as if the series is having an identity-crisis. With deep divesinto serious story telling, such as multiple army-characters being haunted by their past contributions to an ethnic genocide. And other times it flips and uses very "anime" comedy such as slapstick humor to brighten the mood. Which (and I hate to say this) I actually never found genuinely entertaining as much as forced. The very "shonen like" conflicts and fights also end up feeling a bit the same. Like they were meant to entertain a younger audience. Losing a lot of the groundedness to the supernatural abilities, by introducing characters with so strong abilities it gets hard to understand them in context to the rest of the universe.

My biggest complaint with this series however, is something I have to reserve to the soundtrack, which is odd, as I usually don't put this much focus on the music, I've also never head anyone complain about this, so keep in mind this is exclusively my opinion.
But I disliked the soundtrack, not in itself, but mostly how it was implemented. Again, it feels like it's executed with a younger viewer audience in mind. There are many emotional scenes in this series that would actually be more impactful if there was different or even no music at all.
There are also "themes" that play at certain times. Such as when something is revealed, or there's mystery plot afoot, or when a fight is going on. It sounds good, but many of the tracks are so bold, loud and most importantly  overused, that it can get atrociously repetetive if you're binging the series. 

Now that might sound like an overly negative point to leave an otherwise positive review on. But I think it says a lot about what this series does right, if these are the primary concerns I've got. FMA Brotherhood is absolutely a series you must watch if you'd like to jump into an interesting universe you've never seen the likes of before, that will keep you entertained for all 60+ episodes. All I wanted was to address a criticism of the series that I haven't seen yet, and I still enjoyed it to the point that I'd only give it 1 point less in a review score that it has otherwise been recieving.

I put off watching this anime for a long time, despite all the high praise I heard about it, thinking that it would probably be overrated. And boy was I wrong. Very mild spoilers ahead so read at your own risk! Story (10/10): I can definitely say that in my opinion, FMA:B deserves all the praise that it gets. The story is fantastic and moves at a good pace - with 64 episodes, it never felt like the story dragged on or was ever boring. There are some good twists and turns to keep you on your toes, and the fight scenes are great. I'll leaveit at that as to not spoil too much. 

Art (8.5/10): Compared to some of the newer shows, the animation still holds is own (Bones Studio comes through as per usual), but it is definitely not as polished as some anime from more recent years. They do a great job with the fight scenes, especially in the later half of the show 

Characters (10/10): Aside from the story, one of the most compelling things about this show are the characters. You truly grow to care for the Elric brothers and are rooting for them to get their bodies back and get a happy ending. Edward is probably my favorite shounen MC of all time, and it is so satisfying to see him grow (mentally and physically) and learn from his past mistakes.This show is also jam packed with amazing female characters, which is something that the shounen genre is sometimes lacking in. Winry, Riza, Izumi, and Olivier are all amazing (just to name a few). In addition, Greed and Scar are some of the best anti-heroes that I have come across in anime. There are really no one-dimensional characters in this show, and it truly allows FMA:B to shine. 

Enjoyment (10/10): To be honest, I have a hard time finishing shows as I get bored easily. Not once did I consider dropping FMA:B, since it kept me entertained throughout. Especially in the last 2 seasons, it was pretty hard to stop watching once everything that had been leading up to the Promised Day got set into motion.

I do want to talk about a few things that some people might dislike about the show:
1.) Again, the animation is good, IMO, but if you are used to watching anime from more recent years, it might look subpar.
2.) Some people have issues with the comedy in the show. Personally, I didn't have an issue with it, but I can definitely see why some people might. I will say that some of the jokes/running gags do drastically decrease after the first season or two, so if that is something that bothers you, keep in mind that it will not be as prevalent as the show goes on. 
3.) I think this is mostly for people who have seen the 2003 version first, but some people do find the first few episodes to be rushed. I watched FMA:B before reading the manga, and I didn't notice any pacing issues, but just thought I would point that out. 

Overall, FMA:B really is a 10/10 show for me. If you are putting off watching this like I did for a long time, GO WATCH IT! 

FMA:B weaves an amazing and philosophical story about family, war, revenge, love, and ultimately, humanity.

Fullmetal Alchemist is a popular anime series with two versions: Fullmetal Alchemist and Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood. Both versions are considered good, but their plotlines have some differences. In the first version of Fullmetal Alchemist, the first half of the series is considered really good. It features notable moments like the fight between Edward Elric & Roy Mustang and the State Alchemist test taken by Edward Elric. However, the second half of the series takes many twists and turns, and some viewers may find it less impressive than the first half. On the other hand, Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood is true to the manga and has the soul ofthe original story. It is an all-rounded anime with a fantastic, tightly-knit, entertaining storyline. The anime has a mix of humor, action, and dark moments. The first half of the series introduces the characters and their backstories and ends with an almost hopeless situation for our heroes. In the second half, the story takes a faster pace with more action and nail-biting moments.

The decisions and resolutions taken by the Elric brothers at each step of their journey are justified and add to the depth of the series. All characters, including the cute little panda and Yogi, had their importance in the series and helped move the story forward. Introducing new characters like Olivier Mira Armstrong and Lin Yao's gang is well done and doesn't make them superior or inferior to the other characters.

Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood is often considered the best anime series overall, as it has a well-crafted story that is well-paced and engaging. It has elements of comedy, drama, action, adventure, thriller, and slice of life, making it a great watch for all anime lovers. Therefore, it is highly recommended for anyone who is looking for a good anime series to watch.

Before I state my opinion about the show I‘d like to say that this is an anime that holds a special place in my heart, seeing as FMA (Fullmetal Alchemist), and FMAB (Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood) were my very first anime series (well, not including the Pokemon, Naruto and etc. episodes I used to watch on TV as a kid). These were the series that first showed me how great the anime medium can be. That said, this review may or may not be a little biased because of how special the series are for me personally. In short I would describe FMA as a great storyabout the adventures of two brothers, their quest to achieving their goal, their hardships along the way and how their relationship grows stronger despite that. Throw in some likable characters they interact with while on their journey, great fight scenes, lighthearted comedy and a lot of alchemy and you got a general idea what FMA is about.

Story (10)

The story has a clear goal to move towards, but it doesn’t mean that it’s the only thing you’re going to see here. There are plenty of smaller segments, that are kind of short stories of their own, but they don’t go too far off the main story. Most tie into the main story in some way or another and I don’t think I’ve seen anything that felt like it could have been skipped or was unnecessary.

My main complaint with FMAB is that the first 12 or so episodes felt rushed, but if you’d like to watch the story unfold in more detail the first 30 or so episodes of the first anime adaptation of this series (in 2003) covers mostly the same story just in a slower pace.

The beginning aside, in my opinion, FMAB beats the first adaptation in the ending department by a mile. I won’t spoil it for  you if you haven’t seen it yet, but because of this, if you only have the chance to watch one of the adaptations, I’d recommend watching brotherhood, even though both of the adaptations have their own different charms and are worth a watch.

Art (10)

The animation style isn’t overly cute or overly rough and the colors aren’t too bright nor are they too bland. The animation is fluid and I didn’t notice any major faults with it.

I think it’s also worth mentioning that this show has one of if not the best fight scenes, especially involving some sort of magic (in this case – alchemy) that I’ve seen so far in anime.

Sound (10)

The OPs ranged from ok to good, even thought I personally liked the first adaptation’s OP songs better.

I have no complaints about the sound effects. They aren’t out of place and work well.

Personally, I have seen the dubbed version of this anime, and I have to say, the DUB is really good. The voice actors did a good job and they fit their characters well. If you like myself don’t usually watch dubbed anime because a lot of the times it just doesn’t seem to work, but don’t mind it when the DUB is good, I’d recommend at least trying the dubbed version of FMA.

Character (10)

As I have mentioned earlier, I find the characters very likable. Let’s start with the main characters – Edward and Alphonse or Ed and Al for short. The two brothers and their relationship is one my favorite parts of this show. They are smart and capable, yet not perfect. Both of them make mistakes and learn from them. Even though they share a very strong sibling bond with each other, they still disagree and fight at times. These are all things that make them believable human characters and it brings me joy to watch them change and grow over the span of the story.

The brothers aren’t the only characters that change and grow over time, though. The more important supporting characters also develop quite a bit throughout the story, including the villains.

Speaking of villains, FMA has some really good ones. I unfortunately can’t go into much detail about them without spoiling the story, but I can say for sure that I rarely ever see anime villain characters that I love, or should I say love to hate as much as I do in this show. Their motives make sense and I was even able to sympathize with some of them to an extent. Perhaps most importantly, the villains aren’t villains just for the sake of the story having someone for the main characters to defeat, but instead they are actual characters with good reasons for acting the way they do.

Enjoyment (10)

It probably comes as no surprise, when I say that I enjoyed this anime to bits. It was the first anime (well the second if you count the first adaptation as a separate anime, which I personally do not) that I’ve ever seen from start to finish, it has what I consider to be a great story with some of the best characters I’ve ever seen and it probably helps that I am very fond of elements such as alchemy, strong sibling and/or friend relationships and action in not just anime, but other entertainment mediums as well. And to top it all off – a nice and clean animation style and a fitting soundtrack, what’s there not to love?

Overall (10)

Is this anime for everyone? Well, no, I doubt such an anime exists, but that aside I think this anime can be easily enjoyed by most anime viewers. It has a great story for those that want one, great action for those that enjoy shows better when there’s a lot of movement involved, characters that feel human for those that want to see characters change and grow, comedy for those that like to have a good laugh with their anime and etc.

Fullmetal Alchemist really is a great anime, and I think it’s one that you should at least give a try to. Who knows, maybe you’ll find something else it’s worth praising for? Or maybe you’ll find the exact opposite – a major fault that has escaped my attention? Either way, I hope you give it a try.

Now I’m not a fanboy of the franchise by any means. I never read the manga or saw the first adaptation. All I did was watch this show. It’s no “masterpiece” but it is still VERY good. Story [9/10]: The story was by far this show’s biggest high point (and the most important thing by far when rating an anime). The storytelling was properly paced, dynamic, and complex enough to satisfy everyone. There were many twists and surprising reveals along the way, but not too many where it becomes confusing and annoying. Art [4/10]: The animation gets the job done... that’s it. The characters, settings, special effects,and backdrops are bland in design, but are also crisp and well-animated. Visuals clearly weren’t on high priority.

Sound [6/10]: Voices and SFX were amongst the best of the best in terms of audio quality, but no cool sound effects to be found. Music leaves much to be desired, and in some instances causes the show to be dead silent.

Character [6/10]: The characters didn’t really feel too engaging. Most of them were just your by-the-numbers anime tropes. Nothing else to say here.

Enjoyment [10/10]: I really enjoyed watching this show. It’s storytelling kept me engaged and coming back for more. I’m sure you will enjoy this show as well.

Overall [7/10]: When the story is the show’s only high point, I struggle to give this show any more than a 7. I really like this show and I truly recommend it. I just don’t find any other aspect good enough to bump the score up any higher.

NO SPOILER REVIEW Here is a review coming from a young audience, not affected by nostalgia that typically prefers modern anime over old ones. To keep things short, my overall opinion after seeing this anime is that it's good, but, I do not appreciate the fact that the build-up was very long and that it wasn't that good. The pacing killed me halfway through, nearly falling asleep. The reason this anime is so appreciated is because it is long and complex. There were plenty of episodes to build a world from scratch. There were a lot of details and the anime payed attention to them. Thereare a lot of characters meant to represent your average people, that slowly appear into the life of two people, thus making them grow. But these people I'm talking in fact were very boring to watch. The interesting parts came in sets, separated by 10ish episode gaps.

I do appreciate it not being your average shonen, the MC is not powerful at all and the struggle is very hard. The MC grows in power from experience and from nothing else. The anime successfully gives you the feeling of a loss but 

I absolutely disliked the music of this anime because it is old. Can't complain too much, it was made in 2009, however in this review I'm sharing my impression. The animation wasn't that good either, the transitions between frames was slow, fights lack the punch (being nothing to what Shippuden offered for example).

The anime starts low, gets really interesting for a few episodes (20-25 I believe), then falls into that slow pacing up until the last 10 episodes being the climax. 

I don't think this anime deserves this spot on this site. It's ratings are way too high, I'm not saying it's bad but it's overrated. People got too emotionally affected by the ending (which indeed is really good) but forgot how boring it was to get there. There are also a lot of people affected by nostalgia or just old school FMA fans that were proud to see a remake of the original series.

STORY: 10/10

The story is amazing. Complex, a lot of plot twists, a lot of things make sense and it feels realistic (in a way of reality mixing with fantasy, not just pure fantasy). There was a lot of room for chaos and it was a long and hard ride. A lot of amazing details were shown in this anime, something the new ones fail to deliver. I don't think there is anybody in this world that won't enjoy this story.

ART: 8/10

It is an older anime but I still didn't get their art style at all. The eyes are poorly placed, most are too big, and some character's hair are just...yikes. Now I'm reviewing the anime, not the art style chosen by the manga writer, however the anime was supposed to make them a bit more pleasant to watch. I think they did an OK job overall.

SOUND: 7/10

The music has to be the shittiest part of this anime. There is a cycle of sounds played depending on the arc, the problem is it's very very very very repetitive. And it doesn't move you at all. It's just that music you find in old movies overused in most scenarios that try to move your soul a bit but they make you cringe. That's how it is. You'll get to a point where you'll be able to predict what song will come according to the scene.

CHARACTER: 9/10

I liked most characters because they covered the typical types of people you find around you. They were made realistically. None of them spit shit out of their mouths. You'll relate to what most normal humans would say. About their behavior, the main 2 protagonists start from scratch and although they don't suddenly get stronger they do change their decision making and perspective as time passes, this is the process of growing up. The supporting characters overall are good but there are some that simply make you wanna punch them, being good and suddenly becoming bad just to "shake things" up. 

ENJOYMENT: 8/10

In the "interesting" parts I just couldn't stop watching but in the build up episodes they simply made me drowsy or made me wanna check my phone just to change the panorama a bit. I had mixed feelings overall.

OVERALL: 8/10

It is a good anime and I cannot deny it, but again, I do not and I will never really see it as the number #1 anime rated by this site. IMO there are better anime out there worth this spot.

It's a shame because these earlier episodes usually had serious philosophical undertones but the show kept bailing out with jokes and those godawful animation switches. Given the story's dark and serious nature, the humor just felt out of place. It seemed like the showdoesn't take itself seriously and isn't worth my time but I endured for a few more episodes and I'm glad I did.

As the story progressed the brat MC became less bratty and the cute armor-clad brother didn't bring up his foodlist as often. But more importantly they got less screen time! Soon it was apparent that this isn't just a show about two brothers but something bigger. With the spotlight being shared more and more by various side characters, the show revealed its strength.

It took only 46 episodes to create a living, immersive world with a ridiculous amount of characters I'm heavily invested in. I enjoyed the pacing of the conspiracy reveal and I found myself breezing through the episodes. As I learned more about the rough FMA:B world, I also began to appreciate the brothers' childish behaviour and their struggle.

Other than that, the action scenes were well done throughout the show and only got better during the final act. I didn't love or hate the soundtrack, I thought it was mediocre (except Trisha's Lullaby <3). The animation was impressive for the most part but I wasn't a fan of the switches to "chibi". 

Overall, I think FMA:B is very good (8) but not the masterpiece it's made out to be. If you decide to watch it don't quit early, it gets better!
