Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood. Ah yes, the anime that will be on many people’s favorite lists and will forever be revered as the greatest anime of all time. It is so highly acclaimed, but does it meet that expectation. It’s hard to really ever meet such high expectations and it may have been a factor in my opinion on the anime but I think it’s one of the most overrated anime out there. Allow me to explain, Fullmetal Alchemist is a good show, a great show. I was well entertained while watching it. So first I’m going to talk about the more objective parts of the showand why people like it, and what I liked about it. Then I’ll explain why it just wasn’t mind blowing to me, why it is was just a good show and nothing else. Fullmetal Alchemist is a story about two brothers Edward and Alphonse who live in a world of alchemy. Alchemy is a form of practice that can transform the surroundings into other materials or matter. It’s a simple concept but it’s used in some clever ways. After a tragedy that occurred when they were young, when the Elric brothers tried to bring back their mother using alchemy resulted in Alphonse losing his body and Edward losing his arm. In an attempt to bring Alphonse back and restore their former bodies they search for a mythical object known as a philosophers stone.

This basic summary is the meat of the story and it’s what really moves the story forwards. It’s a complex yet easy to digest plot with a huge mystery that slowly unravels before the viewers. There is solid animation, good dialogue, and  a sound concept tied together in a concise world. And honestly there are few objective flaws with Fullmetal Alchemist’s story. A lot of people talk about the “perfect pacing” which I actually disagree with. I think it moves too slowly and could’ve been more like 50 episodes instead of the 64 with just as much depth. That also would’ve given them room for better animation in some of the fights. Some moments and fights were cool don’t get me wrong but they never blew me away. The fights are basic and well done, just like everything else. That’s precisely my problem with Fullmetal Alchemist. It’s basic.

Basic is not a bad thing, and many people just want something that’s basic but good. That’s great for you, but I always want to search for something bold. I like stories that take risks, ones that convey unique messages, or connect to me in an unusual way. Despite Fullmetal Alchemist being an amazing show objectively I found it boring in a lot of ways. The characters didn’t do much for me, with the exception of Roy Mustang. Edward Elric is a basic protagonist and Alphonse is a boring side character. The world is well made and the world building is sound, which is uncommon. But the world feels so much like other anime or shows that I love. Maybe it’s because many shows are inspired by Fullmetal Alchemist but to me it makes the world lack something unique. The concept is not bad, but the plot is mostly straightforward and predictable. There was not a single moment where I truly felt like it had been unpredictable or that the show had tricked me into thinking something.

Those are the reasons why I give Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood a 8/10. It’s good and there are no major flaws. I just didn’t connect with the anime like many people do. I didn’t find its story to be groundbreaking or blow me away. It might be hard to meet the expectations it holds, but I tried my hardest to lower them going in. Even after extensive time thinking about it, I’ve rated this show consistently with my other reviews and this is my final opinion. Until I rewatch it and my opinon maybe changes, Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood will stand as the best show I’ve watched that I don’t like that much. But if you want to watch it, go right ahead. It’s one of my top recommendations because it’s hard to dislike the show. But in my opinon Fullmetal Alchemist is a highly overrated anime that lacks true creative inspiration.

There isn't much more I could say with all the praise it already has, but I truly believe that Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood deserves every bit of it. The pacing is phenomenal; filler is minimal to nonexistent and every episode serves as another step forward. I know a few people who thought that the first few episodes were not explanatory enough, but one of the great things about it is its lack of unnecessarily long narratives; it gives you just enough background information without petulantly walking you through it. FMAB is also one of the only anime that I prefer the dubbed version over the subbed. The voiceactors are fit fantastically in their roles, and the openings and endings were, for the most part, great. The animation was gorgeous as well, especially in action shots.

But I think the most important thing to be taken into account is the plot and characters. At its center, FMAB is about two brothers who have just enough flaws for you to emotionally connect with them, but not so many that it crosses the boundary into overly annoying. The length (64 episodes) allows for steady character development, whether it be for the better or worse. Even the villains have some sort of depth without making it seem like a rushed pity backstory. It can sometimes have crass humor (which serves surprisingly well as comic relief), but it is also harshly realistic; good people die and there isn't always a good reason for it.

Summary: Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is a fantastic show with an engaging plot and interesting characters. What sets it apart from other anime of similar action, fantasy, and adventure themes is its development of relatable and lovable characters. This is one of the best anime to watch if you have never watched one before, as it balances dark themes, humor, and friendship. Its overall quality is superb, and it has stood the test of time, thus far,as the highest rated anime of all time on MAL. The suspense will keep you invested, and it’s awesome that you can now binge-watch it. I recommend it to anyone interestedin trying a new show or getting into anime.

Story: 9/10
Unlike many anime with the same genre, FA:B is not overly plot-driven. The characters develop over time and make choices that coincide with the plot. This is an important aspect of any good story. The viewer gets to know the main characters based on their traumatic past and their goals to reverse the mistakes they’ve made. The world-building is excellent, and watching this from start to finish makes you feel as though the characters’ world isn’t just a fantasy world. 

Art: 9/10
The art is beautiful 90% of the time. There are some scenes where it seems like there are missing frames, but the overall art quality is amazing.

Sound: 10/10
The soundtrack, openings, and endings are absolutely the best part of this anime. If MAL ranked anime based on these categories, FA:B would probably listed #1 for sound alone. Even the voice acting is great, and that can be hard to find in English dubbed anime.

Character: 8/10
Compared with many anime, this show has well-written characters who gradually develop over time. Ed’s face literally gets bigger and more mature as he grows older. Some characters seem to lack depth while many are quite life-like. Overall, the characters help to depict the themes throughout the story.

Enjoyment: 10/10
This is absolutely one of my favorite anime because of its overall quality and how enjoyable it is. It keeps you wanting more until the very end. The ending is also beautiful.

Overall: 9.2/10

Full Metal Alchemist Brotherhood is one of those extremely rare moments in anime (or entertainment in general) where an artist has one very specific vision, idea, goal etc and executes on those fundamentals outstandingly without compromise! FMA is the brainchild of talented female manga writer and artist Hiromu Arakawa and chronicles the journey of two brothers in search of a fantastical stone called the "philosopher's stone" in hopes of using it to get their bodies back. In this quest they meet a myriad of allies and foes ranging from different ethnicities, ideologies, motivations, abilities etc. As well as unearthing dark secrets surrounding their country andgovernment, the morality on the alchemy they use and the murky concept of God. FMAB with its straightforward premise takes on and successfully tackles topics like racism, God V. Science, war, Morality, Immortality etc without ever tripping over itself, overwhelming the viewer and keeping the tone from getting too dark. 

The Animation Behind FMAB is handled by none other then the wonderful studio bones! the steampunk setting is fully realized and brought to life thanks to stunning backgrounds and vistas, fluid character animation and flawless shonen action scenes that put the genres titans to absolute shame! most action or fight scenes in Shonen Anime usually bore me to tears with their terrible pacing, incessant padding and drawn out length. Battles in FMA end as quickly as they suddenly start, dazzling you with absolute stunning choreography and slick animation. needless to say you wont be waiting multiple episodes to finish one fight. 


The entire Score behind FMAB is composed by Akira Senju and while I admittedly am unfamiliar with his previous works, after watching FMAB I really think every animation studio whose serious about making a serious anime should consider hiring him! The music behind the show is simply godlike with its angelic and chilling tracks like the main theme, requiem for the brigadier general, beyond these walls etc to Military hymns like Heroic Bolero, the next chapter, the intrepid, fanfare for the brave, battle scherzo and more! The sound design behind FMAB is absolutely top tier and really comes to life when watching on a 50 inch tv and surround speakers. Gunshots, explosions and all special effects overall have movie like quality to them and really makes you wonder what the standards for other animation studios are. the last few episodes in general really sounded like I was in a movie theater!

The characters behind FMAB are what really make the show what it is. unlike a lot of shonen anime where the cast gets so big it inevitably forgets characters or has a humongous gap in relevancy or importance, FMAB miraculously avoids these pitfalls while having a pretty sizable cast. without spoiling anything I can say that the heroes are heroic and brave but not unbelievably so, most of them suffering with some sort of trauma or problematic past and its watching them power through these struggles to be the hero's their world needs is what makes them so compelling alongside their beforementioned ideologies, pasts and motivations. The same is also true for the villains.

In a era where more and more Shonens are being published everyday it can be to sit down and figure which one you would like to sink your attention into but. However if you could only pick one I would most certainly recommend FMAB. It's a well crafted story that won't cost you a lifetime of watching devotion.

After six long years, I have finally watched Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood. This anime had been sitting in my playlist all that time, always waiting for the right moment. It is ranked as the number one anime on various websites and polls, it carried a weight of expectation. Now that I have experienced it, I can truly say this is one of those rare shows that feels like a journey—one filled with emotion, growth, and meaning. But how good is it ? Story & Plot : Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood begins with a tragic and emotional premise. Edward and Alphonse Elric, two brothers who break the ultimate taboo ofalchemy to bring their mother back to life, suffer terrible consequences. Edward loses his arm and leg, while Alphonse loses his entire body. Their quest to restore what they lost gradually expands into a much larger story, one that connects personal sacrifice with national conspiracy, ancient alchemy, and the pursuit of godhood.

The series explores many themes including alchemy as a form of science, the cost of ambition, sacrifice, war, the idea of God, immortality, morality, and the fragile yet enduring nature of humanity. At first glance, these might sound like familiar or even overused ideas in shonen anime. However, Brotherhood approaches them with unexpected depth and maturity. It also delves into serious real-world issues such as racism and genocide through the Ishvalan conflict, a subplot that adds emotional weight and highlights the consequences of fear, discrimination, and systemic violence.

One of the most meaningful moments comes in a dream sequence involving Hohenheim. He reflects on his long life and the people he has known, showing how much his view of humanity has changed. Without saying it outright, the scene reveals that he has come to respect the strength and hope that people carry despite their suffering. His quiet admiration says a lot about the show’s underlying message—that even though humanity is flawed, it still holds the potential to grow and do good.

The worldbuilding in Brotherhood is also impressive. From the political structure of Amestris to the cultures of other regions like Xing and Ishval, and the detailed mechanics of alchemy, the setting feels alive and thoughtfully designed. Everything has a purpose and adds to the richness of the story.

The narrative is mostly well paced and efficiently told, with very little filler. Each arc builds naturally into the next. However, there were moments when I felt things moved too quickly. Certain elements of the lore, such as the concept of the Philosopher of the East and West, the origins and motivations of the Dwarf in the Flask, and the full depth of Father’s ambitions, could have been explored more. These concepts were incredibly interesting but sometimes felt like they were brushed past too quickly.

Some key ideas also remain somewhat unclear. For example, the Gate of Truth plays a major role in the story, but its nature and the godlike presence within it are never fully explained. The way Father’s stolen souls were returned to the people of Amestris also felt vague and could have used more clarity. 

Despite these small flaws, the story is powerful and memorable. It goes far beyond what most action anime attempt to do. It offers a thoughtful, emotional journey with elements of steampunk, mystery, and philosophical reflection. The concept of an entire nation being engineered for a single man's twisted vision of godhood is both chilling and brilliant. It ties together the personal and the epic in a way that few anime manage to achieve.


Characters :


The cast of Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is one of its strongest elements. I genuinely liked most of the characters, starting with the protagonists Edward and Alphonse Elric. Alongside them, characters like Winry Rockbell, Roy Mustang, Riza Hawkeye, Maes Hughes, Olivier Mira Armstrong (the Ice Queen of Briggs), and her brother Alex Louis Armstrong all leave a strong impression. Scar, Ling, and the warriors from Xing add cultural diversity and complexity. The Homunculi—Greed, Pride, Envy, Wrath, Lust—and their creator, Father, each bring unique traits and thematic relevance. Even the chimeras, who could’ve been forgettable, manage to contribute emotional depth.

My personal favorite characters, aside from the protagonists, are Riza, Winry, Scar, Father, and Hohenheim. Each of them stands out for different reasons—emotional weight, philosophy, or just the sheer strength of their writing.

The Elric brothers’ goal to recover their original bodies is simple on the surface, but their journey is what gives it emotional and moral depth. Along the way, they mature, learn from their past mistakes, and refuse to sacrifice others to achieve their ends. Their relationship is the heart of the show—equal parts heartfelt and comedic. They argue, tease each other, and support one another through the darkest moments. As someone who has a brother, I found their bond very relatable. The love and trust between them, even when they disagree, felt honest and real.

Some might say that Edward and Alphonse's character arcs, or Scar’s redemption, follow familiar patterns. That’s true to an extent, but they’re executed with sincerity. Scar starts as a revenge-driven character, but as he sees the consequences of his actions and confronts the pain he’s caused, he begins to change.

Roy Mustang and Riza Hawkeye’s storyline adds a layer of tension and emotional complexity. Their shared burden from the Ishvalan war, Mustang’s ambition to change the country from within, and Riza’s loyalty without blind obedience create a compelling dynamic. Their interactions show how personal conviction and political ambition can collide, and how trust can survive even the darkest moments.

The relationship between Hohenheim and Father represents a philosophical split—both born from the same origin, but shaped by entirely different views on humanity. Hohenheim comes to appreciate the beauty and hope in people, while Father seeks to discard human weakness altogether. Edward’s evolving view of Hohenheim is one of the more emotional arcs in the show. At first, he resents and blames him, but as he learns more, he finally accepts him, even calling him "Dad" near the end. Fittingly, I’m writing this on Father’s Day, which makes that scene hit even harder.

Winry is a standout among shonen female characters. She isn’t just a side character or romantic interest—she has her own growth, her own pain, and her own strength. When she learns that Scar was the one who killed her parents, her initial reaction is to take revenge. But when Ed and Al stop her and remind her of who she truly is, she makes a choice. She chooses not to kill, but to help, because that’s what her parents—both doctors—would have done. That moment reflects her growth and emotional maturity. She’s not helpless; she actively works to support the brothers, even risking her life. She’s easy to admire, and honestly, she’s one of the most likable and well-written female characters in the genre.

The Homunculi, though villains, each represent a part of human nature. Despite their arrogance and power, they all struggle with identity in their own way. Envy, at his core, is jealous of humans. Greed, who starts off as selfish and power-hungry, comes to understand that what he truly wants is connection—a place to belong and people who accept him. His final arc, especially his bond with Ling, is one of the most emotional parts of the series.

Even minor characters like Shou Tucker leave a lasting impact. His actions are horrifying, but they raise difficult questions about the morality of science when divorced from empathy. It's a chilling reminder of what happens when ambition replaces humanity.

There are a few things that could have been better. Some characters didn’t get enough screen time, and the protagonists’ development could have gone even deeper in certain areas. But these are small criticisms. Overall, I truly loved the characters. Their journeys, relationships, and choices are what make this story unforgettable.

Animation & Music  :


The animation in Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is well done, especially in the fight scenes. For its time, it holds up quite well. This was actually my first experience with Studio BONES, and while I liked their work, I think it could have been better in some parts. Certain moments felt slightly rushed or lacked polish, but overall, the action choreography and expression work were solid.

The music is another highlight. I really liked several of the opening and ending themes, especially the fifth opening, "Rain" by SID, which stands out emotionally and visually. (SID also did "Ranbu no Melody" from Bleach, which is another great track.) The fifth ending, "Ray of Light" by Shoko Nakagawa, also deserves mention for its mood and fitting tone.

Some background OSTs are very memorable, and the music overall fits the atmosphere of the show. That said, I don’t think the soundtrack is among the absolute best in anime, especially compared to a few other series. But comparisons aside, FMAB’s music is strong in its own right, and I’m glad with how it supported the emotional moments.




Other Factors :

The anime is easily accessible and does a great job of drawing in the audience from the very beginning. It’s paced to keep interest, with the early episodes pulling you straight into the story.

This was my first time seeing alchemy as a power system, and I found it unique and fascinating. I didn’t know much about alchemy beforehand, but Fullmetal Alchemist presents it in a science-fantasy style—treating it with the logic of science through concepts like equivalent exchange, while also mixing in magical elements like transmutation and elemental manipulation. It’s a creative system that adds a lot to the story.

I do think the alchemy system could have been explored more deeply. Ideas like the Philosopher’s Stone, Eastern and Western alchemy, and deeper lore had more potential that wasn’t fully tapped. Still, the power system works well for the story, and I appreciated its structure.

The character designs are well-crafted, and many fight scenes are truly enjoyable. Battles like Scar vs Wrath, Wrath vs Greed, Ed and Al vs Scar, Roy Mustang vs Lust, Roy vs Envy, and the climactic battle against Father were all highlights. The animation in these fights combined with the emotional stakes made them memorable.

The voice acting—both in Japanese and English—is strong. Each actor delivers their lines with conviction, and the emotional range of characters is conveyed effectively throughout the series.




Enjoyment  & Impact : 

I really enjoyed Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood from start to finish. Even though there were some aspects that could’ve been handled better, the overall experience was impactful and satisfying. It’s easy to see why this anime has left a mark on so many people—it’s well-written, emotionally resonant, and full of meaningful themes.

That said, for me personally, I felt like something was missing. That special emotional spark that pushes an anime into my top ten just wasn’t quite there. Of course, enjoyment is subjective—it’s not always about the best writing or structure, but more about the personal connection, emotional resonance, and philosophical impact.

That’s why, even though FMAB is a great anime, I can’t give it a perfect score or label it a "masterpiece." For me, series like Dragon Ball, Hunter x Hunter, Bleach, One Piece, Berserk (the manga), Code Geass, Naruto, Yu Yu Hakusho, Steins;Gate, and Summertime Rendering won my heart completely. They hit me on a deeper level, emotionally or thematically.

Still, FMAB is an exceptional anime—one that I respect a lot. And honestly, if I had watched it six years ago, I probably would’ve given it a perfect score. The timing of when we watch certain stories often plays a role in how they impact us, and this was a long-awaited journey that I’m still very glad I took.

Animation & Music : 4/5
Other Factors : 4.25 to 4.5/5
Enjoyment & Impact : 4.25/5

Total Score : 21.25 to 21.5 (85% to 86%)

Overall : 9/10 (A+)

Well well well....FMA. Yep, this is the one, the big one, the one everybody likes, the top anime of [i]all time[/i]. The anime you're [i]supposed[/i] to like and [i]have to[/i] like. "They will lead a good life now so everything is fine!" "War criminals should not be prosecuted and hanged" But in Germany they were, in Japan they were not, many were let go. Maes Hughes, Hawkeye and Colonel Mustang all participate as class A war criminals in FMA and are seen as empathetic, good characters. The only character who wouldn't be a class A war criminal is Louis Armstrong. And the Elrich brothers support the state of Amestris' military who committed the war crimes.

Korean, Chinese to Japanese relations aren't as great as they could be, because Japan seems to refuse to acknowledge what they really did, that it was wrong, apologize and properly atone for their actions. FMAB is a darling of anime. I think it's good, but not as great as people say. This review will mostly be negative, but here's the positive. - The story. The story is beautiful. At face value, it's the story of two brothers, Ed and Al, journeying to recover their bodies after committing Alchemy's taboo: human transmutation. Their journeys take them far and wide, pit them against enemies both human and monster, and force them to face their fears. And in the end, they return backhome, to the place they were in their innocent days, away from the
  crazy world of monsters, conspiracies, genocide, and the like. 

  However, it's also the story of Scar, the manifestation of revenge for
  a downtrodden people, and his journey of reconciliation. It's the
  story of Hohenhein, and his journey from slave 23 to being forced into
  an immortal body, facing a seemingly insurmountable enemy in a
  conspiracy that could consume the world. It's the story of Roy
  Mustang, and his journey to turn the country he loves around with a
  band of comrades willing to descend with him to hell.

The story starts out slow, but once it picks up, you're hooked. You're
  glued to the screen, pressing the next episode button.
- It's a classic shounen. This is both good and bad, but if you like
  classic shounen anime, this one is exactly it. You know the good guys
  will win out in the end, you know there'll be great reveals about
  characters' pasts and how they interrelate. If you like this kind of
  anime, this is the one for you. 

Now, for the negative. 

- The characters. Above, I seemingly praised the characters. Yes, I
  liked their concepts. But I didn't like many of the characters
  themselves. Almost all of the characters felt one-dimensional. Ed and
  Al were standard goody two shoes shounen protagonists. You know that
  they'll never sacrifice their friends for anything. You know that
  they'll fall for silly tricks of the enemy, until of course the grand
  final plan occurs, at which point they'll have predicted everything
  the enemy does (luckily FMAB doesn't have this issue too much, but I'm
  making a point). The other characters are the same. Whenever any tough
  decision arises, you pretty much already know what the characters will
  do.

Furthermore, there's very little development. Ed and Al seem barely to
  change over the course of 64 episodes. The other characters are the
  same.

As for the other characters, many got basically no development at
  all. This is fine, but it docks some points for me b/c it detracted
  from the story. I mean, really, Kimblee's men join their group just
  like that?  And then furthermore, in every scene after, they're just
  there. This is standard in shounen, but for such a masterful (and
  mature) story, I was left a little disappointed.
- The world. Usually when I digest some piece of fiction, I can tell
  whether the author did significant worldbuilding beforehand. In this
  case, my verdict is no. 

There are small details that bug me. What are the power levels of the
  various characters? Ed and Al were completely defeated by Scar the
  first time around, but later they're an even match? Wrath completely
  beats up the first Greed, but the second is fine? As usual with
  shounen, every competent character seems a reasonably equal match for
  every other, which makes no sense. If you have a gun, you beat a guy
  with a sword, and a guy with a sword beats a guy with just his bare
  hands. It isn't rocket science. 

There are also issues with alchemy. How is it Ed can transform a car
  into a completely different design? Actually, why does Ed usually just
  transform his arm into a short spear-like thing? Why isn't Ed using
  alchemy in more clever ways? At some points, there appeared to have
  been limits to alchemic power, but then we are shown them creating
  massive platforms hundreds of feet into the air. Speaking of which,
  why are there so many alchemists, each with their own special name?
  Shouldn't there be more systematization? Mustang's flame alchemy seems
  pretty OP, how has no one else figured out how to copy it? And
  furthermore, why has the military not tried to get the secret of it
  out of him?
- Comic relief. There's random comic relief. Really random. And
  unnecessary. 

Bottom line: this is an anime you watch for the story, through and
through. Don't expect anything too meaningful. But it does what it sets
out to pretty damn well.

In chronological order, I've watched the original FMA series (dubbed over in English, unfortunately), read the manga, then watched FMA Brotherhood (subbed in English, thank GOD!) after giving myself plenty of time in between. If you liked the original, you will LOVE Brotherhood. As other reviews have pointed out, there's a lot to love about this series. Instead of re-hashing all that for you, I'll just point out the differences between the original and Brotherhood and why these differences are the reason that the show's worth watching. Plot: the original series was really compelling as a stand alone. If you've never read the manga, then theorignal isn't too bad. BUT, if you're like me and read the manga (albeit for me I read it AFTER watching the original), you'll notice that the manga has a far more developed plot. And, if you're like me and watched the original and was satisfied with it (more or less, it's flaws and all) and therefore put off with having to watch Brotherhood, a whole other series, and are worried of being disappointed, let me tell you, YOU WILL NOT BE. (want reason? look at other reviews, they all say the same stuff, like the first reveiw that pops up for this). Basically, the plot, since it follows the manga, is friggin amazingly AWESOME and in no way can I find a fault or anything to put it down. Well, actually, I could probably say that the Japanese have a flare for wordiness, but it's for our benefit, considering that there is a lot to take in.

Anyways, back to business. OTHER differences:

Sound: the music is much more dynamic in this series than in the original. There's a lot of varying during the whole series even though they do have a theme music they fall back to. But the music for this series reflects the darkness and twistedness of the plot. You get the sense of some underlying BAD right from the start because of the ambience the music produces. Then there are the voices for the characters, which were well picked, I believe, even for those who watched the original series and were put off by the thought of different voices screwing up preconceived ideas of the characters. None of this occured, but I'll get back to the point on the voices under Characters. Anyways, moving on, the beginning and ending credits change throughout the series, which in my opinion is a good thing because normally I would skip through credits, but the music and animation for them are worth the watch. Which leads me to my next point....

Design: one thing I noticed right away was that the background design differed from the first. The characters were still designed the same as the original, but the setting, like the music, created GREAT ambience. For instance, perspective is very effectively used to emphasize how twisted people can be. The angles for buildings or point of view angles are distorted, showing how distorted people can look at the world and how this world is full of some messed up stuff. It foreshadows the larger plot quite nicely. And anyone with an eye for design will notice how this change in perspective really helps to add to the whole series. It's very noticeable from the start for anyone who watched the original series, but as you progress through the episodes, you don't notice as much because you're so absorbed in the plot, but that doesn't mean that it's not still in use. Unlike the original, there was also much more effort put into the fluidity of the action scenes in Brotherhood. Like any anime, signs of laziness are evident the farther into the series you get. As though to make up for this, the action scenes, and even some of the smaller motions, like the swing of the head and hair, have amazing fluidity that makes watching the show such a delight for any anime fan who's tired of seeing lazy animation (no offence to animators, it's understandable that it would end up that way).

Characters: like some other review noted, because this series follows the original manga closely, you catch far more than just a wicked plot. There are great interactions between the characters. If you're like me and watched the original series but was disappointed that the girl didn't get the guy (sorta), then, because this follows the manga, you will be happy at how this series ends *hinthintwinkwink* (though that's pretty obvious). And like I said earlier, if you watched the original and liked the characters there, you'll love the characters even more in Brotherhood. There's more depth, more emotion, and the voices are well picked to reflect that (I was worried that I wouldn't be able to watch it because I really liked the English voices in the original, but the fact that the Japanese voices were so well chosen just goes to show that the English translation wasn't half bad for finding voices that were pretty similar. However, hands down, the Japanese is alwasy better!)

Overall: YOU. MUST. WATCH. THIS. If you're looking for something with depth, THIS IS IT. There's no fluff, there's no over-ambition (and given the kind of alternative world this is set in, what large ambitions there are seem reasonable enough, all things considered. And besides, without a little ambition, things'd be BOOOORING), there's no time-wasters. You'll dive right in and get hooked! Admitedly, it's fast paced relative to the orignal, but it's to your advantage. The majority of this series is dedicated to the latter half of the manga so that we get right into the grit of it, skipping over some of the fluffy beginning while not compromising it in the least. I only suggest that you don't do all 3 (original series, manga AND Brotherhood) all in one go. I gave myself some space in between because, as mach as I liked the original and LOVED the manga, you're almost put off by the idea of having to go through it ALL OVER AGAIN after JUST having gone through it all ONCE. But, after you've given yourself some R and R, GO FOR IT. It's worth it!

For an anime that is ranked one of the highest of all time, let me state one thing that are unpopular to most of the reviews that really stood out to me-- it's the women power that is winning for me. Almost all my favorite girl characters are found in the series. I patronize how these women are strongly established and profoundly written in the plot, that they are evenly matched to the other male characters of the series. Unlike how the other Shounen animes signify the position of the women as they are minimized to damsels in distresses, and just a tool for the protagonists'emotional and romantic investment that can revitalize their power if their love interest are in verge of danger. 

The FMA: Brotherhood' women are not anything close than it. They are independent, fighters, and epic. Let's start from Mira Armstrong's dominating presence, a formidable and firm leader in high-position, then Izumi, oh dear, she defied the common characterization of a tranquil and reserved image of a mother, as she rules their household and brings down, not only the Elric brothers to their knees, but also she brought down the Central Command. Oh yes, May Chang, my little warrior who unhesitantly and bravely confronted the Father. Lastly, Even Winry Rockbell, she may not as fighter compared to the women mentioned, but the Elric Brothers could not have gone that far without the constant mechanical support from her, and this support is literally their life after all.

There are other more women to be mentioned but it's going to take more paragraphs if I exemplify them all. Even this outstanding women characterization of the series is just a piece of its entire excellence and greatness. From its concept of fundamental law about the equivalent exchange is already interesting to begin with. Then, it bloomed more with its dark yet compelling storylines, brought by improved and well-written characterization in comparison to the older version of the series. In this time, I feel more attached to certain characters like Roy Mustang and Envy because of their relevance accentuation and epic rivalry.  There are even new characters that is introduced, and the story gets even better because of them. 

Ironically, their system of power sounds realistic. There are clear boundaries about their capacity and weaknesses, well, at least for me, I understood it. In line with this, the principle of exchanges and sacrifices bring more realism to the anime, it keeps getting more sense and authentic for audience as the story progresses. The Homunculus are even better written this time. Yes, the FMA (2003) approached it more emotional, but this time, although still they added some emotional flavors to their individuality, but they are much more driven to their positions as antagonists which adds fuel--no a goddamn gasoline and diesel, to their intense heart-throbbing and stupendous battles against the main characters. Yes, I am talking about how Roy Mustang finished Lust and Envy with intense passion where his anguish is converted into a hungered wrath. Damn!

From my viewpoint, how the story ended is justified. It concluded still being faithful to its law principle of equivalent exchange. This law is everything that runs their world. This law is the root of all the personal and external dilemma of each characters that has gone down the history. Edward's sacrifice has justice to it. Moreover, Roy's tragic fate is heart-breaking. Nonetheless. I'm quite glad that the creators remained realistic and did not add some unsolicited miracles to have him a normal life. I am not saying he deserves it, I'm simply telling that things are not an absolute happy ending for everyone. I have a complete satisfaction how it is concluded for all the characters.

I won't further explain the other more aspects that have already been mentioned by other review. To sum it all up, FMA: Brotherhood is a gem, a diamond, and most recommended for people who have not yet seen it. Time might have already gone, but it still stands on the summit, and it shows. This anime is a prime legend to the anime history.

FMB is an anime that everyone should watch sometime in their life. The story is amazingly interesting and there is a vast world-building, which is simultaneously innovative and realistic. Therefore, almost every one of the innumerable characters has an interesting history and well-guarded secrets. As for the art, it's beautifully fitting with the story and characters and music is a strong part of the overall work. It's position is within my top-10 list. Story; 10 Characters; 10 Art; 9 Sound; 10Enjoyment; 10
Average; 9,8

In conclusion, if you're seeking a GOOD anime to watch, this is it. I'm sure you'll love it. But if you're seeking one to just kill time, then I don't recommend it.

Mostly spoiler-free review! I know there's a fair amount of debate as to what the "correct" way to watch Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is. Some insist you have to watch the original series, while others say you don't. Since there was a lot of contradictory information floating around the internet regarding this, I decided to take my brother's advice and just watch Brotherhood as is. That is to say, this is a review coming from someone who has only seen Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood. First off, I enjoyed it. But while I will concede that it may have been the cream of the crop for its time, I don'tthink it holds up by modern standards (in regards to both storytelling and animation quality). As is the case with other cult classics such as Death Note, I think Brotherhood suffers from its own success. A lot of people, myself included, come in with high expectations when a series such as this receives recognition to this degree, and are subsequently let down when the series doesn't turn out to be the life-changing experience that everyone has been hyping it up to be.

Now, with that little preamble out of the way, let's get into the nitty-gritty.

As far as the story goes, the overarching plot and the motivation of the main characters were interesting enough to get me hooked right from the beginning. I was rooting for Ed and Al to get their bodies back the whole way through and I was genuinely interested to see how they would achieve it when it's clearly established that any kind of human transmutation should be impossible. It goes against the laws of nature.

However, while a good story is fine and all, slow pacing or a plot that meanders around can seriously damage it. And I felt like that was exactly the case with Brotherhood. The main plot frequently takes a backseat to bore the audience with politics or history lessons from secondary characters that seem to have very little to do with the situation at hand. Exposition is also handled poorly at times, usually in the form of flashbacks that are placed in the middle of the story with no connection to the present. Meanwhile, most of the main bad guys are playing 4D chess off-screen somewhere.

So if you were expecting an "action-packed shonen" with lots of spectacular fights and intense moments, temper your expectations a little. A good chunk of the show is spent dabbling in politics (I have no idea why the author thought this was a good idea) and things don't really start happening until you're 40-50 episodes in. It's a shame, but I think the ending more than makes up for it, even if some of the plot developments didn't really make a whole lot of sense.

The cast was a mix of both bland characters and interesting characters, and there's quite a number of them so don't feel bad if you can't keep track of all of them. Some of them (four characters in particular) also seem to come into the story out of nowhere with not much of an introduction, but I just learned to accept it. These days most series tend to give secondary characters a little more backstory, but in Brotherhood most of the focus was on the main characters so you're left with a supporting cast that doesn't feel fully fleshed out. That said, some of them can be very likable and I did find a few favorites personally.

Overall, Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood was an entertaining ride with slow pacing and a finale that brings closure to just about everything you were wondering about while watching. Is it worthy of the number one spot? I wouldn't say so, I have watched plenty of shows that are far more deserving of it. Top ten, however? Yeah, definitely. Which is why I'm giving it an 8/10.

Makes you hate the fact that you already finished watching it at the end. Every single character were lovable in their own ways and through them we are taught that everything that happens is a necessity. Music was beautiful in every aspect, suits the mood of each scene and is immensely effective. The characters were full of life with excellent voice acting, personalities and roles that fulfilled the overall storyline marvelously. I can point out many weaknesses, but I see no point in doing so as it has already delivered its purpose in such a convincing way that it drowns them out. A series that touches upon meaning with wonderin life.

I just finished FMA:B and when it ended, the first thing I thought was "wow, this is actually a masterpiece". I never knew it was #1 on myanimelist. In fact, the reason I joined myanimelist was because of this anime. It's just so good, I had to read dozens of reviews because I just couldn't accept the fact that it ended. Story: There are people who've said it wasn't that original, but it is. Just because an anime, FMA:B for example, doesn't go over the top, does not mean it is not original. It is sweet and simple, but at the same time, absolutely mindblowing. Theauthor really knows how to control the story to not make it sound too cliche or mediocre. Edgy? Not really. It's understandable why some characters acted out the way they did.

Art: It's clean, detailed, and can still be considered top-level animation now. The style really draws you in. I can see the hard work put into this anime, and the fighting scenes can really blow you away. 

Sound: No problem about that. Perfectly audible. Love Alphonse's voice. 

Character: I'm just gonna say this, I LOVE LOVE LOVE THE CHARACTERS IN FMA:B. My favourite is Olivier, Scar, Izumi, Alphonse, Hohenheim... sorry I got carried away. There are really outstanding characters that range from badass to cute. I bet you'll even find yourself loving the enemies. I love Envy btw. 

Enjoyment: I literally binge-watched this, and now that i'm left with nothing after finishing it, I try to find something else that can entertain me like FMA:B can, but I still miss it a lot, so i'm thinking of re-watching it. I'm not really a re-watcher, but FMA:B is an exception. So let's just say it gets you completely glued to your screen. There was one time I watched FMA:B all day, and I told my friend "today felt like... an episode of FMA:B." 

Overall: One in a million.

NON-SPOILERY REVIEW: I haven't read the manga nor have seen the original FMA.I started watching the first episode of FMA: B, telling myself that this would be a letdown, that it's just a full-on action anime(which I don't really enjoy a lot).The first episode was alright. It made me read a lot about real world alchemy practices, that led me into watching the 2nd ep. I got hooked after watching the 2nd ep and thus my binge had begun. I had watched the entire anime within 2 weeks (college is a pain). The MCs are 2 brothers who just want their lost bodies back. The plot's simple right? Wrong.One thing leads to another and it just goes on, revealing bigger things in motion.

The music is truly wonderful. The characters feel very real and true.,especially the supporting cast. The later additions to the cast like General Armstrong and Kimblee are one of my favorites.

This anime has something for everyone. It's  action-y, comic, tragic.
Actually had me holding my tears at 2-3 scenes.

I would give it a 9.5/10. I recommend this to anyone who hasn't already watched this and is looking for some anime with really cool characters.

Story (10/10): The story is incredible! It is well thought out and deep from the start till the end. The story writing is flawless with almost no plotholes. The flow of the story was smooth and had a rather good pacing, it wasn't rushed anywhere and had no at all fillers. The ending was really satisfying. The story is a bit slow at the beginning so it may be a little boring, but give it some time, it is a built-up to the climaxing scenes towards the end. I do wish they had more alchemists, they featured only a select few even though it is known asthe land of alchemy.

Art (10/10):
For something that was drawn in 2009, it has some good animation BUT is not the best. Better than some anime in recent years though. The battle scenes were also EPIC. Really liked the character designs, waifus are prettily drawn.

Sound (10/10):
All the OP and ED are so good, personally think OP 3 is the best. The voice acting fits all the characters and also conveys the necessary emotions.

Character (10/10):
All characters are likable, even villains in fact (except for that guy on Ep 4). The villains are well thought out, they had their own motives and aren't there just because they are evil. Some side characters and villains even got character development. The MCs aren't exactly the strongest but nothing wrong with that, in fact, it makes you wonder how they would eventually defeat the villain.

Enjoyment (10/10):
Not much fan-service but that's alright. A lot of comedic scenes that are solid and funny. I also really enjoyed the quotes that they gave. This anime is extremely unforgettable and will forever be etched in my mind.

Overall (10/10):
Just watch it, its number 1 on MAL for a reason c:

After this show being on hold for 2 years or so I finally found the motivation to struggle through this show and I have to say it was worth it. Well, it was still a bit overhyped since I do not believe it deserves number 1 spot. I can totally understand why this show is very popular, but not gonna lie, the first 15 episodes or so are not that good. It gets so much better somewhere around episode 30. There is a previous adaptation of this from 2003 but it is not that good and it has quite a bit of filler and itchanges things here and there. 

Story: These two brothers named Edward and Alphonse Elric lived happily until the day their mother had died. These boys learned alchemy and they tried to resurrect their dead mother, but since human transmutation is taboo and probably not possible, they both made great sacrifices, Edward lost his arm and leg while Alphonse lost his entire body. Now that they have seen the "truth" they can do alchemy without a transmutation circle. Now they start their quest to get their original bodies back. Along their journey they do many things such as make new friends, lose important people, help people, destroy a false god and many more great things. An important part of the story are Homonculi which are artificial humans which are made from philosopher's stone which is made by sacrificing multiple human beings. Along their journey they meet all the 7 deadly sins who are homonculi. All of them have their own unique design and power.

Characters: The cast is very unique I would say. Our main hero Edward is a state alchemist called Fullmetal Alchemist. He is heroic, stubborn and he gets angered quite easily. Due to his height of 148 centimeters he is called little by many people and that ticks him off. Alphonse is Edwrads younger brother. Due to his height and his metallic body, people call him the Fullmetal Alchemist. He is more calm and he is stronger than his older brother. Winry Rockbell is Edwards and Alphonses childhood friend and an automail engineer. Automails are metal prostetics. She cares deeply about the elric brothers but can act quite stubbornly about stuff. Von Hohenheim is the Elric Brothers dad. He is a living philosopher's stone. He is probably my favourite character in the series. He is calm, smart and epic as heck.
Roy Mustang is the flame alchemist. He is probably the deadliest alchemist towards humans and homoculi since he can burn all of them to dust. When he is angry he is one scary mofo, mostly he is calm goofball. There are more great characters to write about but I am too lazy. The supporting cast in this show is amazing. So many great characters.

OST: There are many good tracks here and there. For openings most of them are good. Only the second one kinda sucked in my opinion. My favourite was probably number 4.

This show is a good place to start when watching anime. SO this is a good gateaway anime. If there is something I mildly dislike is the comedy. Don't get me wrong there is some hilarious moments here and there. But at least in the start is was not that funny. The I guess forced chibification of the characters got real annoying at one point but it kinda stopped somewhere in the middle.

If you like shounen anime or just good story and animation I recommend this anime. TBH I think this is one of them must watch anime.

f there is no way out, then you can always do it! My acquaintance with this wonderful anime series was quite long. That there was no time, then the opportunity to watch it ... Very often I came across reviews, mostly laudatory, but did not pay much attention to them. It just so happened that I do not read the number of positive reviews as an indicator of the quality of anime / film / book, etc. But when it finally happened, and I watched this series, I was absolutely delighted! Yes, nothing really fascinated me except for Candy-Candy, Harry Potter and Avatar: the legends of theAang. I just could not tear myself away from this series. The main characters and the plot immediately sunk into the soul and was drawn to find out - and what next?

What upset and even outraged, is the assaults on this anime in the style of: 'It's not in manga', 'Brotherhood is better', etc. No, the Brotherhood is no better! I will express my opinion about it in another review, but I want to say that this series is much deeper in plot than the original manga and the Brotherhood. Yes, it usually happens that an impromptu production cannot surpass the original. But in this case it is.

So, what we have: there is a world parallel to ours (which was confirmed at the end of the series), in which medieval science - alchemy - developed. Yes, at first glance it might seem that this alchemy is akin to magic in Harry Potter, but not so simple! Very quickly we are given to understand that alchemy is precisely SCIENCE (although sometimes it still reminds magic), and it is based on the laws of nature, the main of which is the law of equivalent exchange. 'One cannot get something out of nothing. To get something, one must give back something of equal value ”- this law reads. Let us now recall how Harry Potter and his friends turned living rats and ravens into goblets and back in the classroom, while the animals remained alive! Well this is a digression. The world of Alchemy is completely different. It seems to be similar to our world at the beginning of the 20th century, but at the same time it is closer to steampunk and diesel punk. The fashion of this world is modernized, but simplified. If the heroes wear mi-skirts, then there are no hints of all kinds of sparkles, prints and the like, which makes me personally happy.

Plot: As many could read on Wikipedia, the plot is based on the story of two brothers - Edward and Alphonse Elrikov, who lost their mother at a fairly young age and decided to bring her back to life with the help of alchemy. But the children did not take into account the same law of equivalent exchange, as a result of which the older, Ed, lost his leg, and the younger Al, the whole body. In a desperate attempt to save his brother. Ed also sacrifices his hand and attaches his brother's soul to the armor in the basement of their house. After a while, familiar auto mechanics set Edu prostheses-auto armor instead of arms and legs and the brothers go on a dangerous path in the hope of recovering what was lost. Soon, the boys learn about the philosopher's stone and from now on decide to find it at all costs. Such a plot plot few people can leave indifferent. I will not reveal all the secrets of the plot, but the ending in this series is very unexpected! Predicting it is almost impossible! I can reassure those who are especially impressionable, except that the brothers will eventually achieve their goal. True, they will again have to pay dearly for this.

Characters: This is what you can talk about for a very long time. There are a lot of interesting and simply charming characters. The characters are all different, for every taste, so to speak. The characters and relationships of the characters are revealed very well. When you look at them, you even forget that they are all painted and perceive them as real people. So they are alive, natural and multifaceted in terms of characters.

It's not impossible not to fall in love with the Elric brothers. They are quite different in character, but at the same time they are incredibly similar in their mentality and determination. They are touched to the depths of their souls by brotherly love, caring for each other and attempts to return what was lost precisely to their brother, and not to themselves. These boys suffered a lot of rather cruel trials, but they go through life with their heads held high. Ed, although hot-tempered and sometimes cynical, Al, in contrast to his brother, is quite reasonable. But both brothers are very strong in spirit, kind and incredibly optimistic. And to keep all this in your heart, seeing all the cruelties of life from childhood, is very difficult!

I would also like to mention other memorable characters - the head of the brothers, Colonel Roy Mustang, Lieutenant Lisa Hawkeye, Major Maes Hughes madly adoring his wife and daughter, childhood friend of the guys Winry Rockbell, fond of auto-armor, alchemy teacher of many other Izumi Curtis brothers and many ... The characters turned out bright and memorable. Each has its pros and cons, as well as its own personal drama.

The villains are just as impressive. Some homunculi are worth it! I think it will be more interesting to find out who they are and where they came from. Among them there are both inveterate villains and scum that has ended, and quite pleasant and even tragic characters.

[WARNING FOR SPOILERS ON FIRST PARAGRAPH] I binged FMA:B after binging the 2003 FMA adaptation, and while I fell in love with both adaptations, there's a couple things I missed. I personally LOVE 2003's twist of Mustang being the one who killed Winry's parents, and honestly, to me, it just sounds so much more realistic as a show that shows a bit about how people like him are able to do anything under orders. I feel like in Brotherhood (although probably in the manga canon as well, haven't gotten to it yet) he's made to seem more like just an awful person than a vigilante. I missedthe whole Dante storyline a bit, since I thought she was just an amazingly written villain. I also feel the whole ongoing joke of Ed being short gets really tiring after the first 10 times (or whatever) it's mentioned.

However, in Brotherhood, I find it very beautiful how Hohenheim is portrayed in a much more humane way, instead of the somewhat selfish man desperate for eternal life we see in 2003.

Brotherhood's animation is simply a delight compared to 2003's, however, I personally think 2003's soundtrack is much more elaborate and entrancing.

Basically, I think both have great parts to them. However, 2009 feels much less terrifying and serious than 2003, which is something I missed a bit. Humor is sometimes used in situations where I think it wouldn't be needed, but I believe for younger viewers, it must be a breath of fresh air.

tl;dr both are great and have their own good parts!

I didn't watch it at the time it came outbecause I didn't really understand how it would be different from the 2003 series, and the first episode is kind of a confusing one. They were trying to tell us this would be a brand new story starting from the beginning and following the manga more closely, but it seemed this first episode wouldn't make any sense to anyone who wasn't already familiar with the characters. It was like they were trying to say, yeah it's a new show but come on in look we've got all your favorite guys in it.

Lowart is a youtube channel that has a really long in depth video series talking about all the differences between the two shows, so if you've got like 5 hours to kill check it out. I think that regardless this show is one of those few great anime that manages to tell a complete story in just around 50-75 episodes. I think this is a level of storytelling that is rare in the medium. Most often you'll either get anime that run 12 episodes and never get an ending, go buy the manga please, or you get One Piece. 1000 episodes strong upon writing this and no signs of stopping anytime soon. It's okay to let a story progress quickly and end organically rather than milk it forever just because it keeps making money.

It's a good story with amazing character writing that manages to be complete and cohesive and not go on forever.

So yeah maybe it's a little overhyped because of it's position as the great gateway anime, but honestly you could do much worse for a gateway series. Imagine becoming an anime fan on stuff like Trigun or Cowboy Bebop. Frickin anime boomers.

There's not too much to say about this anime that hasn't been said already, but I did want to share my opinion on it regardless as someone who went in with high standards and was already aware of the rating of this show beforehand. In terms of the pros and cons of this anime, the pros are: Very compelling, thought out, and unique story. It doesn't have many holes in it (none that matter, anyway) and the pacing is pretty close to perfect. It's pretty fast pace at times, especially in the beginning, but it remains to be that perfect balance of not too fast-pacedand not too slow. The characters are all pretty likable for the most part and some have more character development than others. The soundtrack is amazing and definitely help to create and amplify the atmosphere of the scenes in the show. The ending is fantastic, and the story wraps up without leaving any important loose strings. I also love the fact that it doesn't go the typical shounen all-powerful kid route and instead opts for a story in which the protagonist and people around him really aren't that powerful compared to the villains (with one exception) and so it doesn't just come around to deus ex machina bs. Instead, it uses actual strategy and plot progression to deal with the antagonists. 

Now for the cons; I honestly hated the comedy throughout this show. It was extremely repetitive and often cringeworthy, which I could forgive, if it wasn't for the fact that these comedy scenes often take place in the middle of what should be SERIOUS scenes. There's plenty of examples of this that you'll see throughout the show, but the creator clearly does not understand when there should be comedy and when there shouldn't be. I understand not wanting the to take itself too seriously, but when you implore serious and thought-provoking scenes and then have a random burst of comedy it just makes the seriousness less serious, giving viewers a strange mood-whiplash. The story was also pretty boring at times, and I don't think it has anything to do with being slow paced, as it's not. Certain arcs of the story just simply don't have much interesting going on and it led to me just being straight up bored throughout large parts of the show leading up to the climax. The main 2 protagonists were also just...alright? I don't have any real dislike for them but nothing about them was all that interesting to me. Edward, to me, doesn't seem to have much of any 'development'. He was already incredibly remorseful for what he did in the beginning and also realized that humans can't come back and he was foolish to try and play god. In the end, it seems that rather than developing he just came to a sudden realization. Alphonse is just simply a young, loveable and sweet child but that's pretty much all there is to say about him. The father (both the antagonist and the father of ed) are definitely the most interesting characters to say the least. 


Overall, I still really enjoyed this show and thought it lived up to the hype for the most part. It feels really complete and just all around a great story. I wouldn't say it was groundbreaking or a 'masterpiece', though. I don't know if this show is really a 9 but I'm going more off of the words use to describe the numers, with 9 being a 'great' and I do feel that this show is great.

"Hagane no Renkinjutsushi: Fullmetal Alchemist", aka "Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood" is the second anime adaptation of the FMA manga. Unlike the first anime series, Brotherhood follows faithfully the original material. It's considered a masterpiece and an amazing adaptation by many people, but I disagree. Story: 8/10 The plot is really grandiose: in the beginning the story focuses only on the Elric brothers, but then a lot of new characters are introduced. There are no real plot holes, but sometimes the story can be really predictable, especially during the last arc. The ending felt artificial and saccharine. The beginning is pretty bad too: the firstepisode is a poorly written filler, and the first 14 episodes cut away two chapters. Also, the world building isn't as good as people say: in fact, we know nothing about all the countries introduced in the story (like Xing or Drachma), except Amestris. 

 Art: 7/10
 The art style is similar to the manga one, but it didn't work as well as the original. It feels lifeless and the bright colors don't fit he dark tone of the story. The backgrounds are really bland. However, the animation is fluid and the CGI is fine for a 2009 anime.

 Sound: 6/10
 I liked the OPs and the EDs, but the OST is pretty forgettable and the same soundtracks (like Lurking) are reused in almost every episode. The japanese dub is really good.

 Characters: 8/10
 Like I said before, FMAB has a solid cast, but not as much as the manga. Also, there are too many characters, and because of that the main character doesn't have enough screen time to grow as a person. The brotherhood between him and Alphonse is never explored.

 Enjoyment: 9/10
 Despite it being inferior to the manga, I really enjoyed Brotherhood. It wasn't really emotional or anything and the themes aren't very well explored, but I just couldn't stop watching it. The only things that I really didn't like were the first and the last arc, the way the main character was left aside and the cheap comedy. 

 Overall: 8/10
 FMAB is a very good anime, but it's not the best out there. It's vastly inferior to the original manga and it doesn't excel in anything. If you're new to the franchise I recommend  to watch FMA 2003 + Shamballa first, and only then to read the manga or to watch Brotherhood.

FMAB is one of the most famous shows on this site, having held the #1 spot for quite some time, and after having watched it in its entirety I definitely can see why. I don't personally think its my favorite show, but I can definitely see why a large majority of people do. It manages to weave a long and interesting narrative through all 64 of its episodes. When so much of the modern anime scene is dominated by 1 cour shows, it can be nice to see a larger scale narrative like AOT or FMAB, they have more time to develop and set upthe story, leading to a much more satisfying narrative conclusion. Of course problems can arise within longer narratives: the larger amount of space can lead to lengthy filler portions in works with poorly planned or paced narratives, lengthy plots can sometimes become complicated and convoluted, or they can just end up being too damn long for you to ever want to finish. FMAB is the definition of a well executed longer-form narrative, and its 64 episodes are all worth the time investment to reach its conclusion.

The plot woven through those 64 episodes is definitely my favorite part of FMAB, because of how well it fills its runtime. The pacing is sublime, starting comfortably slow as the characters slowly uncover the plot and basic characters, elements, and setting are set up and established. The first chunk of the show is at this slow pace, as Edward and Alphonse go on small adventures dealing with relatively small scale problems as the bigger plot is teased more and more until part of its revealed in a big sub-climax and the stakes are raised and the pacing is sped up. This formula is then continued all the way up until the finale, where all of the elements come together in a super epic climax that ends the long journey with a satisfying conclusion. FMAB also has its own fair share of interesting plot twists throughout its runtime, while none of them are anything as crazy as what's in AOT, they all keep the plot fresh and interesting to make sure our heroes aren't just following the same exact goal for the entirety of the series. Bones did a great job with their execution of the plot and it is easily the strongest part of the series.

FMAB also carries a great sense of humor along with it in addition to its fantastic story. I found the jokes decently funny and they were great at easing the tension in the moments in the show when Ed and Al weren't fighting for their lives against incredibly powerful enemies. Humor is obviously even more subjective then other aspects of an opinion on a series, but personally I liked a good majority of the jokes  in the series and found them to be a refreshing break from the rest of the action and drama that populates FMAB.

Second to the story, my next favorite element would have to be the characters. While I don't think they are a masterclass in character writing, I believe they all feel a bit grounded and relatable in some way. Their are plenty of valid arguments as to why they aren't good because of things like being defined by trauma or wearing their goals on their sleeve, I don't think they are necessarily bad characters for those traits. While sometimes a character can feel like just existing to die in a dramatic fashion, if I still enjoyed that character and their death impacted me, then I say its fine. Their are plenty of really blatant examples of "tear-baiting" characters as I am going to call them and I feel that FMAB isn't really one of those blatant examples. With one exception, I think pretty much every tear-baitey character in the show has some other reason to exist other than just getting a reaction out of the audience when they die. They are more developed and well rounded than characters that exist literally just to die. I ended this series enjoying a majority of the characters and I think that overall they did a pretty good job in their execution of them.

The art of FMAB was definitely one of its more weaker aspects, it was far from anything even resembling bad, but it was definitely one of the most average feeling aspects of the show. The overall style feels pretty generic barring some character designs. It wasn't something that detracted from the viewing experience, but it didn't add anything too special.

The music definitely fairs much better. The show has some good OP's and ED's for one (except for the bad ones) and has some quite memorable tracks played throughout the series. I don't know if its just because they were played throughout a 64 episode series that I have some of them engrained in my memory, but they are memorable all the same. The tracks are all well suited to the show and its style and setting, and exercise great control over the tone and feel from scene to scene.

FMAB is definitely one of the great shows in the vast medium that is anime. It is not personally one of my favorites, but I think it is a great example of what a shounen anime can be given time, effort, and sufficient development. I can totally see why it has received so much praise and will probably continue to for some time. I enjoyed my time watching this show and can firmly recommend it to basically anyone who likes anything even closely resembling the shounen genre.

Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood isn’t just one of the best shounen anime — it’s one of the best anime ever made, period. It delivers on all fronts: story, characters, themes, and world-building. If you’re looking for a series that balances action, emotion, philosophy, and character growth, this is it. The story is masterfully written. It follows the Elric brothers, Edward and Alphonse, as they seek to restore their bodies after a forbidden alchemic ritual goes horribly wrong. What starts as a personal journey quickly expands into a larger plot filled with government conspiracies, moral dilemmas, and ancient truths. Every arc ties into the greater narrative, and thepacing rarely falters. There are moments of laughter, heartbreak, tension, and triumph — all placed with perfect balance.

The characters are phenomenal. Nearly every named character — hero or villain — is given meaningful development. The Elric brothers are both relatable and admirable, and their bond is the emotional core of the story. Side characters like Mustang, Scar, Hohenheim, and the Homunculi are complex and memorable, each representing different aspects of humanity and ideology.

The art is sharp and expressive. While not the most experimental visually, it’s consistent and polished, especially in fight scenes and emotional moments. The animation quality stays high throughout the series, and the soundtrack complements the tone beautifully — from epic battles to quiet, introspective scenes.

There’s a reason this anime sits at the top of so many “best of all time” lists. It tells a complete, impactful story without unnecessary filler, and it sticks the landing perfectly.

Is this anime overhyped? Yes. Is it still enjoyable and good piece? Yes. Can one spot fundamentals of anime art and joy in it? Yes. After long years of avoiding FMA I tried first version from 2003. Eventually I dropped it, because it was too much depressing for me and I really couldn't enjoy it at all. Few years later I tried FMA: Brotherhood and I am amazed. First I would like to say that his anime is overhyped by some core fans. FMA:B is far from being masterpiece but that doesn't mean it's bad anime. It's really good one and I really enjoyed it. However FMA:Bcommunity is defending something that simply doesn't exist, at least from my point of view. Of course whether one does like something or not is really subjective. Still I think I can claim with calm mind that I've seen better anime. With FMA:B I just didn't have that nice feeling of frost on the back of the neck. But it's really great anime.

To start with the bad things... 

1) World and its state lack some development. Basically there are just bubbles with stories you can see, meanwhile it looks like the rest of the world would be dead. 
2) Chracter development of some characters is basically non-existent. One would expect some change after months but no, nothing, some characters are basically the same. 
3) Missed opportunity in some love stories and couples - I know it's technically not romantic anime, however anime is teasing you with few couples again and again and in the end you don't even have satisfaction from it as almost nothing happens at the end of the anime. 
4) Deus ex-machina - some events work on this simple principle, whenever something bad might happen, miraculously some character steps in without further explanation. Sometimes we got explanation but it's still kinda weird. Not really bad mechanism but badly handed, if you will.

While those are some bad things about anime and reasons I am not giving this 10/10 and why is this anime far from being perfect, I have also few positive things:

1) Story itself is amazing - I have already something behind me and also have a lot of experience with story telling and creating custom characters, worlds, etc. Regarding anime I've seen a lot of original ideas as well as some copied ones. But FMA:B really amazed me regarding this, because story is really creative with many details in it and many enjoyable moments. You can feel all emotions within that story, which is something really special. You have reasons to cry, laugh, be scared, be amazed... 
2) Animation - I was a bit skeptical when I saw initial animations but they were amazing. 
3) Music/sound effects - some openings are literally something, that can grab your heart. Music in anime itself is great too and basically is helping you to develop some bond towards the anime. Sound effects aren't wacky or weird and I kinda like some old school touch in some of them.
4) Humour - kinda funny chibi jokes and such things, they are not annoying but rather really enjoyable. 
5) Reasons for plot - basically you are naturally getting new and new reasons for story to continue while they are not annoying and make sense. 
6) Satisfying ending - not something you can say with every anime. I have to admit that I wished for few things to see at the end and didn't happen, which was kinda sad. On the other side ending of the story as whole was really satisfying.

Overall I can definitely recommend this anime. One has to take it with a grain of salt as it's really overhyped for some weird reason and it can really damage your joy from it. But now I see the reason why this anime is so popular, it's not a fluke. And I am happy I gave chance to this anime and finished it.

FMAB review by Rfonzx (potential spoilers!) FMAB. This anime is WIDELY KNOWN around the world for being the number one anime on MAL. 7/14 is the date when I've finally decided to watch FMAB. Why, you said? because I wanted to know the reason why does this anime gets the number one spot on MAL. It took me like 14 days to complete the whole 64 episodes of it. I'd consider it a binge watch, since I usually don't watch anime at a consistent amount of rate. And now, here I am, making a review about this anime. (disclaimer: this is my first time making ananime review, and there's gonna be a POTENTIAL SPOILERS here on the review!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!)

Plot : 9.5/10
At first, I thought the plot of FMAB would be way more superior than the cast. But I was 100% sure that I was wrong back then. But that doesn't mean that the plot was bad, it was good. The pacing of this anime is fine, you just gotta pause the certain confusing part of the episode to make sure that you don't miss anything. The first 50 episodes are good, but the last 14 episodes are definitely the best part. It was like a roller coaster of emotion, there are times when you feel like you're gonna bawl your eyes out, and there are times when you feel a heartwarming feelings in you.

Art (Sound and animations)
For the sound, it was definitely a 7.75. It was nothing special, but it sure does the job, especially at the last few episodes, it was done thoroughly. For the opening and endings, my favorite openings are the 5th one while my favorite endings are the 4th one. Animation-wise, it was around a 8.5-9. Some of the fight scenes are very well made and I found nothing (about the animation) that bothers me.

Cast : 9.75
So basically the Elric Bros are the main attention of the cast. Their character journey throughout the anime is beautifully made, especially at the 60-64th episode. That's basically their whole character conclusion. The way Ed overcomes his hardships throughout the series and then finding out what was the true meaning of the "truth" really is was defo the peak moment on the anime. 95% of the cast serves a huuuugeee role on the plot. They were made for a necessary purposes. And almost every one of them are well written (IMO the best written characters on this anime are Scar, Hohenheim, and Edward). FMAB's cast is definitely one of the best cast that I've ever seen. (This cast is in my opinion slightly better than AOT's)

Enjoyment: 9.75/10
Well, my enjoyment for the series would be a 10 if only I didn't get spoiled. But it was   very enjoyable nonetheless.

Overall: 9.5/10
Overall, this anime satisfied myself in almost every aspect (except the sound, it didn't fulfill my expectation very well). My predicted rating for the series before I watched the whole thing is actually a 10. I would never expect it to be a 9.5, but you know what? 9,5 is still a high rating. 

Well, now I know why does this anime is the best-rated anime on MAL. It 100% deserves the rating, cause it's a great anime to watch and I had a great journey watching it. It's not the best anime ever made, though. There are a few animes that are better than FMAB (Like Eva, AOT, and ASV). But it doesn't mean that FMAB is not worth the watch just because it isn't the best anime ever made.  If you haven't seen the anime yet, then you're truly missing out! It deserves the watch!!
