As I get older, I find myself often seeking out novelty when it comes to entertainment. Like with games, I still enjoy epic RPG and RTS games, but these days I'm mostly drawn to ones with unusual concepts like taking on the role of a shop keeper or a passport stamper rather than a world-saving hero. Anime is no exception, so when I came across one about a slime - that most humble of monsters residing on the bottom rung of the RPG food chain - my immediate reaction was "sign me up, Scotty!" Novelty concepts can only get you so far though; a lot hinges onthe execution. The execution of "That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime", or TenSura for short, is nothing special. The show is passable, and has moments when it delivers on the novelty premise. But overall it doesn't feel as fresh as I had hoped.

TenSura seems to have its fingers stuck in several popular pies. In case you haven't guessed from the synopsis-style name, the show originates from a series of light novels, set squarely in the trendy isekai game world, where girls are mostly big-breasted moebaits, all drawn to the protagonist like flies to a slimy poo. In addition, TenSura wants to be comedy, drama, action, fantasy adventure amongst other things. As a result of being spread so thinly, large parts of the series comes off as sterile, going through the typical motions of whatever it's trying to be with varying degrees of success, but never quite striking gold.

To start with, TenSura leans too heavily on its JRPG origins. While I can appreciate a few good jokes referencing the sort games the show parodies, the trappings of the settings are so in-your-face that it interferes with the storytelling. One of the main symptoms takes the form of the Great Sage. This is some AI-esq entity residing in the mind of Rimuru, our slimy main character, acting as his guide, his advisor and his analyst all rolled into one. I understand it's the in-story representation of a game's manual/system for easing in a new player, which is actually a pretty good parody idea. But that kind of gimmick can only be played for a quick laugh. TenSura chooses instead to have the Great Sage act as a uncomfortably big plot device, a cheap and deep well of knowledge which can be plumbed for exposition at the leisure of Rimuru, our slimy n00b.

This kick-down-the-barriers approach to storytelling is something TenSura does a lot. Not a single obstacle appear to exist in this fantasy world that Rimuru, our great slimy leader, cannot overcome within a couple of episodes, whether through brains or brawn. To be fair, I do like the fact that Rimuru doesn't just use his overpowered powers to muscle his way to solutions, he also applies the skills and experience of his previous life as a middle management salaryman. In this respect TenSura reminds me a little of Maoyuu. But it also suffers the same problem as Maoyuu, in that Rimuru operates at a level so far above everyone else that the story struggles to build up any tension or drama. With a few powerful attacks, Rimuru can decimate an army; with a few choice words or action, he can sway enemies into loyal allies. Everything feels too easy.

The dramatic elements of TenSura suffers particularly from the shortcuts taken by the writing. The anime's idea of fleshing out the characters consists of crowbarring in a tragic backstory right before they kick the bucket, and then expect you to care, even though you've only known the character for about half an hour. The underwhelming writing also shows itself in the dialogues, where we get treated to regurgitated "classic" lines such as "BAKA BAKA BAKA BAKA BAKA BAKA BAKA BAKA!!"

As an action series, TenSura does serve up some pretty cool battle sequences and flashy special effects. But Rimuru, our overpowered slimy protagonist, tends to drain the tension out of most battles he gets involved in.

Comedy is what TenSura does best, and the show delivers its fair share of amusing jokes. Unfortunately though, TenSura thinks it's funnier than it actually is. The show has a tendency to milk its jokes beyond their worth through over-reaction and repitition. When the jokes are funny, the milking diminishes the humour; when the jokes aren't funny, the anime just comes off as lame. Kind of like being in the presence of an irritating guy who insists on gaffawing at every joke he makes. It only gets worse when he starts telling the same ones over and over.

TenSura is at its most amusing when making good use of the novel premise. Had the show ended after one cour, it would have been better for it. But not content to focus on the one good thing it has, TenSura overextends in order to hit all the popular bases. Predictably, the novelty starts wearing off in the weaker second half, to which TenSura responds by turning to fake novelty, the kind which have become stone wall cliches by this point. For example, TenSura would introduce a demon lord who - get this - takes the form of a pink haired, hyper active moeblob with an annoyingly high pitched voice! Who could possibly have guessed! By this point, female characters in TenSura had become cancerous in general. It's like they were designed to irritate, and the voice actresses duly obliged by turning in a suite of nails-on-chalkboard-worthy performances. Also, The joke about Rimuru, our lecherous slimy harem-lead, nestling against a girl's jiggling jugs and being fawned and fought over by everyone not in possession of a dick may have been funny first time round, but it's certainly not good enough as a running gag.

Hmmm, this review came off harsher than I intended. I guess it's hard to expound on TenSura's strengths when it doesn't really have any outstanding points. Much like a slime, it mostly ambles along in an cutesy, inoffensive, mildly amusing kind of manner. "Jack of all trades" is another way of describing the show except labelling it as "jack" flatters it - it's more like an eight of all trades and certainly master of none.

Personal rating: +0.5 (decent)

LA was not expecting to like it but damn was LA surprised by Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken by the end of it. Isekai had flood of mediocre and lazy installments for anime from Isekai wa Smartphone to Tomo ni. to Death March kara Hajimaru Isekai Kyousoukyoku and LA just started to get tired of the trend, but Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken was a fresh of breath air in a sense. Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken at the start starts off like your typical isekai overpowered main protagonist harem-like anime series just that this time the main protagonist turns into a slime before he goes intoanother world and he quickly learns overpowered abilities that make him feared, but him being a slime, a monster KNOWN to be a "starter monster" in RPG's, not many buy this. LA didn't like this as a premise not to mention slightly rushed especially with the transition of the main protagonist Satoru Mikami into another world into a slime and his quick gather of abilities making him an all powerful monster. But Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is definitely one fo those shows where you just have to carry on watching it and to this credit LA will say the first few episodes weren't a great first impression towards this series.

It's not until Rimuru (Satoru's slime form name in his new world) starts making a small goblin village flourish and gaining new allies where the key to this anime truly lies. See Rimuru knows he can't go back to his world, his previous life was snuffed out, so he has no plans of going back so he might as well make the most of it in this new world, so with the good natured person he is, he helps the small goblin village from attacks from other monsters and from then on, gathers allies, monster and human alike. Thing is due to his good natured demeanor, Rimuru NEVER kills anyone and rather talks it out, he only "eats" them if he has no choice and the villain in question is causing more trouble than he's worth that he'll resort to extreme "final move" methods and with this he gain allies, from wolves, lizardmen, dwarves, fairies, demons and oni.

There is one other character of note and that is Rimuru's "chosen" one by the name of Shizue Izawa voiced bu Yumiri Hanamori, another person summoned into this world, but forced through a demon pact, Rimuru befriends her and later on passes her legacy onto Rimuru, giving Rimuru more motivation and something to strive for in this world than his own and two great things comes from entire ordeal.

One and the most obvious one being that Rimuru grows through his friendships and allies especially with Shizue as she was extremely important to Rimuru's growth as a character throughout the anime because of it and this extends onto any new ally he faces even if they are at first deterred by Rimuru, he let bygones by bygones and makes their place in Rimuru's flourishing village grow that much more as a result.

The second and the more obvious one is that Shizue's inclusion added ALOT of world building to Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken's world, what does LA mean by that?, well though the anime mostly resides in the goblin village at first, Rimuru explores his new world, makes trade deals, recruits blacksmiths, architects, magic users to grow not only his village but the world building itself, like a two for one deal and how they implemented this was actually ingeniously done. Coming from an isekai, the main focus for the most part, the bland main male protagonist, Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken manages to work it's world building and it's character development all in one just by simply befriending them.

Now the other part of the world building comes in with Shizue and how she was summoned into the world, which brings up new lore as the world Rimuru is in now are also inhabited by humans from his previous world, like this is a normal occurrence. Lastly would be the villains themselves and this ties it in as a demon summoned Shizue and one of Shizue's motivations was to find her master, now passed onto Rimuru wants to find Shizue's master, but it's not easy when the demons are one, powerful and two, send in monsters or plan up something that threatens Rimuru's village and his allies' territories.

If Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken was telling of a theme, it's showing the positive, befriending nature of Rimuru that is at the core of Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken and sure it took time for this theme to be fleshed out in the anime but it was pretty solid by the end of the anime even with all the demon scheming and other important character backstories were going on at the time.

With all that being said, LA's favourite characters form the anime (and there are ALOT of character to be honest) are, Millim Nava voiced by Rina Hidaka as a hyper genki and powerful demon lord but fancies Rimuru also she had some great comedic moments at that (though LA thought she was a filler only character for some reason but no she's canon!), Shino voiced by M.A.O an oni who is Rimuru's secretary and has an obvious crush on Rimuru and finally Gobuta voiced by Asuna Tomari, a pipsqueak of a goblin but has some crazy latent luck or he was naturally powerful (an obvious but good gag for this character and comes to a direct comparison to Rimuru in a ways of looking weak but is waay more powerful than they look) and Shizue gets a mention for being a pinnacle part of the anime and the turning point of when the anime got REALLY good.

8Bit who did the animation actually did an amazing job with the animation, from the exotic character designs and some impressive battle animation. The character designs are just by default exotic with the variety of species Rimuru take sin and sometimes some changes to them with Rimuru's magic and whatnot and LA is some fo the few that actually liked the oni's change to be more human-like features. The battle animation was greatly done with each attack done with great impact helped by the sound direction and background work. 8Bit outdid themselves with the animation to be totally honest here though 8Bit had always had potential from their other anime works, this was just showing what they could really do and maybe more.

Voice cast, well due to the large cast, LA will go with only the most notable ones, Miho Okusaki as Rimuru was great with an amazing range of cadence and really gave life to Rimuru and his likable personality, Rina Hidaka of course gets a mention as the destructive genki Millim, Yumiri Hanamori as Shizue was awesome, M.A.O and Sayaka Senbongi as Shion and Shuna was rather well done even as a pigeonholed role from both but still. Great cast what else?

LA will say that Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken isn't without flaws, LA already mentioned the first few episodes were rushed and cliched of an isekai but there is another one and that is as much as LA LOVES the world building in this anime, Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken does tend to exposition ALOT using the Grand Sage voiced by Megumi Toyoguchi, but man there were episodes where it was exposition and not much else, yes it helps us the audience gets us in the know as well as setup and build up for the upcoming episodes but it did kill the pacing...."rarely" though.

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is one of those shows you just can't judge on the first episode, you NEED to watch the entire thing and your judgment and feelings towards this anime will change, it did for LA as LA thought LA was gonna see the typical overpowered harem isekai anime scthick all over again, but nope, we get a one part Rimuru wrecks a monstrosity that the demons made, one part wholesome anime about a slime who befriends and grows a NATION of monsters filled with character development from even some minor characters and great amount of world building to make this world both have that nostalgic RPG feel but also make the world alive and realized at the same time, yes the anime does get exposition heavy at times but that does not detract from what Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken has and had going for it and with it already announcing a second season, there is ALOT more potential that Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken can go and LA will be interested where it'll go in it's second season. Color LA surprised by this isekai installment. 

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken maybe on normal mode, but man LA didn't think making a Civilization anime adaptation with a slime could be this much fun!

Please note this review is intended to be read by those that have finished watching Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken and while care has been taken to minimize story related spoilers there may still be spoilers within character analysis. You have been warned. Based off a popular manga and light novel of the same name Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken which is better known by its English title of That time I got reincarnated as a slime and its synonym’s of Tensura is a fantasy and shounen anime that gives us the opportunity to see what will happen if a mid-aged office worker who seemsto be content with his life as just another salaryman that lives in the metropolis of Tokyo were to one day while providing his juniors with some well earned life lessons were to suffer a truly untimely death that would rather than transport him to the netherworld where all deceased would go would rather see him transported to an alternate world that’s more akin to that of a game world than the real world. However, rather than being transported to said world as a human being as one would expect he would instead be reincarnated as something that can be said to be the lowest of monsters which is that of a slime. 

The Isekai genre of anime, light novels and manga fame is a well-trodden one thanks largely due to the ease of use of its main concept which is the transportation of a being human or otherwise from one world to another parallel world. Looking back through the previous anime season’s one can see many great examples of the genre such as the famed Konosuba, Re Zero and Log Horizon series. However, apart from the genre, there is one other common theme that links these series together and this is the fact that whichever world the main characters of these series find themselves transported too they will still remain as human. In this Tensura can be said to be somewhat unique as after death the main character of the series rather than being reincarnated as a human as previous series have done instead is reincarnated as a slime a creature that is seen to be the lowest of monsters. 

This concept of being reincarnated as a creature rather than a human being I thought was interesting and notable as while providing a much needed breath of fresh air into the genre it also provided an interesting opportunity to see a new fantasy world from the perspective of a human being that while being in the form of a monster has the knowledge that comes from the fact that he retains the memories that he had in his previous life. This combination of being a monster that has memories of subjects and matters that are visually unknown to the people of this new world was what can be said to be the main reason that drew me to the series as this knowledge of the mc allows him to not just create magic, organizations, towns and societies that are visually unknown to the world but also allow him to change and advance the various races that inhabit the land and dispel the sense of inherent distrust that exists between the various races by forging alliances between them and teaching them to respect and treat others fairly. This concept of trying to instill peace and order within the new world while making sure that each race is able to advance in tech level in uniform fashion, I felt was admirable as Rimuru’s actions not only changed himself and his allies but also the world around him as well. This sense of trying to change the world through diplomacy and teaching of new concepts to others in order to change the various races and their views on others ensured that this series was one of the best series of this season and I was glad that I decided to watch the series from start to finish. 

The overall story for Tensura takes place in a fantasy world that while having the standard races of humans, elves, dwarves, orcs, and goblins also have some unique exotic races like the ogre’s, direwolves, dragons, demons and Dryad’s that manage to fit surprisingly well into the fabric of the world’s races. Similar to fantasy realms of other series the various races of the world are broadly divided into regions in which they inhabit with towns and villagers being the most common forms of settlements. In this world, while peace was indeed in full reign it can be said that not every race got on with each other with harmony and indeed conflict would break out with the suddenness of a flare. The series overall story follows the life of Rimuru tempest a human being from the modern world who after suffering an untimely death in his home world was reincarnated as a slime in this new fantasy world. Rather than become an OP fighter slime as one would no doubt expected him to be Rimuru instead decides to take it slow and learn not just about this world but also get a feel for not just his newfound abilities but also of how the various races that inhabit the land view him and other races that they share this land with. This sense of taking things slow and learning not just about how each race lived in the world but also how their societies can be advanced and integrated with others so as to create a sense of unity within the world and help bring about peace can be said to be one of the main themes of the story and a theme that I felt took great advantage of not just the various types of races that existed within the world but also of the sense of democracy that came from Rimuru’s origin of being from a modern civilized democratic society like modern day Japan. 

Rimuru Tempest 

Rimuru Tempest portrayed by new seiyuu Miho Okasaki is one of the main characters of the series and is the main protagonist of the series. In his initial form, Rimuru was a mid age salaryman that lived-in modern-day Tokyo that while having everything that life could have offered him aspired what many people in his position would wish for which was to have some sort of excitement in his life that would spice things up for him. As a result of this despite the demands of his job and the stress that came from modern-day city life, he still maintained a cheerful and friendly personality that enabled him to get on well with others easily a trait that unfortunately proved to be his undoing and caused him to become an unfortunate casualty. After his reincarnation as a slime Rimuru’s personality changed dramatically. While still retaining his friendly and cheerful nature Rimuru also developed a sense of curiousness to explore this new world that he had been transported to and a desire to test out the various things that he had discovered. While being reincarnated as a slime would no doubt have taken an average human being some time to get accustomed to it can be seen that even as a slime, he had not lost any of the traits that he had in his previous life. While curious to explore Rimuru was also intelligent and fast thinking and wasn’t afraid of experimenting with his new-found powers and form now that the old-world rules did not apply to him. This can be seen well in his attempts to create new attacks and trying them without any kind of safeguard in place. This sense of wanting to test out ideas however wasn’t restricted to the testing of his powers however as Rimuru true to his nature was also willing to experiment with somewhat riskier ideas like creating completely new societies that have more than one race in them a plan that could easily have backfired had it not been Rimuru that was doing it. This shows that while developing a sense of curiosity Rimuru had also developed a sense of creativity as well and one that wasn’t restricted to one world’s knowledge and was willing to create a wide manner of things no matter how outlandish they may sound to the people of this new world with the town of unified races that Rimuru created over the course of the series to be a good example of this. 

Despite being transformed into a slime it can be seen that Rimuru has lost none of the friendly and easy-going nature that defined his original self. This can be seen well in the many first encounters that he has with the many races that inhabit this world. Despite commanding a number of impressive abilities that would have given most people pause it can be said that Rimuru is a calm and understanding person by nature that tries to ensure that all parties are relaxed before interaction begins. While this can be seen to be a weakness of sorts here it can also be said to be the opposite as Rimuru as a result of being freed from the stress and demands of modern day life now has all the time that he needs to analyze the various situations that he comes across in his journeys and come up with the best possible answers that can benefit all parties. While noted to be someone that preferred to deal with situations via diplomatic means it can be said that Rimuru was by no means someone that was afraid to counter those that were rude to him or his allies and was willing to verbally spar with those that he felt had offended him or his friends something that I felt matched well with his friendly and caring nature while also showing off his intelligence and his wittiness. A good example of this is shown in the initial exchanges between Rimuru’s town and the lizardmen. In the beginning of the series largely due to the inexperience that he had in dealing with new races, Rimuru was noted to have a certain lack of awareness on the feelings of others and the needs and desires of the races that he encounters over the course of the series. As a result, in the beginning while his orders were certainly followed accordingly it can be seen that not all races were ready to follow him. However as the series goes on and Rimuru got to see and understand the kinds of struggles, needs and desires that each race had within them Rimuru gradually began to realize that in this world each race was like an individual person that had their own unique beliefs, needs and desires and as a result gradually learned to be more considerate towards the feelings of those around him something that I felt fitted well with Rimuru’s role as a leader. 

Overall the character of Rimuru I felt was an interesting one and while death might have been a traumatic experience to some it can be said that the death of his initial body and the act of being reincarnated as a slime in a brand new world had the opposite effect as it instead gave him the freedom to for the first time in his life take things easy and slow and actually enjoy the new world in which he had been sent into. Seeing Rimuru manifest the infinite sense of curiosity and creativity that had been suppressed by the demands of modern day life and use it to try and change not just the races that he encounters in his travels but also the world as a whole as well in an effort to create a peaceful society I thought was an interesting development and direction for his character as while for the most part it derived from his desire to live an easy life in this new world it also derived from both the fact that he was from a modern democratic society where peace was second nature. This sense of combining character development and direction with the personal beliefs and desires that one has learned from hard-earned life experience I thought was interesting as it added a more personal feel to the development of Rimuru while also matching well with the series overall theme of advancing society. 

Shizue 

Shizue Izawa portrayed by Yumiri Hanamori of Yuru Camp fame is one of the main supporting characters within the series and is one of Rimuru’s allies within the series. In her initial appearances Shizue who is more commonly known as the masked swordswoman on account of both her skills as a swordswoman and the mask that she wore when on duty was seen to be a quiet, calm and composed young woman who despite her fame was kind, caring and polite to all that she met in her journey. While a quiet and composed person by nature Shizue was also someone that was shown to be curious about matters and subjects that she had not seen before which is best shown in her reaction at seeing races that would otherwise have been hostile to her instead show her kindness and care. At the same time despite her fame as a famed swordswoman Shizue was someone that was noted to prefer observing and understanding new situations before making a decision rather than simply drawing her sword and fall back on standard protocols of eliminating races on the off chance that they are hostile something that I felt put her in good stead and ensured that she managed to bond well with not just the members of Rimuru’s future town but also Rimuru himself. 

While a kind and caring person by nature and one that would not hesitate to use her powers to protect her friends and comrades from harm from the onset it can be seen that Shizue was someone that preferred to keep her true emotions and feelings hidden behind her mask. As the series goes on it can be seen that Shizue’s mask rather than merely keeping her identity a secret from those that she doesn’t trust also serves as a sort of sanctuary of sorts for her as it is only within the mask that Shizue is able to reveal her true feelings. Unlike the kind and confident personality that she shows on the surface it can be seen that beneath her mask Shizue is someone that’s emotionally fragile and lonely that stems from not just her role and position as a famous swordswoman but also from the many regrets that had formed within her as a result of the many discoveries that she has made regarding not just her own powers but also that of her charges as well. As a result of this it can be seen that in addition to being emotionally fragile and lonely Shizue also possesses a deep fear that perhaps one day if she’s not focused that her powers would not only go berserk but also injure those that she was supposed to be protecting. As a result of these fears, it’s perhaps unsurprising that Shizue would desire to find and befriend people that she can share her secret pain and grief with but alas for her she was not successful until she encountered Rimuru. Though the interactions that Shizue had with Rimuru were relatively short ones it can be seen that in her last days Shizue thoroughly enjoyed spending her time with Rimuru as for the first time in her long life she was able to reveal to someone that she trusted all of the pain and regrets that she had been holding beneath her mask for so long and the one wish that she despite her power was unable to fulfill that she hoped that Rimuru her first confidant would be able to in her place. 

The character of Shizue I felt was an interesting one as the contrast between her position and role as a powerful swordswoman that was widely seen by many as a powerful but kind, steadfast and dependable fighter that can face down the fiercest of enemies with icy calmness and her hidden side of a lonely, insecure and emotionally fragile young woman that longed to find someone that she could pour her heart out to being especially so. In a way despite the way that society views her it can be seen that Shizue was somewhat of a tragic figure as she was not only brought to this world against her will but also forced to take up the role that she was ill-suited for. While persevering in her duties as a valued member of society in an effort to both protect the innocent but also find a way back home Shizue much to her horror found that not only will her control of her powers start to decrease as she ages but that her valued charges would also start to enter the final roads of their lives as well. This combination of a professional struggle and the hidden personal struggle that she tries hard to conceal with from friends in an effort to not worry them I thought was well done and conceived as it added a more emotional element to her character’s struggles and made her relationship with Rimuru that much more special. 

Shion 

Shion portrayed by veteran seiyuu Mao Ichimichi of Aoki Hagane No Arpeggio and Digimon adventure Tri fame is one of the main supporting characters of the series and is one of Rimuru’s main allies within the series. A member of the Ogre race and one of the survivors of that village Shion in her initial appearances was seen to be a proud, confident, stubborn and a somewhat fiery person by nature that preferred to strike first rather than use diplomacy when meeting new races.  This last trait is shown well in the first encounter that she and her party had with Rimuru and his village. However, despite her tendency to act first Shion is also someone that can be said to have a strong sense of honor and willing to respect those that are able to show their resolve even when they are backed into a corner which I felt goes well with her spirit as a warrior. In line with this Shion is someone that isn’t afraid of facing down strong foes on the field even if the said foe has proven to be much more powerful that she is. 

After becoming a member of the village and after being uplifted by Rimuru Shion’s personality gradually starts to change. While still retaining her strong loyalty to her fellow ogre’s and to the village that acted as their homeland Shion like the rest of the ogre’s also developed a strong loyalty to both Rimuru and the town that he had created due to the fact that he not only gave them a new location in which they can call home but also allow them to get revenge on the orc lord that was responsible for the destruction of their village. However, unlike the rest of the ogre’s it can be said that with Shion’s loyalty comes an intense romantic interest in Rimuru which while excessive at times often provides a good deal of comic relief for her character with notable examples being how bad she is at cooking. As a result of this dual amount of affection and loyalty that Shion has for her lord and the village it can be seen quite clearly that she’s very proud of Rimuru and of the notable alliance that he had formed with the various races that inhabit it and as such she will not tolerate any type of slander of either. 

Shuna 

Shuna portrayed by veteran seiyuu Sayaka Senbongi of Girlish Number and Clockwork Planet fame is one of the main supporting characters of the series and is one Rimuru’s main allies within the series. A member of the ogre race and one of the survivors of that village Shuna is also Benimaru’s younger sister and a true princess of that race. From her initial appearance Shuna was seen to be a quiet, perceptive and intelligent person by nature that unlike her brother Benimaru and her friend Shion was seen to understand the value of diplomacy and the need to be cautious and rational when dealing with new races and situations. While a quiet person by nature Shuna was also noted to possess a degree of bravery that one would hardly expect from a quiet girl like her and she was willing to go to great lengths to ascertain and confirm a theory that she had discovered. This is shown well during the first encounter between Rimuru and the members of the Ogre’s of which she was a part off when she stepped in to defuse the quickly escalating situation that transpired between the two parties. 

After joining the village and being uplifted Shuna like the rest of the ogre’s gradually began to change in personality. While still retaining her trademarked quiet and calm nature Shuna also began to develop a desire to be useful to her new lord and to be useful enough to be relied upon by giving her a degree of responsibility something that I felt was not just cute but also showed her desire to be of better use to her village and to her new allies. While certainly weaker than her fellow ogre’s in frontline combat Shuna however more than made up for it with the vast knowledge that she had in medicine and in this, it can be seen is where she truly shines. While clearly intelligent Shuna true to her personality did not show any degree of arrogance in her actions and indeed she was willing to not just learn about different cultures but also techniques that have been created by other races which does well in showing her hardworking and earnest nature. Like Shion Shuna too is shown to have a great deal of affection for Rimuru but unlike Shion who is more open with her feelings Shuna’s feelings towards her lords tend to be more subtle. Though not often seen the rivalry between the two friends over their affections for Rimuru are always amusing to watch and add a sense of hilarity to the scenes in which they take place. 

Millim 

Millim portrayed by veteran seiyuu Rina Hidaka of Sword Art Online and Ryuuou no Oshigoto fame is one of the main supporting characters within the series and is one of Rimuru’s main allies within the series. A young human female and also one of the oldest of the demon lords that currently inhabit the world to which Rimuru calls home Millim from her initial appearance is seen to be a positive, curious and earnest young lady that approached each new situation with both determination and a somewhat childish desire to be surprised. Unlike the more traditional image that can be inferred from that of a demon lord Millim rather than being a brooding, dark and cynical person who enjoys making mortals dance to their tune is quite the opposite in that she while disliking the various rules and agreements that are in place within the world is instead someone that can be said to be somewhat of a free spirit that approaches each day with cheerfulness and a desire to try out new food and experiences and meet new surprises aspects that are more in line with that a average teenage girl than that of a demon lord. However, this schoolgirl side of her will vanish once Milim gets serious for this is when she shows off the demon lord side of her that’s she known for far across the land. 

In contrast to Millim’s default schoolgirl self which is kind, caring and protective of her friends and allies Millim’s demon lord self can be said to be the total opposite. In this form to which she will adapt when things get serious Millim’s kind and caring personality is instead replaced by that of arrogance and confidence in her abilities as a demon lord and unlike in her alternate self she will not hesitate to strike the enemy before they can prepare for her. While hitting hard and fast with her attacks it can also be seen that Millim also takes great care to observe her enemy and use the knowledge that she gained in centuries of learning magic and actual combat to deal with the enemy’s attacks while making sure that her own are as effective as possible showing that while she may look relatively young for her role that Millim’s combat skills are indeed genuine. This is shown well within the first fight between Rimuru and Millim in which she was consistently able to get the upper hand in that fight despite Rimuru’s attempt to counter her. Though Millim’s demon lord form is indeed powerful its interesting to note that even in this form Millim’s curiosity to experience new things are still present to some degree and can easily be exploited to end things peacefully as shown in the manner of how Rimuru ended the fight that he had with her. In this, it can be seen that while Millim herself is a fearsome combatant that can match Rimuru quite easily in terms of combat strength that she’s a child at heart that can easily be distracted when presented with things that she hasn’t seen before. 

The character of Millim I felt was an interesting one with the contrast between her two forms and with them their respective personalities being especially so. While the image that most people would have upon the mention of the term demon lord would no doubt be some scheming  demon that sits on a throne somewhere working on his next big plan of conquest Millim is a bit of an exception to this rule as if one did not know her personally one would no doubt think that she was just your average teenage girl that was enjoying the youth that all girls would go through before adulthood. Indeed, it is this view that truly makes her stand out for unlike other demon lords that are shown in the series Milim while a genuine demon lord with combat abilities that are equal to or above that of Rimuru rather than treat others with arrogance and cruelty instead treats all that she encounters with respect, politeness and cheerfulness that add a degree of freshness to her character. More than anything seeing Millim gradually learn about society and seeing how she befriends and bonds with the members of the village while enjoying all of the benefits that comes from living with those that she gradually learns to care about was an interesting experience for both us the viewer and for Millim herself as well. This development is seen especially well when Millim sees her friends and allies getting hurt by outsiders as it is here where we can truly see Millim’s strong desire to protect them by unleashing her demon form. Seeing Millim not just learn about what a society is like but also see the value of friendship and bonds that can be found there I felt was interesting and highlighted just how much Millim has grown as a character. Seeing her switch between forms so readily in order to protect those that she considers dear to her was also endearing as well. 

AMV 
In terms of animation, I thought that the various locations and settings that were featured within the series were both well thought out and designed and featured quite a strong variety of terrain that matched well with the races that called those locations their homes. Notable examples of this included the goblin village, the dwarven homeland of Dwargon and the Freedom academy that housed the students that Shizue was trying to save. Of these locations the Goblin village which later transforms into a city that serves as the capital of Rimuru’s Jura Tempest Federation is undoubtedly  my favorite due to the fact that the city was essentially built from the ground up using both the ideas that Rimuru had from his former home and also because of how it symbolized the core beliefs of his dream which was to build a city that housed citizens of all races that can live alongside each other without fear of tension and disagreements that could escalate into conflict. 

In terms of character design, I felt that the series featured quite the large variety of both races and creatures within its overall story. Each of the races within the series whether it was the beasts that Rimuru and co had to fight within the series or the individuals of each race I thought was very well designed and detailed. While the standard conventions of how humans, elves and dwarves looked were established long ago I thought that the series did well in showing the more exotic races that weren’t featured in conventional work with the series depiction of the ogre’s, Dryads and goblins being especially well done. The series depiction of Orcs as pigs I felt was an interesting take on how the race looked. In terms of combat animation, I thought that the series featured some pretty impressive fights that while usually short were well thought out and made great use of both terrain features and simple but creative use of tactics and Rimuru’s own abilities. Notable fights within the series that I enjoyed seeing was the battle between the goblins and the direwolves, the battle to defend the village from Ifrit, the battle against the Orc Lord and the battle against demon lord Millim. While Rimuru is the main character within the series I was also thankful in that the various races that he had uplifted with the naming were also given the chance to show off their improved stats within the series as well with the Kijin in particular being able to make a satisfying bang in their combat debut.  

In terms of music, the series made use of two opening themes which was Nameless Story and Meguru Mono that was sung by Takuma Terashima and Three ending themes which were Nameless story that was sung by Takuma Terashima, Another colony that was sung by TRUE and Little soldier that was sung by veteran seiyuu singer Azusa Tadokoro. All of these songs I felt were catchy ones with Meguru Mono, Another Colony and Little Soldier being my favorites. Of the series OST, I felt that it did a great job of dividing its time between peaceful and calming music for scenes that showed the development of characters and infrastructure and more dramatic music for the combat scenes. At the same time, I also felt that the Opening and ending themes of the series was used well to both give us a look at characters that have yet to appear within the series and at the same time show the development of said characters and the town as the series progresses. While certainly subtle I felt that this aspect was used well to show not just how many friends and allies Rimuru has made over the course of the series but also in how much he changed the world as well. 

In terms of voice acting I felt that the series main voice cast all did an excellent job at portraying their assigned characters whether they were main ones or support ones. In particular I feel that Miho Okasaki, Yumiri Hanamori, Mao Ichimichi, Sayaka Senbongi and Rina Hidaka deserve special praise as I felt that they all did an excellent job in portraying the characters of Rimuru, Shizue, Shion, Shuna and Millim respectively. Miho Okasaki in particular really impressed me with her portrayal of Rimuru and I hope that the experience that she had gained in portraying Rimuru would help greatly in allowing her to develop her skills as a seiyuu and make a career within the seiyuu industry. In addition, while I didn’t cover them within this review, I also thought that Makoto Furukawa, Asuna Tomari, Chikahiro Kobayashi and Rie Tanaka all did an excellent job at portraying the characters of Benimaru, Gobuta, Ranga and Treyni respectively. 

Overall conclusion 

Overall Tensura was an anime that I really enjoyed watching and I have to say it’s definitely one of this season’s best animes. Its main strong points in my opinion is its excellent and unique premise, strong story, well designed and developed characters, excellent voice acting, its strong emphasis on real-world issues like nation building and integrating different races into one society and its emphasis on changing the world through society and tech advancement rather than through military means. At the same time, I also thought that the series did a great job at skillfully blending the genres of comedy, action and fantasy together something that can be said to be inherently tricky within an anime. 

The overall premise of Tensura which is the death and reincarnation of a human being from the modern world to a parallel is nothing really new since it serves as the main form of transportation for the Isekai genre. However, while the form that they would reincarnate into can vary substantially being reincarnated as a slime which is a monster that is widely considered to be the lowest on monsters has to be the most unique form I ever seen. While being reincarnated as a slime instead of a normal human being that can make much more effective usage of his modern-day education and memories can be seen as a disadvantage as after all very few people take slimes seriously the form of a slime can also provide some unique advantages that the larger forms lack such as a unique perspective on how monsters behave and operate in the world, deception and misdirection and a less threatening appearance the last point being especially useful for Rimuru given his focus on diplomatic means to resolve crisis. All in all I felt that the form of a slime that Rimuru took after being reincarnated rather than give him a host of disadvantages that many would have expected actually provided a great deal of unique advantages that allowed him to not just overcome the many different trials that comes from his adventures but at the same time act as a safety net due to a slime’s unique body structure. More than anything I felt that being a slime rather than say a human being actually had a hand in contributing to Rimuru’s success in convincing the various races to work together with him. 

The overall story for the series I felt was one of the series main strong points and was one that I really enjoyed. Typical Isekai stories tend to focus on a hero that after being reincarnated in the new world would one day receive a quest in which they must fulfill a difficult quest that would see them face anything from dragons to demons while protecting humans from the predations of the evil demi humans and monsters that inhabit the dark places. However, what if this story is replaced by one where the main focus rather than focusing on dealing out death to anything that’s not human instead is replaced by one where the main focus is on learning about the various races that inhabit the land, uniting them and advancing their tech level in order to instill changes to not just their living conditions but also create an ability to evolve their society so that they can be equal to their surrounding countries and no longer be seen as a mere monsters. It is this focus on learning, expanding and advancing of the various races that Rimuru encounters over the course of his journey that can be said to be the true joy of this anime as we get to see Rimuru not just overturn the concept that all monsters were threats to humans by not just giving them personality but also their unique culture, taste’s, likes and dislikes aspects that many would argue that only humans would have. Seeing Rimuru recognize this by treating them not as beasts but as humans by giving them names and working with them to forge bonds with others and make friends and not enemies that culminated  in the creation of not just the town of Tempest but also of the larger Jura Tempest Federation I felt was immensely satisfying as more than anything it represented a great change within the series not just to the various non-human races but also to the many human nations as well. 

Overall Tensura was an anime series that I really enjoyed, and it is undoubtedly one of the seasons best animes on account of its unique premise, strong story, excellent voice cast, its skillful use of real-world issues that aren’t usually seen within anime and its emphasis on diplomacy rather than on physical might. As a final score, I would say that Tensura easily deserves a score of 9/10. While the series started strong I felt that the story arcs near the end while introducing some interesting new characters didn’t expand them enough to make them compelling.

Saying the iseaki genre has overstayed its welcome in recent years is an understatement.  Once upon a time, the isekai used to be a respective genre for the anime medium. Many of isekai anime that came out before 2016 range from good to great. Some of my favourites being Escaflowne, Fushigi Yuugi and El Hazard. Unfortunately ever since Konosuba and Re:Zero the isekai genre has rapidly gone downhill in terms of quality. Not only various isekai anime since Re:Zero were fundamentally bad in every way, but they take such a mockery of the genre. Instead of exploring fascinating worlds, stories and characters we get horrendous deretropes, sick waifu pandering, beta husk main leads, recycled and shameless world-building.

It doesn't help that many of the authors behind are clearly inexperienced writers with no passion for telling a story and only doing so for the money. This is not to say that every isekai anime post Re: Zero was bad in fact there was a couple of isekai anime that I liked and That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime is one of them.

A show I had no exceptions manages to be the best modern isekai I have seen period.

The plot setup is what you expect from this genre. The protagonist gets killed by an accident in the real world. The protagonist gets sent to a fantasy world, the protagonist has to adapt to the new surroundings you get the drill. 
Despite the typical isekai set Slime actually manages to do some things partiality different.
For one, our protagonist is a middle-aged man instead of another teenager. This aspect alone really made Rimuru Tempest stand out of them as he's going to be much more mature and layback protagonist for the viewer to relate to.

One thing that I appreciated is how self-aware it is. The show loves makes fun of cliches and tropes for the fantasy/isekai genre for example in one episode Rimuru comments on the glowing angry red-eye cliche. (Goblin Slayer and Berserk 2017) I found it so humorous that I could not stop laughing. Speaking of comedy, the comedy in Slime is also very good.
It has a great sense of humour from start to finish, many of the jokes seemed to land perfectly thanks to comedic timing and structure and the show is generally funny.
The show is, for the most part, is well-paced never dragged or rushed.

The writing least for the first half is one point with very little hiccups. My favourite arc in the show was the Shizu arc. Not only that arc was amazingly well written from beginning to end but this was the arc that made me love Rimuru. I already said he was different from other isekai protagonists but this was the arc that demonstrated it the most, especially with he's 'swell written dialogue.

If there's was one thing that Slime has over other isekai anime is the amazing attention to detail with its world-building. The world-building for Slime is outstanding because not only the series was capable of making the world feel alive but the attention to detail from the monster races, lore and various locations were stunning. Everything I said so far ties up to the main theme of Slime which is cooperation. We see characters from various races and backgrounds come to work together to build the ultimate monster village, so they can live in peace.

Sadly this series is not perfect. For one, despite the fascinating simple nature, I feel the show barely had stakes when it comes to conflict. Many of the conflicts that happen in this season were solved with ease due to overpowered Rimuru and his pals were. It may not be as bad compare other isekai anime it doesn't make it less jarring knowing that Rimuru and his pals would quickly solve any conflict with little to no struggle.

Hopefully, this problem will be fixed in season 2.

The second half is notably weaker than the first half. Not only the show became mostly directionless, but the writing started to be quite problematic at times. It was a shocking cliche overall.

The dialogue became less charming and the final arc of the season wasn't all that interesting. It's such a shame that this season ended on a weak note yes it second half had some great moments but these moments didn't save the second half from being inferior then again I've seen worse isekai second half *Cough Shield Hero, Re:Zero and Konosuba*.

Now we have the characters which are surprisingly pretty great. They may not be the best-written cast in the world or anything but they are still a likeable and fun bunch of characters that you can grow attached to in some way.

At first glance, Rimuru Tempest may be another self insert isekai protagonist with no personality and quirks but as the series progress you will start how unique and different Rimuri is compared to any other isekai protagonist and that is why he is mature. Before this series, all isekai protagonists were either goofy, loud and over the top and that trend got tiring over time as they were a bunch of isekai anime, especially in recent memory just featured a generic teenage protagonist. Besides those differences, I really like Rimuru as a protagonist.

I found him to be very smart. I really liked his determination of making his own town and it was very likeable for beginning to end despite him being overpowered then again I blame the writing rather than the character itself.

The supporting characters are also very good.
Each of the supporting characters is unique in terms of characterisation and personality.
I also liked how they developed alongside the plot, meaning they are not just mindless minions that follow Rimuru for the sake of it. They all follow Rimuru's because of various reasons.
My favourite supporting characters were Milim, Souei, Shion, Benimaru, and Shizue.

Studio 8bit is a pretty niche studio when it comes to anime as they haven't made anything that is the worth of apart from numerous throwaway animes. So, I expected this series to have mediocre visuals, but the animation staff of Slime proved me wrong.
The character’s designs were well drawn especially Rimuru’s human form. The background scenery is beautiful to look at, and it's filled with colour.
The animation is smooth, crisp, well animated and consistent. It didn't rely on still frames nor recycled animation.

The soundtrack was done by Elements Garden, the same people that produced the soundtrack for Uta no Prince Sama and Symphogear. Personally, I thought the soundtrack was pretty good for an isekai. The soundtrack features a good score of adventurous, upbeat, 8bit and fantasy tracks that perfectly captures the tone of the series.
The opening themes for Slime are absolutely fantastic. Both of them give that peaceful and lack back vibe of the series. My favourite out of the two is the 2nd opening Meguru Mono.

Unfortunately, I cannot say the same thing for the ending themes as they were forgettable. They weren't bad ending themes by any means but they didn't resonate with me compared to opening themes.
The English dub done by Funimation is one of the best dubs I heard in a long while. It's very well acted, the audio quality was clean and all the English actors did a great job with the roles that they were given.

The best performance in the dub is hands down Brittney Karbowski. She did a magnificent job voicing the quirky and laid back Rimuru Tempest.

Despite its issues with the second half as well as the lack of stakes, I had a great time with Slime.
It may not be winning any writing awards anytime soon but it won the best isekai series award due to its amazing world-building, charming characters. Strong English dub, beautiful production values and a great soundtrack.
With that said I hope future authors will follow on Slime's footsteps because I want to see a good isekai anime that will be on par or even surpass Slime. I don't want to see another isekai anime that prioritizes waifus over storytelling nor a half-fast isekai anime that has no passion or soul.

Take some time and put some effort, that's all I task.

Follow the Slime, avoid the Smartphone.

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken may be one of the most decent isekai recently released… But please, can we stop pretending this serie is perfect? The premise of this serie is pretty much the same as other isekais: MC dies and gets transported to a fantasy/RPG game world, but in this case he reincarnates as a slime. Slimes are well recognized to be the most basic and weak creatures in fantasy worlds, but sometimes they have some traits like broken skills, elemental resistances or ailments inmunity, that may make them powerful creatures which shouldn’t be underestimated (Dragon Quest is a well-known example). Slimes in this worldare pretty much like that, but since they don't have intellect enough they are not considered as a threat. Here is when our MC appears. MC, subsequently named Rimuru Tempest, wakes up in a cave in this amorphous and gummy body, after a quick review he is informed about his condition by a kind of inner voice just called Daikenja (think of her like those pop ups tutorials in videogames) and without much else to do, Rimuru starts to explore the cave.


Now talking about the serie in general, one of the best aspects about TenSura is the worldbuilding. Yes, this isekai actually HAS worldbuilding. The serie basically explains everything, the current situation, the world and its creatures, terminology, skills, magic effects, you name it. Of course this means there is a lot of exposition, sometimes too much (like in the first chapter), but it is presented in straightforward and concise sentences instead of walls of texts, so it doesn't end up being overwhelming. Most of this exposition comes from Daikenja to Rimuru and hence the viewer, but sometimes Rimuru himself explains the situation. 


Slimes have an unique skill called Predator that allows them to absorb, keep and analyze materials and enemies, so Rimuru spends like a month in the cave farming materials and gaining experience, stats and skills, becoming very powerful in the process. Soon he meets a sealed dragon named Veldora, and after a cringe but funny conversation, Veldora helps him to see, gives him a name and they become friends. Rimuru is also told more about the world and how he is not the only person transported from another world. That’s how, after absorbing Veldora in order to eliminate the seal, Rimuru leaves the cave with a new objective: to find more people from his world.


Now Rimuru and the viewer are facing a new world, a… pretty common fantasy world. The serie is honest and doesn’t hesitate to show a normal and lighthearted fantasy enviroment with its typical creatures like goblins, dwarfs, orcs and of course humans. Helped with a decent palette of colors and nice backgrounds, this world feels alive and charming. TenSura is self-conscious about what it’s showing, without pretensions of being what it’s not, the plot is not supposed to be taken so seriously so you can get in the mood pretty easily.


From this point the plot can be summarized in Rimuru getting involved in some races’ problems and helping them solving those problems, either by meritocracy or by force, and in the end making these creatures his subordinates and building a big “family”. Pacing is another positive point, every arc lasts enough to introduce new characters and main problem, it handles to explain all the important information and resolves the situation without rushing or lengthening. 


Even so, there is a big issue this series has: Rimuru gets so OP that he gets basically everything with little to no effort at all, even when the serie justifies everything. Predator and Daikenja are very broken tools, not only Rimuru can use all the skills he absorbs to beat all enemies he faces with ease, not only he can stock almost infinite materials and use them without caution when it’s necessary, but he also gets convenient explanations of what he doesn’t know via Daikenja. All of this breaks the tension and makes the serie predictable. 


But major issues around the serie are not just because of Rimuru’s powers, it’s the way the plot is too convenient to him that it puts the perfect situation so that Rimuru can solve it very easily. Just look at the first chapters, for example: He CONVENIENTLY appears in a place full of materials and monsters he CONVENIENTLY can absorb with his OP skill, then he CONVENIENTLY meets a powerful dragon that helps him to escape, and after that he CONVENIENTLY finds a goblin village with a problem he can easily solve because of his absorbed skills. Now he has a village of goblins and wolves which revere him, but he needs blacksmiths so he goes to a city to get them, he CONVENIENTLY meets the best blacksmith dwarfs in the city which have a big problem that Rimuru can CONVENIENTLY solve by just absorb a sword, analyze it and make a lot of copies with all the materials he CONVENIENTLY kept from the cave, so now the dwarfs are happy to revere him… Again, the serie at least explains the basics about every individual situation so it’s possible to justify them (like how he was able to make sword copies because he had enough saved materials), this is enough to put TenSura above others of the genre, but it’s not enough justification for all the plot conveniences surrounding Rimuru. This is just a mediocre writting.


This is a big problem especially for action moments because no matter how powerful the enemy is, you know Rimuru and his gang can easily get rid of it without much complication. You know the good guys are going to win against the bad guys, like a shounen, but unlike shounen or actions series in general, here tensión is non-existent because how OP good guys are. Actions scenes are not always supposed to be good because of the sometimes obvious outcome, but the scene by itself, to see how good guys handle to beat bad guys against all the problems they might go through (and even they may lose). Here nothing of that happens, making actions scenes pretty dull and uninterested in the long run.


Since there’s an overall lighthearted mood around, there are comedy moments too, but comedy is a pretty weak aspect of the serie. Most comedic scenes are summarized in dull boke-tsukkomi gags and plain jokes using cliches LNs are plagued of, making comedy in general feel very forced and fail to be funny. This serie is also overwhelmingly cliche, almost every trope of the manual can be found here: lolis, onee-sans, fanservice, bishounens, bouncing boobs, harem elements, and going through typical situations like OP characters wrecking everyone and everything easily, bullying the ineptest guy, harem chicks arguing each other, mortal cooking, onsen, etc. All of those issues aren’t bad per se, but in this case they are just flatly placed onscreen with no subtlety and with the vague intention of being funny. Tropes that have been heavily used and are no longer funny. Even when there are scenes with gags, situations or jokes that at least can make you smile, in regards of purely comedic scenes there’s not creativity, there’s not enough wit to make a genuinely funny scene, just the same well-known cliches reused. 


Characters are by far the weakest part of the serie. Rimuru as a character is just ok, at least he has personality unlike other Light Novels MCs, but it’s a pretty basic one. That’s not entirely bad because it fits with the lighthearted mood the serie has and makes Rimuru easy to relate with. Actually the main issue with that is the lack of any depth, making the character plain, and for a MC this is bad because it might make the viewer get bored or lose interest, also limits a lot the character’s potential. It doesn’t have to be a big depth, but something that says Rimuru is more than just your average MC. Also, it’s really hard to believe how someone that basic and limited apparently has so much charm as the serie puts it; just some kind words and a demostration of his powers are enough to convince people that Rimuru “is such a very nice and reliable slime” and instantly they are willing to be part of his family and revere him… That’s the kind of things that make Rimuru look more like your typical Gary Stu light novel MC.


Even all said before, Rimuru is maybe the best character in the serie, but that’s because the rest of the cast are just stereotypical characters who barely have personality (and some of them mainly for “comedy” purposes). Actually there are pretty interesting characters there, but the main problem is that they revere Rimuru so much that they lose any hint of characterization or development they might have: 

-Ok, goblins and wolves were just simple monsters so initially they didn’t need characterization at all, but after they evolved some of them were shown with actual personality, but they just kept there as background characters revering Rimuru, with no evolution or something that would make viewer get interesed on them as individual characters, like Gobuta, Rigur or Rigurd. This may also apply to Kaijin or Gabiru who had characterization before becoming Rimuru’s subordinate. 

-Ranga actually started with personality, doubts about his father and former leader, but after this latter were defeated and killed by Rimuru he just… accepted him, and became one of his most loyal subordinates, losing basically any trace of personality. I mean, for real? He saw how his father was brutally killed in front of him and he didn’t get mad, sad or decided to take the leadership, he just forgot everything and became so affective with his new leader in a way you can’t believe it. You may blame the fear of see how someone that strong easily kills his leader as a reason to surrender to him, and in fact it is a reasonable justification to that, but not to become so affective and losing any personality in order to be just a guardian dog. 

-Onis are where the serie wasted a lot of potential. When I said that there were pretty interesting characters I was referring mostly to them. They are more than simple monsters unlike goblins or wolves, each one of them have different personalities that were kept after becoming Rimuru’s subordinates, and actually they had a goal before that, since they lost their village. So… what happened after they reached their goal and decided to stay as Rimuru’s subordinates? Were their personalities and pasts developed or even exploited? Of course not! Well, they are treated as more than just NPCs unlike goblins and wolves, but most of their interventions are very shallow, like if they weren’t so important as characters. We have the proud leader, the wise old man, the mysterious silent man and the big quiet one just fulfiling those roles, some “comedic” moment and nothing more. The two girls are worse, they are just waifu baits with opposite personalities that the serie uses for the classic “harem chicks arguing about MC attention”, even worse, they are kind of like Ranga when they suddenly became so affective towards Rimuru that you can’t believe it, losing any posibility of individual characterization thanks to that extreme loyality.

-Millim is the loli factor in this equation and your typical “ridiculously powerful but kawaii brainless chick” who allied with Rimuru because plot said so (really, she didn’t have a reason at all) and we need another waifu bait for the weebs. Nothing more worth mentioning.

-You may have noticed I haven’t talked about Shizu yet even when she’s supposed to be important for the main plot, that’s because her characterization was so shallowly shown she can’t even count as proper character, and it’s the main proof this serie is terrible in characterization. This girl is, like Rimuru, another person invoked from his world, and when they met she established their situation is not so uncommon, potentially making this a pillar for the main plot and for Rimuru and Shizu’s development and relation. So what the serie did after that? Instead of giving Shizu an important role and time to develop her, the serie just showed her cruel past when she arrived with excesive victimization, then she “unleashed” her power CONVENIENTLY after meet Rimuru so he could “help her” absorbing her power (becoming more OP) finishing her life in the process and then giving him her “last will” by allowing Rimuru to absorb her body and appearance… All in an attempt to create cheap drama around Shizu, trying to make the viewer empathize with her but in the wrong way because at the end there’s nothing important left to bond with, all that just makes Shizu more a plot device than a proper character. That was actually one of the worst arcs of the show, and it evidences that the serie is bad at dealing with dramas and serious issues, which also affects narrative of those serious arcs. 

-Veldora is in a similar situation. After he got absorbed by Rimuru he just stopped existing as a character and more as a plot device, because his absence just worked as a reason to move the plot.

Of course the serie can’t be expected to develop all characters since there are a lot, but at least it should pick the most important ones and give them some depth (especially for story purposes) instead of just treat them like walking tropes.


Then we get to the final arc, which it’s about the other invoked people Shizu talked about, and which I said it might be a pillar for the main plot and for Rimuru’s characterization, so it’s supposed to be a pretty important arc… And what did we get? This arc sums up basically everything that is wrong with this anime: Rimuru’s skills and OPness killing any tensión (now he can assemble spirits too? Are you kidding me?), wasted characters with tiny to no characterization (none of the supposedly important kids’ personalities or pasts were explored, they were just mere plot devices), A LOT of plot conveniences (in just one chapter Rimuru got kids’ respect by killing a dragon that CONVENIENTLY appeared from nowhere, that was seen CONVENIENTLY by a merchant that accepted to do business with Rimuru, and one of his girls CONVENIENTLY knew where Spirit Queen can be found) and otaku pandering. On top of that, a new problem the serie hadn’t faced up to this point: the pacing was very rushed (several weeks of bonding between Rimuru and the kids passed in just a few minutes, for example), making the plot even more convenient than the rest of the serie, and the introduced characters were forgettable. This arc makes clear that this serie isn’t going to improve in any way. It’s a shame.


With everything said above, I just can ask: why is this serie, full of those issues commonly criticized in most LN adaptations, getting a free pass? Why is getting too much praise and high scores even when it falls under the same tropes that mediocre and much more criticized LNs also fall?


But please don’t get me wrong, with all its ups and downs TenSura is a decent serie I pretty enjoyed. But the serie is far from being perfect, and I thought it would be good bringing some criticism to the table pointing out all the good and bad things the serie did instead of just say shallow claims like “it’s good because I liked it and characters made me laugh” or “this is utter crap because Rimuru is so OP and nothing happens”. So yeah, the reason this serie stands out as one of the most decent isekais recently released is more because most of those isekais are pretty bad rather than by its own merits. But hey! It actually HAS merits.


tl;dr: Interesting premise, charming mood and decent worldbuilding, but terrible characters and bad handling of serious issues when tries to be more ambitious. This serie is fine but it’s not a masterpiece or even something close. Please stop overrating and overhyping things, THAT is the real cancer of the community.

Summary: That Time I Got Reincarnated As A Slime is, overall, a fun and undemanding series that is more concerned with being "enjoyable" than being "good". This sounds like a backhanded compliment, but I consider it a good thing. There's a lot of things you can complain about with this series when you really get into it, but its rarely boring and if you're into this sort of fantasy show, you'll almost certainly have a good time watching it even in spite of those. Note: Negatives section contains spoilers for Shizu and her character arc. Positives: + It's fun. Vague, I know, but it's avery entertaining show even though it's fairly predictable.  The episodes move fast and you often want to start the next one right away.

+ The action is cool.  In particular, Rimuru's ability to absorb, copy and recombine different kinds of magic leads to all sorts of creative uses of their powers.

+ Relaxing vibe.  It's not like there's no drama in this series, and it does get serious and engage with heavier themes at some points, but overall it's a show about good people getting along with each other.  The threats to Rimuru and his town of monsters are rarely serious, people are generally honest and straightforward, and characters often decide that coming to a mutual understanding is better than fighting.  It's a bit naive in its worldview, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing.  This is supposed to be a fantasy after all, so I think it's fine to have a world where everyone is basically decent, as opposed to the usual tropes about life in those worlds being brutal and difficult.

Negatives:

- Side characters are an issue.  There are a few good ones, Shion being the best as far as I'm concerned, but overall they lack impact and there are too many of them.  It feels like there was a dictate that at least one new side character has to be added in every episode.  The ones that already exist get cycled out and ignored as new ones are introduced, so none of them have time to really develop a presence.  This is fixed a little bit in the 2nd half of the season, but remains an issue throughout.

- Not enough Shizu.  Shizu is made to be the emotional core of the show, as Rimuru absorbs her body on her deathbed to receive a human form and inherits her dying wishes and regrets.  This is a good idea in theory, and could have been very powerful, but it feels wasted by the fact that Shizu was only around for a few episodes and had only the most superficial relationship with Rimuru before her death, not even knowing their name until her last moments.  If she had been around longer and had been able to bond with the other characters, her arc would have been far more impactful and better.  It feels like it was too rushed given her importance to the story.

- Milim.  Annoying demon loli included as blatant fanservice for creepy masturbators who just want to stare at her mostly bare ass.  It's kind of embarrassing how direct they are about her having no value to the series beyond this.  This is exactly the sort of thing that gives anime and its fans a bad reputation in mainstream society.

- In general, the serious parts of the series are not that strong.  I get that a series like this can't be 100% fluff, but any time things get serious, it feels like it's operating outside its comfort zone and doesn't really handle it that well.  It's hard to know how to react to a show that's mostly lighthearted suddenly bringing up things like slavery and children with terminal illnesses.

With a plethora of Isekai anime persistently flooding the medium every season, one can't help but grow weary and averse to the genre as a whole. Admittedly, "That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime" sounds like a show with a nebulous premise and as far as Isekai cliches go (which I shan't delve into), Slime does represent those tropes to a T. Yet... one can't help but be inexplicably drawn into the series and just enjoy themselves to their fullest. Unexpectedly, despite the generic traits in the world it presents, Slime manages to accomplish the rare feat of keeping you invested in the fantasyelements prevalent. It paints a vibrant world inhabited (obviously) by a wide diversity of races with their own intricate relationship dynamics, which is gradually shifted with the induction of our dear op slime MC (and various plot points). More importantly, interest in this setting is sustained by our endearing MC who is just so bubbly optimistic that every interaction it has just ends up being satisfying. Because of how wholesome our MC is, it inadvertently appeals to the various parties it meets, resulting in very intriguing relationships being born. As a viewer, one inevitably slips into the routine of binge-watching to find out how this slime will continue to venture and eventually cement its place in this new world.

Also worth noting is how the show excels in it's neat pacing and refrains from dumping exorbitant amounts of information on the viewer, allowing viewers the opportunity to immerse themselves in the fantasy world and appreciate it as presented. Slime is punctilious in maintaining balance between the small but steadily expanding world of our MC, and the disclosure of preexisting information about the larger world in the objective sense, providing viewers ample exposure and hence understanding of the alternate fantasy world.

Battle scenes might lack expected tension, but the aftermath and emotional catharsis that precedes/accompanies it does rectify such problems. Personally, it is precisely because the fights aren't overtly serious that we can appreciate the technicalities and/or the motivations of the combatants (which are aptly linked to the world's settings). Furthermore, one can even go as far as to say that because fights are dominated by our MC that it complements the overall vibe of the show, enabling the MC chances to further exhibit its affectionate nature. 

Arguably, Slime never detracts from it's intent as a true blue Isekai fantasy show and never takes itself too seriously, thus allowing for an enjoyable watch. In fact, the supposed cliches that should be demerits never feel like cliches and instead provide an inexplicably refreshing feeling to the genre. Though it cannot be denied that certain characters do fall flat and potential development is squandered for the sake of said cliches, which is a shame considering the direction the show appears to be proceeding in. 

As for the technical aspects of the show, nothing much can be said except for how spectacular and invigorating the soundtrack is. Art is nothing breathtaking but is sufficiently vivacious.

Overall, if you are able to get past the "Isekai barrier" of this show and enjoy it for what is presented, Slime will probably be worth your while.
