There's all these demons that chat and sip wine in their mansion but why don't we see them do anything? Who knows but that's why I'm hopeful for season 2.

It has definitely become a religious offering for every season to have “THAT” one Isekai that will have a good percentage of the fandom's following no matter how trash it is, in the food industry, that would be where McDonald's ranks up with, something very familiar that's easy to get into with a very simple to grasp concept that remains very true to the “modern” reception of Anime. Unfortunately, “Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken” matches up with everything mentioned above, however, as unexpected as it is, the trashy part couldn't be more wrong. On the surface, “Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken” seems like your type ofIsekai where your virgin pervert dude is thrown into a cursed land, along with his magical weapon and a shallow cast of females that form his harem save the world and live happily ever after. “Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken” has so little in common with your average Isekai and so much more with a world-renowned RPG game with a Skyrim-like depth in both worldbuilding and event handling making every episode more of a save checkpoint that bit by bit get you closer to the end game filling you with a great sense of achievement at the end of your journey.


Story (8/10):
Trust me, as generic and boring as it might strike you, it does get a whole lot better. Of course, every Isekai starts the same, the protagonist has to enter a new world after they either die or just give up on their world, sometimes it's just mandatory and doesn't give the said protagonist a chance to decide, but that's irrelevant to this.
You have this relatable middle-aged dude, somewhat of a capable gentleman of the working class that's just fed u with how he's living, suddenly surrenders his life to save an acquaintance of his, next second he's in another world that screams of RPG, but this time, it's neither an attractive shallow handsome-head that gets all of them hoes neither a powerhouse badass edgy rascal that gets his victory on demand. He just gets reincarnated... as a... S-Slime. I swear I wasn't going for the pun.

The plot runs through speedy pacing that really does justice to its short self-contained arcs. There is a lot of action and also a balanced amount of dialogue that serves a great deed into building the world around the characters making them feel like an ant, something very insignificant against a much greater entity, but that doesn't limit from their influence.


Art (8/10):
If Anime could get sick, one of those devastating plagues would be the lack of inconsistency visually speaking. Some of the fights, not, let's say, all of the fights look outstanding, almost breathtaking with smooth cartography and slick camera movement.
On a general note, the show does have a noticeable almost warm visual effect layered on everything that makes everything look more greenish and natural that emphasized the medieval theme that houses the event of the story. The colors look bright and attractive while still easy to keep up with the action.
The anatomy is one other thing I feel they've done right, there is something about it that just screams of RPG, everybody looks like a heavily customizable NPC from a Bethesda game.


Sound (8/10):
Voice acting wide, I can't really complain about anything while still can't find something to really praise that much, it felt decent, just above average at best, probably the ridiculous of high voices wasn't my cup of tea, but I really have to give it to the sound effects and the background soundtracks, oh, just so good, and you know how much cool abilities from magic to an ever more magical kind of magic, vocally simulating those can be a real challenge but the team behind this side of the show knew what they were doing, straight out of a quality AAA title.
I can spit it the way I have it on my mind, but it's something very satisfying that highlights those short but yet powerful fire burst sound effects.
The soundtracks were really amazing as well, as you'd grown on them on your favorite RPG, the same was here, you could swear you've had countless hours of fun while watching and paying attention to them like you would do when playing a video game.


Characters (7.5/10):
I can't stand for the show and say it had anything revolutionary regarding its character cast if anything, that was a HUGE roster to keep track of. And I'm not kidding, a tremendous amount of new faces make it to the screen every arc, and no, they stay there until the last episode, with is one plus point for not neglecting any characters. Take some notes, Naruto.
It feels really bad to not give off a slightly higher score on this pick, but I got to really take out my frustrations on some boring and badly written characters that are just there for the same of filling a character spot. Yes, talking about you, Milim, if that was how your correctly spelled and I'm not bothering to check, that's how much I care.
A wide selection of characters are just there as an image of what it's supposed to be a powerhouse, but having a shallow childish figure hold a great title of power and following while being easily swayed by a gram of honey, Nah, that sounds like a wasted potential on a stupid loli from me.


Enjoyment (9/10):
You can imagine the satisfaction I got after every achievement done by the protagonist, as he's narrating what he's going through, you really feel like the person with the controller at hand doing everything yourself, starting off basically from scratch, literally, just a piece of moving slime with no primitive senses or anything to making it into a badass ruler that can start blad thunderbolts with a rise of a finer, just how badass is that?


Overall (8.1/10):
I really, really recommend this pick and even dare to recommend it to people that are not into Isekai because it truly does offer a unique experience that a lot of other similar shows fail to deliver upon. It's got likable characters, pacing fast enough to keep the action good and the excitement high all the time, and of course, it's got a lot of hype surrounding it.

Welcome to my review of the anime 'Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken", often also just called "the Slime anime". This anime is produced by the studio 8bit and it consists of 24 epsidoes, originally 25. The last episode became a special which I am also talking about in this review at its end. The studio 8bit is more or less unknown and rarely comes to attention with a great anime title, if at all. Only three anime they previously did have recognition in the anime community; those being Infinite Stratos, Rewrite, and the most known of all three, Grisaia no Kajitsu (Fruit of Grisaia). Thispretty dry track record might end now. Studio 8bit might find themselves on more contracts after they landed a massive hit with 'That time I got reincarnated as a Slime'. Slime has become a save watch for the last two seasons it aired. Mostly everyone watched this show and just as many praised it. But is the praise justified or this just another overhyped anime title like many others before? 


Story/plot: Before saying anything, let start with that this anime is an Isekai. I will trust you that you know what that word means in this community. The story starts with Mikami Satoru, a regular everyday nice guy who just happens to get stabbed in the back by a robber out of unfortunate events. What continues is Satoru being reincarnated as a Slime in a Fantasy World. It starts in a cave where he gradually evolves by absorbing and killing various things and creatures. At one point it ends up meeting the storm dragon Veldora who is locked in that cave thanks to a spell. The Slime and the Dragon Form a friendship and give each others names. From then on they are Veldora and Rimuru Tempest. And from that day on Rimuru ends up helping others and bukding up relationships with other creatures.
So what is this anime about? To steal the words of others I say "This is not an Isekai, this is Civilization The Anime". And truly, the anime actually feels more like a civilization building game than an Isekai anime. Even past the civilization point Slime Datta Ken is surprisingly tame when it comes to the themes. Don't get me wrong, there is violence! But the theme and atmosphere of the anime is more or less very friendly and upbeat; something rare these days.

Art: The artstyle of Slime Datta Ken is very soft and light. The surrounding and background have a watercolor vibe to them. The characters also look pretty decent. Fighting animation was throughout the show really solid and sometimes even high quality. I don't remember the show dropping in quality at any point but I could have missed it.

Sound: Openings and Endings were solid, the ending more than the Openings. As far as my personal taste goes both the second OP and ED were the better ones. BGM was also solid but nothing stuck with me. SFX were of course there but I don't remember anything worth noting.

Characters: There are a lot of characters. A lot. Listing everyone is a bit tiring and most of them aren't worth even mentioning. The one and only one worth mentioning is the main character itself, Rimuru Tempest. Carried over from his past life Rimuru still has all his emotions, memories and self. Through these we learn Rimuru's personality. A fellow who likes peace and dislikes conficts and problems. All in all every character is fairly plain and easy constructed. Slime Datta Ken is not a deep anime do it does not need deep anime.

Enjoyment & verdict (of the main show): I'd say I overall really enjoyed the anime and it was a fun and cool ride. Slime is not the next big thing but it does what it does right. Being a nice more relaxed show is a good change for once. Now do I recommend it? Yes, I would say I recommend it as it is a nice show to watch and for what it does it's a good show. I give this anime an 8/10.

OVA verdict: Nice finisher for the show but overall unimportant and only slighly funny. If you have the time you can enjoy this last last episode, otherwise you are not going to miss anything amazing or groundbreaking.

And that's it for my review, I hope you liked it and I will see you in my next review!

For 24 episodes, this flowed very nicely. I didn't get bored at any one time and I could drop the series off for a little bit and pick it right up and not feel like I missed anything or run into a continuity issue that required me to go back and re-educate myself on. At the beginning, I knew that I was going to enjoy at least the MC from a voice perspective. Brittany Karbowski is my favorite VA and really impressed me with Rimiru. While it was kind of light in tone throughout the whole show for Rimiru, her presentation to each situation matched perfectly.I think what impressed me most about this within regards to the lack of range in emotion is the sheer volume of dialogue she had to go through. I think it could be safe to say that she had about half of all dialogue. I couldn't imagine just how exhaustive that would have to be.

In regards to the show and the storyline, I enjoyed how each situation was handled, however I think they were too many conflicts. Most were brought up and resolved in two episodes and all of the decisions to major problems were done on the fly, like with the Cryptid and the summoned children. It just happened all at once and been and BAM, they were resolved. It was extremely frustrating to watch. I really would have preferred if they cut back on one or two confrontation(s) versus having six or seven. Give me a longer, drawn out interaction, perhaps in three episodes instead of two like is seen in a lot of other shows. I would also like to have seen ownership by the characters rather than an easy solution, like when Milim took down the Cryptid. One large shot and it was over with.

Despite its shortcomings, it's well worth watching to enjoy. I know that there are spin-off episodes that I caught two of and a movie and five OVAs. I can't say that I liked the show enough to chase all of that down, though.

Certainly worth a recommend.

Welcome to TenSura, one of the latest additions to the niche and undersaturated genre known as "isekai" *laugh track plays*. Since there are about 17 isekais produced every anime season, studios have realized that in order to produce a truly successful isekai, they need to grab the viewer's attention in the first couple episodes. What happens after that? Eh, who cares. The show's already popular. Story (4/10): I believe one of the greatest flaws of TenSura is the concept itself. The idea of a light-hearted Overlord may sound good on paper, but it fails in execution. Overlord works as a show because Ainz is cool. Theproblem with TenSura is that Rimuru really... isn't cool. He's OP in a Kirito-like, boring way, in that he lacks any personality other than being an average, nice person. After the pretty good first few episodes (up through the establishment of the goblin village) Rimuru just doesn't do anything interesting. I'm struggling to recall what actually happened in the arcs because there's not really anything connecting them. Rimuru just goes to some random place and gets more allies for his village by talking to them. Personally, I don't find that this makes for a very entertaining show. There's no overarching plot, no "cool factor," and no tension since Rimuru can easily defeat any enemy with his OP isekai protagonist skills. Oh yeah, apparently there was a comedy aspect here? I didn't find it funny, and apparently MAL didn't either since this show doesn't have a comedy tag.

Characters (5/10): Who? The only character listed as a "main" in TenSura is Rimuru, who, as discussed above, I do not like. The other characters include a harem of personality-less dolls, some side characters like Souei who attempt to compensate for Rimuru's lack of coolness, and random characters that appear once and are never brought up again. Shizu, the only character that may be argued to be "well-written" is nothing but a well-disguised MacGuffin. All she does is progress the plot.

I'd like to talk about the random side characters in further detail. The problem here is that this season is pretty much an introduction into the universe. You get all of these characters that are simply introduced and left alone, like demon lord with clown servants, demon lord with blonde hair, knight girl who is hinted to be Shizu's disciple, those adventurers from the guild near the end of the show, and probably others that I've forgotten about. They're probably going to be important in the next season, but what about this season? 

Art (8/10): Pretty solid. The character designs are relatively memorable. The color scheme and the overall art help build the comforting, light-hearted atmosphere that the show strives for. The fights are nicely animated.

Sound (8/10): Idk why I'm giving this a high rating. There's this one OST that plays during every battle that's stuck in my head, so apparently that somehow makes the sound good. The OP and ED themes also nicely mirror the quality of the show. Just like the show was good at the start and became a drag, the first OP and ED were good, and the second ones really weren't.

Enjoyment & Overall (6/10): TenSura was extremely bland, but I can't really give it a lower rating since it was decent enough for me to have the desire to watch every new episode. I'm really hoping that this was simply a setup season and that season two will be better, since this season seems to lay the groundwork and nothing else, but only time will tell.

I think that watching this anime is worthwhile since the storyline is exciting and enjoyable to watch. In the beginning, it is a little slow for about 3-5 episodes then the story starts to pick up. You get to see character development as well as power-ups in power and abilities. Maybe for some, it may not be their type of anime to watch, but I liked it. A few scenes were hilarious to watch and I did like many of the characters. In addition, the animation of the fights between the characters are high-quality and look well done. A few flaws within the show isthe fact that the storyline can tend to go by pretty quick, but that is understanding considering the show is only 24 eps. If given the time, I probably would rewatch it especially if another season is released. I feel the story gets more interesting as the show progresses as well.

Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken: an anime with monsters, but all of good vibes What happens when an office worker almost in his forties, of good character and full of common sense, is transported to a fantasy world turned into an almost almighty monster? Well, this anime series from last fall season offers us a version of these events. The result: some very relaxed adventures to pass the time. In October of last year, another anime was released on Japanese television of a genre that has been in vogue there for a few years now: the Isekai. And what is the Isekai? In short, someone -a teenager,a university student, a middle-aged character ... - is transported or reincarnated in another world ("isekai": another world). Normally he does it with some kind of special superpower and with a mission to undertake - the reason why he is in that new world - but it is not an indispensable trope.

What usually happens one hundred percent of the time is that the world is fantastic and contains magical creatures -what would be an epic adventure without monsters to shoot down?-. And since the rise of novels such as Sword Art Online -which, paradoxically, is not strictly speaking of this genre- the way in which the protagonists of these stories explore, interact and experience these fantastic worlds blatantly resembles the mechanics behind a MMORPG.


Well: Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken (translated to English as "That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime”) is an isekai of the new ones, with its multiplayer roleplay mechanics , level ups, information interface, and even evolution of monsters. But what story does it really tell us? The synopsis is the following.

One day, Satoru Mikami, 37, an ordinary worker who lives in Tokyo and has no girlfriend or commitment, saves the life of Tamura, his workmate, and dies on the spot. But his story does not end there, because as his last thoughts leave his head, a strange entity is configuring the characteristics of his new body to reincarnate in another world.

So, to his surprise, Satoru will wake up again from the sweet dream, fully aware of his previous life, but as a slime: the classic video game slime monster like Dragon Quest. Full of optimism and ready to live a fuller life, Satoru, renamed Rimuru Tempest by a whole dragon, sets off to explore this new world, in which he will undo wrongs of all kinds thanks to his peculiar set of skills and, on the way, He will make friends with all kinds of monsters.


It is not a very original plot, and having a protagonist with a series of extraordinary skills and abilities that save him from almost any situation can cause you to lose interest by eliminating a source of conflicts. But the truth is that the series does not focus much on the conflicts that Rimuru lives: the problems are almost always solved in a practical or peaceful way, and the battles are usually an excuse for his friends to shine.

Our protagonist is a deus ex machina who sometimes saves the situation at the last moment in a very convenient way, but the story that it is telling us is not really about people fighting with superpowers. It does not matter that Rimuru ends the monster of turn in one or two movements, what really keeps us interested in the series is how these characters get to know each other and establish alliances and friendships.


In general, it is a series of very calm adventures, of slow pace and without compulsion. In fact, the moments of dramatic tension can be resolved quickly and although they are not forgotten, they do not creep beyond the resolution. It is a series designed to invoke pleasant, happy and warm feelings in who is seeing it. It is so relaxed and cheerful that, in fact, it could be considered a weakness.

It is missing more dramatic tension, some conflict that is difficult to resolve or with an unsatisfactory resolution. The series is a little naive: the problems are always resolved, there is no sense of danger at any time and everyone is in the end very friendly. If the characters -which, in all honesty, are very archetypal: the cool guy with bad attitude, the hypercompetent assistant with generous breasts, the short and funny friend, the Yamato Nadeshiko, etc.- were not so nice and sympathetic, the interest of the series in this first season would have been off very soon.

Another weakness of the series has to do with the rhythm of it. The first half has a slow progress: it details the adventures of Rimuru very much, but it is a constant rhythm and although it is slow, it engages. The second half breaks that constant rhythm: it goes to the bone of the story, cutting off superfluous details, but losing the charm that hooked you in the first half and, with it, part of the interest. Sometimes the cuts are such that they liquidate a whole fight or solve a problem with a narrative line.

From a more technical point of view, the series -animated by the 8-Bit studio- is in the average of the anime of 24 episodes for television. There are not many pirouettes in the direction, and the designs are quite generic; but the drawing is regular, consistent, and some battles are pretty fun to watch. The casting of voices is correct and the simple and environmental music helps to give an air of RPG of the Super Nintendo.

In the end, it would not be too crazy to claim that Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken is a nice anime to watch. It does not stand out in any section nor is it among the best of the last six months, but it can give us a few afternoons of entertainment and relaxation for those who like adventures. The series has been well received and will have a second season -and who knows if more, seeing that the manga that adapts the same novels, currently in publication, is being a success-. It seems we will have this "good slime" for a while.

How is this absolutely bland ass anime rated 8+ on MAL? I have no idea what the state of the fandom is but I’m assuming it’s a bunch of kids who got introduced into anime through this show. The characters are at best a convenient throwaway plot point to get MC to the top of this fictional world, which is literally blander than British food. The show goes through multiple story arcs which are meant to be character introductions/ development, but the writer also decided that (somehow) covering 40 ish characters is a good idea, which means that most characters get only surface level interactions.The backstory of MC and most supporting characters could be written by a 6 year old. The show tosses out names and expositions at the convenience of the MC and hands everything to him. 
The fights are somewhat creative during the first few episodes due to the somewhat unique setting of the MC and his powers, but quickly get repetitive. The characters all cycle the same overpowered abilities and/or techniques in the fights.
Further, every time a new power scaling is introduced it takes about 3-4 episodes before the mc gets on that power level or surpasses it.
This is an isekai power fantasy where the MC is heinously unaware of his own shortcomings and fills the gap with the tremendous amounts of power he has been provided. 
It’s quite fitting that the MC is a slime because he couldn’t be more bland if he wanted to. This guy is literally more one dimensional than tadano from Komi can’t communicate. 
The dialogues are super boring and repetitive and often I found myself rewinding the episodes a few seconds or minutes because I zoned out due to the amount of filler dialogue and absolute nonsense garbage magic bullshit which came out of the writer’s pen. 
The animation is slightly above average but nothing special and it leaves much to be desired, considering how repetitive the fights are. 
The score sounds like nursery rhymes half the time and it feels like it was composed by someone who’s never seen a musical instrument before in their life just throwing random darts at the music sheet and picking whichever notes stuck. 
Even most of the jokes left me stone faced, wondering what I was doing with my life.
Overall this anime is the definition of mid with a mid storyline, mid characters, mid art style, mid dialogue, mid bgm, and pretty mid jokes. This shit was so mid it literally gave me a mid life crisis, and I put this anime on hold for 2 weeks before picking it back up to finish this shit. 
And for the absolute midness Tensei shitara slime datta ken gets a 5.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Snoozefest The first handful of episodes actually set up a really promising start to a potentially groundbreaking isekai. It's also the only anime where a tsundere dragon gets vored by a slime, so I definitely have to give it credit for that. However, as the show enters the 10+ episode mark, a critical issue becomes apparent. This issue is the fact that the show's writers don't care about the new side characters that are introduced for Rimuru to help with, yet at the same time expect us to care. For some unexplainable reason, the show decides to have some genericshonen fights, perhaps in an attempt to get some free publicity from "Epic Anime Fight Scene Complication #12 2019" on YouTube. Yet nothing about these fights is epic. There are no stakes, no "wow" moments, no memorable punches...they're just sort of there. 

By the end of the series, I really didn't care about what Rimuru was going to do to save the day this time. The fun that was present in the beginning of the series had pretty much diminished as it churned out tropes that could probably be found done better in fantasy shonen from a decade ago.

Despite my harsh criticism over the overall atmosphere/my enjoyment of the series, there are redeemable elements that belonged in a better series. Rimuru is a bit overpowered, but overall a good character. Shizue, the goblins, the wolves, Millim - all of them could've set the ground for a really good fantasy series.

The best way to describe Slime overall is "so close, yet so far." In the development of the series, an essential checkmark was clearly missed before releasing it: "isn't freaking boring."

“If it looks like I stand no chance I’ll run away and think up a new plan, but otherwise, I should see how strong it is with my own eyes, right?” – Rimuru Tempest Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is an isekai that offers the audience action, comedy, world building and a little god-complex moments. Story: 9/10 I loved the concept of building you own village/city while making friendships/alliances with other humans/monsters (there were a lot of "/'s" in that sentence). While Rimuru may be some kind of god-complex character, he is still not the strongest in that world, thus he needs to form alliances with other individualsto grow in military might. Combine that with seeing and experiencing an evolution of the city of Tempest and you have a great story. The world of Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken also offers a lot of possibilities since it is so vast in powers, monsters and countries. There will be a lot of stuff the author can expand on, which could make a franchise out of Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken.

Usually in other isekai anime, the main character is weak compared to other armies/people in that world and thus he/she has to grovel to defeat them. Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken isn't like this. Rimuru is already an overpowered character who can easily defeat the majority of countries in the world of Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken. We are introduced to stronger characters though, which keeps the story interesting.

Art: 7/10

When I watched the first couple of episodes, I wasn't amazed by the art. Especially because this anime aired in 2018, which should make its animation look clean and modern. Because this wasn't really the case, I would have initially given Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken a 5/10 for art. That was until the fight scenes showed up. Combined with amazing sound effects, the fight scenes were something else. The animation looked clean and the aura's of different magic spells reminded me of the Fate/Stay series. This boosted the score from a 5/10 to a 7/10.

Sound: 7/10

While the sound effects were awesome, the OST's weren't very memorable to me. Especially compared to other anime like: SAO, Boku no Hero Academia, Haikyuu etc... This doesn't mean that the OST's weren't good. They fulfilled their purpose: accompany the scenes in the anime well. 
The OP and ED were pretty good. They're nothing crazy, but they were enjoyable to listen to.

Character: 5/10

This is one of the only things I disliked about Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken, which made it a 7/10 and not an 8/10. 
The characters overall were pretty boring and didn't have much to offer. Although some characters were pretty colorful (Gobta, Veldora, Milim, Rimuru), most weren't (Behimaru, Ranga, Souei, Shuna...). This has to do with the anime introducing a vast cast of characters. They didn't have time to expand on all the stories of those characters, thus making them appear plain and boring on the surface.

What bugged me the most was that the characters are just too forgiving. A lot of the characters also don't stick to their own beliefs and just follow Rimuru like a flock of sheep. They basically see Rimuru as their God and will do anything he says. This makes a lot of the characters look weak mentally.

Enjoyment: 9/10

The only reason why I didn't give enjoyment a 10/10 is because I wasn't as hooked to the story towards the end of the season (episode 20-24) as I was at the beginning of the season. The excitement kind of faded out, because there wasn't much happening (especially in the Spirit Arc). 
Overall, the story really intrigued me and it radiated a wholesome vibe. 

Overall: 7/10

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is one of the best isekai I have seen so far. It has great world build, an enjoyable story and was exciting from beginning to end (except for episode 20-24). 
I would certainly recommend this anime to anyone who loves isekai/adventure/fantasy/action anime!

7/10 This is undeniably not a masterpiece. This show has very little character development, pacing issues, and very little plot development (so far). That's okay. A show doesn't need any of those things to be enjoyable. I feel like a lot of people get caught up in what a show 'ought' to have, while ignoring its potential for enjoyment regardless of what it does or doesn't have. If you haven't seen Slime, then I'd tell you that it's primarily about world development. I specifically mean development, and not worldbuilding. The difference being that worldbuilding is focused on creating a comprehensive, interlocking and coherent universe. While development isjust that: how the world develops.

In that sense, this show is very solid. If you're looking for character development, or a comprehensive and well built world, or a deeper, hidden theme, you won't find it here. Instead, you'll enter it thinking this will be a standard Isekai where the MC learns and grows and eventually outclasses everyone.

Not true in Slime. The MC is overpowered, sure, but the way their power is used is what defines the show. The MC uses their power to build and serve as the ruler of a town. That town grows and prospers throughout the series, and the relationships the fledgling civilization establishes are what the show explores.

In this sense, it provides the same satisfaction that well done character development provides. You see something you love grow and change, eventually blossoming into something much more impressive. That's why I like this show. I don't care about the plot, or the characters as much as I'm excited to see what happens to the world itself. And for that, I'd give it a 7/10. It's solidly entertaining, but doesn't reach deeper into my heart than that.

I love this anime a lot. And I mean alot! I was hesitant to watch it at first until my friend recommended it to me so I gave it a go and boy was I addicted. So addicted, I just had to find out what happens next and completed the entire webnovels and a couple of light novels aswell. Ahhhhh! Just too good. You might think what the hell, a slime as the mc. But its just amazing. The world building and the plot is so intricate probably because it was adapted from a novel but it really draws people in. The comedy was great andthe character development was top tier with Rimuru getting more powers and granting more power to his subordinates. Truly the best story of a slime from the bottom climbing his way to power and the life of luxury he sets his goal on. :)

A random guy working a standard 9-5 gets killed and guess what, isekai time! This is the whole backstory of Rimuru Tempest the main character of this story. But what is Rimuru? He's a slime, one of the weakest magical creatures of all, or is he? let's find out! Let's keep this review short because i don't think there is much to say about Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken. It's an isekai that is so fast phased it makes you feel like there is not a single pause in the narrative. From episode 2 to episode 24 you never get a moment to breath, every singleepisode there is atleast a fight or a major event that shapes the world. 
Sometimes it's hard to understand what's going to happen not because of the complexity of the story but rather the opposite, it's so linear that it's stunning how the author could jump from one plot point to another. 

The only way i could describe is that rather than you devouring this anime it's the other way around, Slime is devouring you leaving nothing behind but a deside to watch the next episode. This is the strongest point for this story centered around our hero Rimuru, it's fun, it's light, it's packed with action, add a little bit of fanservice (maybe too much but still bereable) and the recipe is done. 

Now since the plot and the worldbuilding of Season 1 was extremely plain, with everything happening without a real reasoning or atleast without a reason explained in a decent manner i suppose next seasons will slow down in order to work on what season 1 left behind, the world building. 

Now let's get down to the critical parts.
There is no way on earth that everyone in this story are enemies and then the next episode after being defeated become best friends forever. It's fun to watch but in terms of story depth it just doesn't sound right. So if you are looking for a deep story go watch something else.

In any case judging an entire franchise from first season would be insane and i actually really enjoyed watching it so regardless of how plain some plot point might be it's still something i'd reccomend!

Another isekai anime... Story - 9/10 - A man is killed on the street and he is reincarnated as a slime. What to say. Kinda nice, fighting anime with a good pace and isekai story. Our main character is kinda overpowered and he is trying to do his best to change things around him to his ideals. I would say there are many interesting events and characters. It's just regular wholesome and funny anime with many spells and races etc. Maybe a few episodes from the start are boring but from the 4th episode, everything is getting much better and smoother. Art - 9/10 - The art is pretty good, I'm really satisfied with it.

Character - 9/10 - The main character is a friendly slime who is trying to protect others and make their life better. Supporting characters are funny, or cute, or both. You will find some waifu everywhere.

Brief overview: It's about nation-building. This review will be based on the whole series up to season 3. 8/10 for the series Introduction A former Human has been stabbed in his previous life. He was therefore reincarnated into another world with a very broken ability that allowed him to absorb any abilities within that world and become that ability. However, it is at a cost of becoming a different species which left him to be Rimuru the slime. Throughout his journey, he meets up with a few goblins that have been constantly attacked by the wolves clan due to the significant difference between the power level of the goblinsand wolves. Rimuru then defeated them and settled the war between Goblins and wolves to become partners. This is when Rimuru discovers that the current place they're in is mostly filled with monsters and many of them have independent mindsets. Rimuru sets out a goal to establish this place that can allow both Humans and Monsters to live in peace together. 

Story 9/10
At first, the story is quite good. They begin the story by introducing problems in which there are many problems such as the lack of understanding of this world, The current place they're in has an independent monster group that is not unified, and an overlord that wants to cause the downfall of that nation. Rimuru started tackling those problems bit by bit and instead of using violence he took a different approach by establishing friendships, allies, and trades along the way. This shows Rimuru's capability as a leader and how to manage those issues properly which is a pretty important skill to learn as he is a former manager. Towards the later series, the interesting narrative has been explained, and everything feels like it is meant to end. The only purpose is to prolong the series with no important narrative involved such as building an entertainment district or a train system. The villains mostly felt left out and the series mostly focused on political and economic trade, which made most of the action nonexistent.

Characters 8/10
The main character Rimuru is quite a well-portrayed character in a manager's sense. There is quite a lot of educational content to learn from Rimuru on how to become a better manager. It is hard to be a well-liked manager because you can't be too much of in control or you will be viewed as a tyrant and at the same time you can't be too lenient as everyone would not see you as a boss. Rimuru keeps this balance well to give his subordinates the freedom to do their jobs and at the same time correct the mistakes of their subordinates. It is important to give punishment but those punishments must be learned from their mistake which most of Rimuru punishment did. Other characters are quite generic in a sense but they're not bad just typical. However, they do have a lot of likable personalities and quite some good backstories as well.

Animation 7/10
The animation is strange. They're not bad but very generic in a sense. In the usual scene when there is no fight the animation looks fine however when there is a fight scene the animation looks good yet average at the same time. That's mainly because the fight scenes are too fast and is hard to catch up on what the character's fighting style looks like. This makes the scene feel or look scribbled however they are not. It's still not a bad fight scene but is not up to the level of Bleach TYBW.

TLDR
It's about a reincarnated human that is currently a Slime who wants to build a nation that both Humans and Monster can live in peace. However, to achieve that goal their is a lot of unsolve problems which Rimuru needs to tackle it one by one which this shows a great example on how to mange a work environment in a sense. The animation is good but when it comes to fight scene the fighting scene looks a bit too fast which makes it feel scribbled but in reality is not.

"THAT TIME I GOT REINCARNATED AS A SLIME" Genre- Adventure, Action, Magic, Fantasy, Isekai, Comedy. What does it mean to live an average and basic life? Does it include the list of all the things that you want to do or does it mean to keep working every day just to support your daily needs? And if it's the latter, does that actually mean living or surviving just one other day to hope for a better tomorrow? Satoru is an average Japanese male, who has a pretty decent and average life where he works like any other salaryman, eats like them, and exists in the world like them,but one day due to a stabbing incident, he loses his life and gets reincarnated as a slime in another world. A world filled with different creatures, adventuring parties, heroes, demon lords, and most of all, a world filled with magic and its entities. From here the story of Satoru (now nicknamed Rimuru) the most powerful slime to ever exist, starts. From fighting many battles to befriending different magical creatures that join his settlement, Rimuru and his party keep getting stronger but what are the foes that await him, that is something that you must find for yourself.

On the aspect of technicalities, this anime delivers to you 2 main things. One is top-of-the-line animation, and the other is a story that you could keep watching for hours and hours with no end. And with the way that this season ended, you can be sure that there is more thrill yet to come.

This anime is absolutely a "MUST WATCH."

After an untimely death, Satoru Mikami is reincarnated in another world as a slime. (Literally the title of the anime...) He decides to make the most of his new found life, and embarks on a journey that will shake up the world around him. That Time I got Reincarnated as a Slime is a very boring and dull isekai anime that everyone likes literally just cause the main character is an overpowered slime, and his best trait is that he is really nice… Great… How riveting. For those that haven't seen it, the short version of my complaints would be a boring nice guy protagonist and abunch of lacking side characters. For those that have seen it, imagine with me, what this anime would be like if the main character was never a slime to begin with. Then ask yourself “does it still hold up as a good isekai that stands above the many generic ones?” No, it wouldn't, most of the elements it's viewers say they like would instead EASILY be dismissed as just "more isekai garbage" and other comments of that nature.

There’s a reason the best, and arguably the only isekai anime you should watch are Overlord, Re:ZERO, Konosuba, as of 2019, The Rising of the Shield Hero. That same reason is why those four have a crossover anime called isekai Quartet , and that reason is that those four anime have a large cast of great beloved characters, and the lead characters themselves have distinct personalities that the fans have loved to see shift and adapt to the law breaking environments they are placed in for better or worse. Not because their protagonist is simply a "nice guy" with obedient followers that are devoid of any interesting characteristics that end up creating a story that feels disgustingly slow and boring. That's my biggest gripe with this anime, when you don't factor in the characters, everything else is fine from the world building to story and of course it's quality, but my priority in any piece of media is always the characters FIRST. Characters and their journeys are what most of us love to discuss or remember in the first place, and ultimately is what drives sales for the stupidly expensive merchandise we buy and love.

Look, after that rant about it's characters, that's not to say I didn't like anyone. Here's where my review transitions from the negatives to the positives. The later half of the anime introduces characters that gave me the will to keep watching, and ended up helping me get through to the end of the anime. Specifically Gabiru with his lizardmen crew, Demon Lord Millim Nava, and all the isekai children in the last arc. In addition I also mentioned earlier the world building, story, and quality are all fleshed out and pretty solid overall. I should also mention this anime has competent fight scenes involving massive power levels, while I may not like most super flashy anime fights, if that's your jam you'll enjoy it. So all in all, while my personal tastes for characters was not met here, there was enough here in Slime Reincarnation for me to get through to the end. It's not exactly a glowing review, but then again in my opinion it's cause the anime is not worthy of such high praise. It is GOOD, don't mistake that, but I don't believe in the hype the rest of the world had for this anime. If you want a slow burn that becomes a solid experience that is ultimately harmless, go ahead and watch, if you want a great isekai, watch any of the five I mentioned above. I write these reviews hoping to help readers like you enjoy yourself. Even if my opinions get the better of me, I do this as an anime fan, for anime fans. I'm actually kind of looking forward to season 2 coming this year!

I feel like sometimes we are scraping the bottom of the barrel for Isekai ideas...well that is if you only watched the first couple of episodes. But then you realise that is not enough so you have to think of something. Thenyou have an idea, how about make it the anime equivalent of Civilisation. 


Sit back, relax and be friends with Ghandi because he has all of those nukes as a I present to you the anime review for That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime. Lets begin. 


Story: 6.5/10

We begin with seeing a middle aged business man by the name of Satoru Mikami getting stabbed by a random assailant and is bleeding to death. With his friend by his side, he tells him that his final wish is for him to destroy his hard hard drive on the computer (clearly a man who has correctly prioritised his wishes). Instead of passing to the great beyond though, he finds himself reincarnated as a slime. Trying to figure out where he is, running into some colourful characters and given the name Rimuru Tempest. He sets out onto the new world and prepares to leave his mark on the world, whether intentional or not. 

When the first couple of episodes features a slime making conversation with a Tsundere dragon, you know you are in for something special here. And that is somewhat the case as the story goes on. The story feels like the it is split into different arcs as there always seem to be a new obstacle or threat that Rimuru has to overcome. Normally in different scenarios which is nice because sometimes you need to watch something more relaxing or something more intense and it seems to know when it wants to do a more relaxing arc or a more intense arc. Although, the more battle heavy arcs don't carry too much tension since the good guys are overpowered as f**k but it is always nice to live out a power fantasy, but that is just accepting that these guys and gals are strong. Is that a bad thing? Well the show gives us some reasons as to why some of these characters are strong or get stronger. Rimuru gains the powers of whatever he devours, so we him gain more power as he fights greater and greater threats. As for the rest of the cast, the power of the name is what gives them strength because they are given and identity rather than be some nameless monster. 

But what this show does well is it takes what is good about an Isekai anime and builds on it. Discovering a new world, meeting unique people and creatures, gaining strength over time and becoming an important figurehead of the world. But Rimuru doesn't do it by gaining strength and power, he does it by building a society of monsters. 

The overarching plot of this story IMO is Rimuru is trying to help build a society for monsters to coexist together in harmony. What starts off as uniting a tribe of Goblins with a pack of Direwolves turns into a massive community consisting of Goblins, Direwolves, Trolls, Dwarves, Orcs, Lizardmen and Dryads and living in peace together, as well as making alliances and trade agreements with neighbouring kingdoms. Rimuru doesn't simply ask or has it fall on his shoulder, he has either earn, make deals or create scenarios where it can benefit both parties. It is nice to see Rimuru simply trying to reach out instead of simply giving it to them because would you immediately make a deal with a slime? The show plays on the stereotypes of typical fantasy monsters and makes sure that the monsters are treated as equals to the rest of society by earning their respect. That what this show does well, it makes Rimuru have to earn their respect, rather than just giving it to him. 

The show narrative is enjoyable to watch...for the first half of this show. The second half is where I think momentum starts to slow down and we just get episodes that have moments but is just a load of meh. Not really exciting or emotional or tense or anything like that. While it does still have its comedy moments, the second half feels lacklustre. I put the blame on its weaker second sub plot that I will get into later on. Then it just ends, like that. Nothing to get me hyped for another season, it just ends and we're given two filler episodes to round out the show. Even the finale episode that ends the current story ends in a montage sequence for about half the episode. Talk about going out on a whimper. 


Characters: 8/10

Rimuru Tempest is indeed the main character of this show and honestly, it is nice to see an overpowered character not get everything handed to him, or her, or it. Slimes don't have genders but since Rimuru was originally a male businessman, I'll just refer to it as a male. Okay so Rimuru is, like other Isekai protagonists, a vessel used to allow us to see the world that he (as well as us) does not know about. So how do you get around doing that? Well building a society of course. Being a slime obviously has its disadvantages as slimes are considered cannon fodder enemies by fantasy standards. So when a slime is the leader of a community of monsters, well then people are just going to get confused. So Rimuru has to earn the respect of the people he comes across in order to make sure he is not some average slime. Of course his overpowered status does help but he also uses his knowledge of a businessman and thinks with a level head to get out of scenarios unscathed and benefits him and the people that serve under him. For example, when you encounter a rather chirpy daemon girl with overwhelming power, what would you do? Would you do 
a) Face her in a one on one battle. 
b) Send your subordinates after her. 
c) Make peace with her. 
d) Plead for mercy and serve her like a dog. 
If you answered any of those, you would not benefit the people you are protecting. Rimuru would rather do a bit of a) and a bit of c) so that Rimuru would get her attention but not go to far in order not to danger the lives he is protecting. He doesn't just recklessly charge in but instead assess the situation and tires to come up with a solution for any scenario. I respect that because he is thinking of the situation logically rather than just being reckless. It really does make him a great protagonist. 

The rest of the cast is vast and varied with various quirks and personalities and they are all endearing. Some fall into stereotypes but with a cast this big, I can forgive that. There are some standout obviously. Gabiru is a Lizardmen that is so full of himself as to being a great leader and great warrior that is just funny for him to get thwacked and gut punched when he totally deserves it. Millim who appears later in the series has a very nice chirpy personality and childlike wonder that acts as a wild card and a constant headache for Rimuru. Then there is Gobuta, who acts as the lovable underdog who wouldn't think would kick your ass until he does. 

There is one character in this show however that I think the show underdeveloped and that's Shizue Izawa. Despite being a main driving force for Rimuru when going forward, her overall relevance to the plot and screen time feels small despite being supposed to be a major element to the plot. Her main relevance is to give Rimuru a human form and that's really it. The whole subplot about fulfilling her final wishes is rather underwhelming and rather tedious at times. It only really comes into the final episodes of the show where she is an important factor but I feel you could have some some small rewrites and you wouldn't see much of a change. Some people might not agree with me on this point but it was a nagging factor for me. 


Animation: 5.5/10

Lets just say I'm not a big fan on the show's art style. It looks rather poor and does not look like a lot of effort was put into it. Particularly with the foresty areas where the backgrounds looked poorly drawn and was hastily put together. Some aspects and locations were slightly done better but honestly, it really does look primitive and I do not like it. Character designs are better in this regard and varied. Gobuta in particular is my favourite for its intentions. Gobuta design looks crappy compared to the others but I think that it was intentional because it hampers in that Gobuta is an underdog that doesn't look like he can kick your ass. So that is a nice touch. The animation itself fine. Sometimes the fight scenes can bring the best out of the animation but other times, it looks very meh, even cheap at times. So it can be inconsistent but it never really bothered me. Although I do like the expressions Rimuru makes which is nice since a slime doesn't really make facial expressions.


Sound: 7.5/10 

The soundtrack I would say does its job well. There always seems to be a soundtrack made for the scenario and I enjoyed it. While none particularity stand out, they definitely add to a scene. Whether it is a more calming scene, a sense of foreboding or a battle scene, there always seem to be a nice OST to compliment to a scene. 

I also particularly enjoyed the openings as well. Notice I said openings, so both of them are good IMO. "Nameless story" and "Meguru Mono" (which are both done Takuma Terashima) have good production values and does well at showing the cast and giving them a nice spotlight. Both vocal performances are also definitely good as well of the instrumentals matching the pace that the opening is trying to match. If I had to choose one, it would probably be the first one because the animation is top notch and something that the rest of the anime wishes to be like. The endings as well add are nice extensions to the openings as they act as nice closing sequences to the ending of each episode so I particularly enjoyed them. 


Conclusion: 

Slime definitely has its quirks that make it an enjoyable Isekai anime. It does stumble in some area, mainly in animation and some areas in the character department, but does have the necessary niches that make Isekai anime enjoyable and then some. The way the story progresses, how Rimuru grows his reputation, the huge cast of characters that are enjoyable in their own right for the most part and having good openings. Even the second opening stands out in a winter season that is f***ing stacked with good anime openings. Yet the show does stumble in the its major subplot and kind of fizzles out in the end, leaving to a rather unsatisfying conclusion. It left me not hyped for Season 2 of this show whereas and ending that has to be continued for another season should get me hyped.  

The appeal in Slime however, is that it takes what is good about an Isekai anime and runs with it. The power fantasy, the unexplored world, the characters you meet along the way. They are all here. And since they are all aspects I enjoyed, that should make it a highly recommended anime right? Yes and No. Power fantasy is something that only some people will enjoy and some people will criticise it. Even though the show does a good job of explaining it, it probably won't persuade people.

My Personal Enjoyment: 7/10 


Overall score: 6.9/10  Recommendation: Consider it

Fall 2018 and winter 2019 feature a number of isekai(-ish) adaptations, like Goblin Slayer or Shield Hero, with a strong fan base behind them due to popular manga or light novels. Tensei Slime also belongs into this category, however this anime sets itself apart from the competition with one distinct feature – it is a damn good and entertaining adaptation. The studio even manged to sneak some memes into it. SCORE: Good - 7 STORY: Entertaining but repetitive. As usual for the isekai genre our protagonist is granted a second chance in a fantasy world filled with magic, monsters and game-like systems, instead of eternal afterlife. The catch –main hero is a blue blob, a slime. And this concept works, because there is no world apocalypse to stop or girl’s heart to conquer, at least for now. This is basic escapism with focus on entertainment.
Narrative puts Rimaru in center of outcasts and follows his selfless task to create a peacefull community. This journey is defenitely a fun watch. There are several problems though: all the different story arcs have similar structure and become repetitive after a while: new faction is introduced -> initial conflicts arise -> big battle -> troublemakers are defeated, moderate parts join Slime-sama and get an upgrade. The show peaks midway during the orc invasion arc and cannot infuse its story with new ideas, tension or excitement afterwards. 
Pacing is like a boulder rolling down a hill. Early episodes can be considered as slow, but they do a great job at introducing the viewer to characters and world with its mechanics, while you crave for more when end creddits roll. As the story progresses, pacing becomes faster and faster; episodes in the second half turn into random events loosely hold together, not a cohesive story with a hook for more slimy content.
The way characters are treated fuels this displeasure further. 

CHARACTERS: A one slime show.
Slime-sama is an OP character, he will solve every problem with ease, win every battle and befriend everyone, but does not necessary take the good karma option on every occasion. Blue blob just enjoys his newfound life and does whatever he wants. The show also manages to transfer his joy, optimism or euphory onto the viewer. As an escapism power fantasy projection, this character works exceptionally well and fulfills its purpose.
Rimaru collects countless colorful followers. Each time a new group is introduced, those new characters will get a short backstory and a name to segregeta them from faceless redshirts. Fullstop. Expect no further development, as focus shifts with each new arc, older characters have to move to the background and remain frozen in the established master – subordinate relationship, thus there are no deeper character arcs or any development. Furthermore, this is a one man (slime) show, because everyone else is a support character and is defined through interactions with Rimuru. The show could use at least one character, who walks besides Rimaru, not behind him. 

ART & ANIMATION: I could not imagine a blue blob could look this good. 
This show looks good. Character models are detailed, colorful, interesting and stay on model for the entire run; backgrounds utilize a washed-up art style, but can express enough diversity, detail or create beatiful vistas and fit nicely into the slime world. 
Animations are crisp and enhance not only fights, but also mundane everyday scenes. Slime itself looks especially gorgeous with funny grimaces or little details, like dog ears and tail attachements when Rimaru transforms from wolf into a slime in ep2. Kudos to the animators. This is how you fill a seemingly expressionless character with charisma and offer an upgrde from paper onto blue screen, I am looking at you Edgelord Bones & Goblin Scrappypants. 

SOUND: Applause to all voice actors.
OP, ED as well as background music are nothing extraordinary, especially the later one is entirely unnoticeable. 
On the other hand, all the voice actors did a fantasic job and filled every character with soul and joy. It is obvious how much fun people had during recordings and this positive atmosphere is transferred directly into the characters and finally the viewer.

Tensei Slime is a prime example how a show can be, if everyone gives their best. Sadly, even the best production team cannot go beyound the boundaries set up by its source material.

As the final (also a filler) episode quoted: "Ignorance is bliss in this world," TenSura for me is another junkfood anime. It is another power-tripping, escapism story. It was entertaining at first, but after the addition of the ogres to Rimuru's forces, I've realized that every episode are just copies of the same episode. Every character are just a rehash from the same source. I can understand that Rimuru has the actual potential to be the powerful being that he is, but the story did not even show how he did. If one argues that what makes TenSure great is not about his powers butfor the nation-building and world building, then I'd argue that those aspects are subpar, or at most average. Every character and conflicts involved with them are simply shrugged off by first being overpowered by Rimuru, and then exalt him as the Great Rimuru. I do not feel any weight in the story or characters at all. There are some parts that I felt something different. Shizu's story is a good contrast to the overall story. It's much more compelling, and I would have liked it if it has been explored more. Although these parts still give off the same annoying blind praise to Shizu.

There are other isekai lightnovels that showed great world building and making connections to other nations. Mushoku Tensei is of another level in this aspect, and now it is getting an adaptation, it has been quite late.

Alright, first of all lemme say that this is what is saving the Isekai genre. All the isekais in the year before this have been absolute garbage. like death march, isekai wa smartphone, etc. It's been giving the isekai genre a bad name and the isekai genre is a really popular genre. If you read manga like me you would know how fucking popular it is; it even has its own genre in manga. Now what makes Reincarnated as a Slime different from other isekais? Well first of all, it breaks the cliches of other isekais. The anime isabout this middle-aged man who gets stabbed and dies. He then reincarnated into another world with overpowered powers (cliched) but he is reincarnated as a Slime! Also wanna add how the first episode is already enough to engage watchers to become heavily interested.
 
    What makes this anime not cliched is the fact that most of the characters are so unique and interesting. The MC, Rimuru Tempest, is a lot different from other MCs. He is funny character who treats everyone he meets nicely. And what I mean by that is he tries to make friends with literally everyone. Everytime an enemy strikes Rimuru will defeat them and then invite them to join his village. And speaking of the village, Rimuru's goal at the start of the anime was to find a way to break the seal of Veldora the dragon. Rimuru then starts a civilization with goblins. This eventually expands and becomes more "modernized" and included many races, all which came from races that Rimuru has helped or have been attacked from. Have you ever had a moment when you realize that the time you spent on something was actually just wasting your life? This is not a quote from the show, but from myself after seeing the 20-something-th episode. Usually a story, be it anime, manga, comic, movie, book..., means something to learn, an experience to enjoy, a relaxation method, a fun time, a way to escape from ordinary life... whatever. This one here is one to force you to reasses the life choices that have lead you to seeing it. Tl;dr: just a bad anime. Too much fan service takes away any developement of the story,already made impossible by an unbearably broken protagonist. Unless that is what you're looking for, I would recommend almost any other isekai I've seen before this one.

It is my first time writing a review here, and I'll try to avoid spoilers, but some minor ones might slip here and there. So let's get to it. The story starts as in any standard isekai: we have our lonely protagonist having acomplished not much in life just existing there as the standard not-very-social anime protagonist. He is stabbed and proceeds to die. To his surprise he is reincarnated, but not in the traditional way. Rather, he finds himself inhabiting the body of a slime. This twist of originality leads us to belive that this is going to be a different kind of isekai: maybe one taking the satire and humurous approach to it? Maybe a critique to the genre? Maybe just an original and fresh one? And as a concept and as an idea I have to say it's great, so much so that it is also the main reason why its score is 3 and not -2. 

Sadly, from here on it is all downhill. To start with, let's talk about how *** broken the protagonist is. And I'm not talking about how overpowered he is, having no problem dealing with any physical obstacle be it a monster or a human. That alone could have been something to work with. It is an interesting concept to develop. The problem is that they obviously do not develop nor work with it. He is obviously invencible but he'll pretend he is not time and time again just for the sake of it. But that's no all. He's also broken as a character. Once he becomes a slime the standard not-very-social anime protagonist also dies with his previous body. And the thing gets so absolutely absurd that he goes on and does not make a single mistake in the entire series (at least that I can remember, and of course I'm not gonna rewatch it, if you were to suggest it). It goes beyond plot armor, he is just God or something. Talking powerful people into being by his side? No problem! Designing an entire city from scratch? Also not a problem. Adquiring international recognition for a nation of monsters, when for some reason they we're not recognised before despite being de facto one (or rather, many) and having the social and political structures to be considered one? Sure, he didn't even have to put effort into it because the other nations' leaders came to him!

And this leads us to the next big flaw of it: just the whole story. It just exists to deliver fan service, despite their best efforts to desguise it as whatever it its. Let's dive a bit into it nontheless. The basic premise that apparently the protagonist strives to achieve is to creat a peaceful nation in this new world where monsters, humans, and everyone can be happy and he can relax and enjoy life. Okay seems legit, why the apparently? Because it's contradiction time! Sure let's build this paradise of acceptance but I'm gonna say to every big shot I fight "It is kill or be killed, kiddo", and because of how broken the story is they will join me afterwards regardless. And I don't want to get into politics BUT if the nation you are going to create is of authoritarian and militaristic nature, why desguise it as something else? It is an interesting concept on its own nontheless but it feels completely out of place when inserted into the story. But worry not because the protagonist is just going to abandon it mid-series to go teach because a girl he has known for like a few days told him.

Ah and sure, as we have no defined clear villain, let's just spit here and there some words about Demon Lords with a few shoots of shady characters that will never be properly introduced or, in some cases, we'll even don't know who are we being shown. Don't let the developement of a story get in the way between you and more fan service. 

Overall, it is an anime to be avoided, unless you really like isekai and you just want a bit of fan service without much else into it. While the art and the sound are pretty standard: not bad, not outstanding; the good premise the story starts with is just wasted in not-at-all developed characters (except for few exceptions), a broken protagonist and an horrible depelopement of the story itself which ends up being just dreadful.

Never in my life have I been so disappointed with an anime. [MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD]When I first started watching this anime, I thought it was great. The concept was awesome and the first episode had a pretty enthralling hook. I was sure that this would be an anime I would look back on with love and affection. The initial high of the first episode was great. But holy shit, it was a mad rush downhill from there.

I have a few things with this anime that I would like to discuss, namely: Rimuru's potions, characters, enemies, pacing, plot and general repetition.

First item on the list, Rimuru's potions. These potions are severely overused and essentially allow the main character's friends and comrades to rarely die or suffer any major consequences for fighting whatsoever. This gives every fight the feel that it doesn't really matter and removes any tension that you might feel during said fight. 

Second item on the list, the characters. Some of the characters in this anime were well thought-out and deep. An example of this is Satoru Mikami, a character who is flawed, but who also has his strengths. Sadly, this is the end of the list of good characters that come to mind, as the remainder of them are shallow and seem to only serve the purpose of filling out the ranks. The creators of this anime seem to have focused on quantity rather than quality, constantly introducing multiple characters at a single time and not bothering to give them any depth. Looking at them now, more than 65% of the characters could have been completely cut from the show without any adverse effects whatsoever. The lack of strong supporting characters is made even more unbearable by the protagonist being a Mary Sue and falling into the cliché of being nice because nice people are nice. 

The third item on my list is perhaps the biggest one for me personally. The enemies. Oh my god the enemies. The show devotes a decent amount of effort into alluding towards a huge threat that’s looming over the protagonist but fails to ever deliver, leaving an unfulfilling taste in the viewer’s mouth and a desire for something of any consequence to happen. The conflict that does occur seems to materialize itself out of thin air, as if the creators finally realised that nothing had happened for 6 episodes and had a panic attack, quickly drawing up an idea for some large thing to get set up for half an episode, then promptly get defeated before you can take a sip of your coffee. Lovely. It’s really disheartening for me to see an anime with such amazing potential and a great hook fizzle out into a big nothing-burger. 

The fourth item on my list is pacing, which tends to be closely tied in with the third and fourth items, but still deserves its own listing. This show has some serious issues with pacing. On the one hand, they spend an entire episode on one character’s death, and on the other, they only spend one episode on defeating a giant evil monster that’s been slumbering for 1000 years or whatever. These major issues combined with the first item on my list leave a supremely bitter taste in my mouth, as the characters involved don’t suffer any losses or damages when defeating ‘super evil villain with the power to destroy the planet #45’.

The fifth item on my list is the plot. While the concept of the anime is truly outstanding, the execution is what I would call piss-poor. One particularly jarring event of this occurring happens a little past the 2/3 mark of the series and features the main character completely fucking off from the place that the entire plot has revolved around and doing his own thing for someone that he knew for a single day and who died many episodes prior. I wouldn’t have minded this if it had been for a character I cared about, but, going back to characters for a second, the character that the protagonist was doing it for was one that hadn’t been well developed at all. And the plot largely revolves around this poorly-written and ill thought out character, constantly revisiting her 3 episodes of relevance.

This brings me to my sixth and final point, repetition. This was probably the most annoying part of this anime to me, as it is an egregious insult to the viewer’s intelligence. The way they repeat things over and over makes me think that the creators of the anime believe their viewers to have an attention span of less than a goldfish. Multiple pivotal plot mechanics are reiterated a multiplicity of times throughout the course of the anime and it really makes me feel a sense of contempt towards the creators.

In closing, I was extremely excited to watch this anime at first, as I had heard some good things about it. The sound and art were both good, but the plot and deeper concepts of the shows production were insanely lacking in both function and depth. I really wanted to like this anime, but the more I watched, the more I began to despise it.

Thanks for reading and hope you stay safe fellow anime lovers. Minty Out.

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is one of those Isekai that paves the way for others to follow. When talking about good Isekai its important to understand what makes certain series better than others, why do some shows see so much praise and success and others seem to become the laughing stock of the anime community? In my mind the 2 most important things are Originality and Execution. Firstly, Slime does not feel ultra generic. It absolutely feels like its own story and exists separately from the rest of the slop that tends to get pushed out every year. While there are elements of fan-service andother things that are generally found throughout the Genre, Slime never feels like it uses those elements in a way that its overdone or overused. And as I mentioned earlier, it feels like Slime will largely pave the way for other shows to follow, as the Genre evolves you will find other shows take and mould ideas that feel uniquely Slime related.


Secondly is execution, and this is a no-brainier. Slime has some absolutely excellent animation, which is easy enough to point to. Something that I think isn't talked about enough is the sound design (Which is even better in Season 2) which goes a long way in improving the overall experience. It can be hard to point to other shows where this same idea is as prevalent, however I think the most obvious is JoJo, where not only the music but the fights have excellent sound design. I think some people may disagree? In my mind however the way that its done is fantastic and helps build on the hype of action scenes, and in some cases even the slower moments.


I'd also like to talk about the voice-acting. I think its pretty great, with some caveats. For people watching based on a recommendation, I worry that some people will find Rimuru's voice a bit annoying. Which in some cases can be a bit of a turn-off. Although once you get some ways into the first season it absolutely grows on you, and by the time you get to the second season your already 100% there anyway.


In all, Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is absolutely a Genre defining series that really does deserves the praise and continuation its received. I'm also excited for the third season to air, so look forward for that!

Rimuru is a great character that shows a few trace aspects of his old life, but more than anything serves as a reference point for explaining the world to the audience.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime completely exceeded my expectations. I gave it a 9/10 because it nails that perfect balance between world building, action, comedy, and feel good storytelling. What starts off as a quirky premise, an average guy reincarnated as a slime, quickly turns into an epic, character driven journey full of charm and depth. Rimuru, our gooey protagonist, is one of the most lovable main characters in the isekai genre. He’s powerful, yes, but it’s his kindness, diplomacy, and desire to build a peaceful society that really make him stand out. Watching him grow from a literal blob into a respectedleader who unites monsters, humans, and even demons is both exciting and satisfying.

The animation is clean, the cast is diverse and fun, and the pacing keeps you hooked without ever feeling too heavy. Whether you’re an isekai veteran or just dipping your toes into the genre, Slime is a must-watch that brings both heart and humor in equal measure.
