That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Monster Politician/Tycoon. That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime is one of those rare light novel isekai's that I can honestly say I enjoy. The premise is in the light novel title, 37 year old Satoru Mikami is reincarnated into a Dragony Questy type world as a slime after a random stabbing attack and becomes immediately over powered after meeting, befriending and eating an ancient, sealed, tsundere true dragon called Veldora and receiving the name Rimuru Tempest. What comes next is a much more interesting story starting with helping a goblin village survive a dire wolf pack torecruiting other races to help them rebuild their village which then escalates to founding a nation. 

Studio 8bit must of had a lot of fun animating Rimuru in his slime form. He is very bouncy and squishy and it's very satisfying to watching him traverse the land and transform between that and his human form which he gets later in the serious. Rimuru is also a great character. Being a former 37 year old who has worked in construction and who has lived an adult life with adult reasoning abilities makes him far more interesting to watch build a nation and to problem solve political situations rather than a 14 year old, meek, high school loser who got hit by truck-kun and doesn't know what he/she is doing. His passive personality means that disputes are settled with words rather than conflict, but when conflict does happen studio 8bit really makes sure the battles are explosive and satisfying with great animation and amazing sound design to give the magic some "oof".

The world building is solid and explained well. The lore behind summoning humans from our world  in order to create weapons for other kingdoms military is interesting and I like the way the author uses this to connect Shizu who's from a different ( and very fiery) time period of Japan to Rimuru. I also like the way demon lords are handled. They're more a class of intelligent monster rather than a single evil entity which is refreshing and can lead to some interesting interacts. 
Of course this is a light novel adaptation so there is some fan service indulgences here and there, but not enough to turn anyone away who doesn't like that sort of thing. Though some might be a bit turned off by Milim's design even if she is one of the best characters. 

My only real complaints would be the way order of events are structured towards the end of the season and the final episode which I think is a filler episode for some reason? This episode makes the skimming over of some important plot details unjust and throws off the overall good pacing. 

I do think the manga is the best way to enjoy the story of slime, but that doesn't mean I discount the anime entirely. In fact I encourage you to watch it. It's a very enjoyable story that at it's core is about finding a place of belonging amongst those who are different from you and it has some genuinely moving moments. I was cutting onions during episode 8. 

There are times where I come back to Slime just watch an episode or two because I like it that much. It's a good, city building anime with great characters and lot's to enjoy.

I really enjoyed the story and the overall execution of the anime. The plot is engaging, and the characters are interesting and well-developed. However, I found that using negative names like “Diablo” or “Belzebul” for characters who are actually good can be confusing and might create discomfort for some viewers. I think replacing these names with more neutral or positive terms like “monster” could make the anime more accessible and enjoyable for a wider audience. The frequent use of “demon” for kind characters felt a bit off, although the word “oni” didn’t bother me at all. The character Mirlin (Lorde) had an early scene that focusedon her underwear, which seemed a little superficial. As the story progressed, her wardrobe and character portrayal became more appropriate, making her eccentric personality more enjoyable and likable.

Overall, I loved the anime and the world it presents. These small adjustments—especially with names and terms for good characters—could help the show appeal even more to western audiences while preserving the essence of the story.

Tensei Slime is a pretty fun watch. It's a generally light-hearted story, a power fantasy with a really endearing protagonist and a plethora of cool side characters. This anime has its moments of drama, vengeance, even tragedy, but its overall tone is definitely of the "everything will be okay!" kind, and it's such a breath of fresh air. There's a reason why this anime specifically has a popular slice-of-life spin-off, where literally nothing happens and you're just there to watch the characters have fun. Still, that's not to take away from the actual story of this world. The story doesn't shy away from somewhat darker themes.Characters have tragic backstories or circumstances, and on very rare occasions, even the "good guys" can die. Not everything is fine and dandy, though it's easy to forget that when you're watching Rimuru messing around with his friends. The story balances comedy and fun with drama and suspense very well, and the plot is constantly moving forward so that you'll always be entertained by something.

Rimuru and his friends are also fun to watch. They're likeable and entertaining, despite not being super nuanced. The character designs are mostly distinct and interesting, save for a few character design downgrades that were probably made to appeal to a wider audience (i.e. fanservice) and make it easier for the animators to draw regular humans. It's a shame, but not a complete deal breaker.

Oh, also, the animation and sound design is excellent. Enough said.

Tensei Slime is a fun isekai featuring a rare breed called 'OP protagonist who doesn't let the power get to his head'. Just try not to think too hard about the story, sit back, and enjoy the show.

This show is a light novel that has a very straightforward story and as is advertised from its title lmao; It's a decent time-passer of a show in my opinion but if we're gonna have to be objective and look at it on the lens of how 'impactful' this show was I would have to say it was very generic overall (considering its a fantasy-isekai too). Is it worth the watch? I am not really sure. Its entertaining for what it is but some people may think its a waste of time and that may be valid. Btw this review constitutes all of the seasonsit has produced.

Animation (5/10) - Honestly, I don't think it was terrible. Very standardized for its time and goes out of its way to surpass its standards every now and then on some important fight scenes or certain scenes that has plot heft. Its coloring is also vibrant a lot of the times, which really helps on ability and setting definition, so props to that as one of its standout definitions. But overall? I think it was alright for what it was.

Storyline (5/10) - Considering how there are so many isekais are out there, let's just lay it out as it is: It's not the most original concept of all time. Average guy dies and transformed into a a mythical entity on another timeline that has limitless potential for growth. It's a blueprint that's kind of 'common' dare I say. And the way he also powerscales is also very steady through the course of time which leads to having no plot challenges and just him becoming very OP eventually.

It's just him basically taking over the world he spawned at and a lot of the times, the thrill just come from his subordinates getting stuck at the jaws of defeat/trouble and will just simply put a closer with him stepping in to save them. So for me, I thought it was very mild not gonna lie.

Music (5/10) - Their audio library also meets no difference. It was entirely made to cater to the storyline and nothing too groundbreaking or catchy in my opinion (like Kana Boon's tracks for Naruto or King Gnu for JJK). Just mostly instrumentals that creates the ambiance alike to fantasy RPGs. Although props to their track "Like Flames" by AmarLee and "Sorrow". I think it was one of their better songs they have created and it was a vibe lmao.

But overall, I guess the most accurate way to describe this is "mediocre" and the best way is "alright".

Overall - 5 out of 10

I'll not write a separate review for both season. I just get it over with here. What is this show all about. In sort: A middle-aged office worker reincarnated as a ridiculously OP slime. His goal is basically to bounce to the world peace. Ok, ok, in reality he just wants to establish a peaceful kingdom, but we all know where this is going. This show is too lighthearted to be honest. If you want any realism look elsewhere. It feels like it was written by a child... I mean there is no conflict here. Everybody forgive everything (and by everything I mean basically a genocide). Friendshipsforming out of nowhere and so on. Everything goes the way out as our resident slime wants it.

There was a moment in the 2nd season when it looked like there will be a tone change and the carelessness will have some consequence finally, but in the same scene it was magically resolved... So no worries there is not much nail-biting here.

The story itself is quite shallow, and episodic. Nothing much to mention here honestly. Don't look for deep message or meanings. You won't have sleepless night after you watched it.

However what I wrote so far is not neccessary a bad thing. Sometimes we just want a little fun, and this is exactly the right state of mind to watch this show.

So let's talk about the good part. Pretty much all the characters are loveable even though most of them are cardboard cutouts. So yeah if you prefer well-written interesting characters then this is not the show you are looking for. However I think they were fine for their purpose.

Visually in my opinion this is quite nice work, however in the past few years this quality is pretty standard. I don't think an anime needs to be look better than this though. So I'm not complainging.

There is quite a lot of fight scene (this is a power fantasy after all), and they were well animated. The animation conveyed the sense of speed, power and weight really well. One of the best example is the scene where Geld fought with Shogo (if I remember his name correctly) with bare hand.

I rarely talk about it, but the strongest aspect of the show was actually the sounds. The sounds effect were amazing, which further enhanced the already good fight scenes. I'm not sure if I ever felt this much power behind each punch, sword crossing or magic just by hearing it. Top notch work. 

So all in all pretty shallow, but fun to watch show with a few jokes you can laugh on.

Another anime in the wide family of isekais. The question is then: Does it bring anything new or interesting to the genre? The answer is no. Breakdown: - Art: 9/10 Let's start with a good point, fights were very pleasant to watch, from choreographs to effects. I'm not a good judge of art, but that was good enough for me, even exceeded a few expectations. - Sound: 5/10 For this one I'm biased, despite trying hard I still cannot stand the vast majority of anime music. Little girls shouting in a microphone is not pleasant to my ears. However, ambient music and sounds were alright, skip intro andending if you're like me.

- Characters: 3/10
The main issue in this anime. Main protagonist was resurrected and transmigrated from another universe, this isekai hero is just like any other isekai hero: Overpowered, hardly relatable with, his anterior life is irrelevant, not adding any value to the story. Worse, while the character was a grown up man in their original world, their psychology is completely morphed into that of a teen girl for the sake of matching appearance.
Regarding the rest of the cast, except for a few somewhat interesting characters, we have our usual harem of super-badass, ultra-dedicated, huge-breasted females swarming around the hero. Shall I repeat... Boring?

- Story: 2/10
World with magic, kingdoms, beasts, demons, main character surrounds himself with tons of large-breasted allies, gets unexpected favors constantly and Deux Ex Machina every 3 episodes... Boring.

- Enjoyment: 5/10 
Fully unplug your brain, and you may have some fun.
That's what I hoped, but on my part this little voice in my head "this is nonsense", "seen that... that too", "doesn't make sense at all" wouldn't be quiet, due to the very low quality of the story and characters.

Overall: 5/10
While watching these 24 episodes was a complete waste of time in terms of enrichment, discovering interesting stories and universes, it does offer some enjoyment and has a few, rare redeeming qualities, mostly fights. 
Hence if your only alternative is to stare at a blank wall, you may prefer watching this anime. You may.

I had initially given this anime so much credit because it was balancing two difficult things: the need to differentiate itself from the over-saturated Isekai genre and 2) having an OP main character. However, one comment said that the anime wasn't really about the character himself, but about the reactions to him. The appeal of the Isekai genre is to give the viewer a relatable lens to a fantasy world, but the twist for this anime is that we not only get that, but also a fantastical predicament in the world itself as an assumed low level slime defies everyone's expectations by turning out tobe far more capable than they thought. 

I did enjoy the anime, but I am going to refrain from recommending it since there were some issues while viewing it, and I think the recent efforts it's taking with its plot is making it collapse under its own weight. 

The initial theme of the show became one of world building and peaceful relations among different species, which began as the Slime had accidentally caused a power vacuum within the region, and then worked to correct this. However, the Slime also had a desire to find other's who may have been brought into this world who were also from his homeland of Japan. He does find one, but ends up adopting her ideals, leading him to temporarily leave the settlement and characters we've grown to love for the past 19 episodes. Apparently, episodes 20-24 are not filler, which makes me fear the anime's future direction as it is a clear departure from what has been developing. 

As I said before, this anime isn't really about the main character, but the world around him, and it was a huge mistake to isolate him into a different part of the world with a different objective and expect viewers to still be interested. I may return for Season 2, as there are still so many characters that I love from the show, but I'd rather you avoid it in case it crashes and burns, as I have already skipped plenty of boring episodes already.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime is a show I know had a lot of hype surrounding it. I definitely want to say I didn't hate the first chunk of the show. It was yet another isekai to add to the list in quite an over saturated market for these types of shows. I was worried I'd hate it but I actually found it very pleasant and enjoyable. But suddenly by like episode 12 or 13 I fell off the bandwagon and felt kind of bored. It became a very generic fantasy anime that really didn't do anything new or exciting. I feltas thought the characters went from fun and enjoyable to suddenly over powered or just paper thin dull. The show just kind of fell into the meh pile for me. I felt like I wanted more and something unique but I just kind of felt underwhelmed by how average and indifferent I felt. I watched some of the show dubbed but not all of it because the dub was pretty bad and the translation was really cringe. I could tell that wasn't the original story dialogue and was bad localization. I didn't let that affect my score. It's definitely a show I preferred subbed. Anyways, when there is an isekai a minute I feel exhausted from shows like this. That does add a bit of a bias to my rating probably but I definitely have been invested in some really awesome isekai anime that have really made the concept a lot of fun. This show just feels more of the same. It has the MMORPG feeling and interface the character uses and it's in a generic fantasy landscape. It's nice to see how a slime can build and rule a town and how it accomplishes so much, but this show loses it's flavor and became less and less interesting as the show continued for me. If this show does interest you I definitely say to check it out regardless of how I feel since we all have different interests and taste. It seems a lot of people enjoy this show. For me I'm glad I watched it but I'm not compelled to read the light novel or continue to follow this series unless it pulls something truly amazing that gets the community buzzing.

I didn't want to find the anime adaptation of a manga I loved being total crap. The reason I find the anime adequate is because well..I don't think its an absolutely terrible adaptation, its just not doing the manga or light novel justice. So why did I make this review? Well.. I just would like to clarify a little bit since I see a lot of terrible reviews for this show. I know I'm being biased but hopefully I can change some of you guys thoughts on this.

If you don't want to have to read a long ass review, the summary is that the show is not meant to be all amazing world building, plot and epic action filled adventure that injects you with a large dose of adrenaline per episode. Or at least in the manga per chapter. I mean episode 23 ended on i think chapter 50 something in the manga. And if what was mentioned in the other reviews are right (with the amount of people mentioning this issue.. i know this is fact), there are a lot of fan service scenes which deter a lot of viewers. Many mentions how the show is basically a huge harem plot where chicks are attracted to a slime. Ok fair enough, an acceptable argument. The issue i see here is that maybe its just me.. but i dont think there are a lot of fan service moments in the manga. I'm not denying that there isn't any.. but not so much that it hinders the story and makes you think its just a fan service-ing series.

Now in light of this.. I feel that maybe the anime increases the amount of said scenes, further reducing the amount of screen time proper, more relevant scenes can get in a single episode. Not to mention they have to cram 2 whole chapters into a single episode (assuming they don't have any episode that only covers 1 chapter), thats kinda tight to make a compelling story.

So why do I think of this despite not having watched the entire series? Again.. this is based on the reviews I've been seeing. Now to make things clear, I am not in anyway saying the other reviews are wrong, I'm just giving my two cents on this topic is all since I don't want other MAL lurkers that don't read the manga or LN to come see the review section and decided not to give this series a try. OK? Alright? Good. Let's start.

Based on what I've been reading, many seems to have very superficial understandings and information of the overall story. Be it the characterization of each well uh.. characters, and/or overall world building. A great example would be the Demon Lord Millim Nava. A review mentions her as a disaster class being that got done in by freaking candy (or honey to be more accurate). Well first of all, she is a cut above disaster, she is catastrophe class. A demon ranking so high up and rare that with the very few number of beings that can be categorized as one, the entire world just decided to not make it an official class. So far in the story there are only 2 known catastrophe class: Millim and Veldora. Ok, next. If you think that Rimuru defeating Millim with honey is BS.. Well, it kinda is BS.. But it makes sense. I mean I'm a fan of the series and all, but there is just no way Rimuru at that time and even later in the story (by later i mean waaay later like, 'not even the manga has caught up to the LN' later) he still wouldn't be able to beat Millim. If you can't beat 'em, join 'em. Or in this case.. gain their favour.

Now u all askin right? But lol he just fed her honey why did his followers applauded him like he did something crazy? Ughh unless didn't you read the paragraph above, i mentioned how Millim is a special being, so terrifyingly powerful that she can practically destroy KINGDOMS if she felt like it. Emphasis on the S. More than 1. Ok? Her strength is infamous throughout the world as she is a cute little girl with pony tails that can stand toe to toe with the Storm Dragon Veldora, hailed as a freaking Guardian Deity by the monsters of the Great Jura Forest. Ok? Entire nations and kingdoms needed to think twice to invade nearby kingdoms because well.. a sealed Veldora happens to be there. Veldora's very existence deters nations from invading nearby kindoms. Think about it. Most monsters would just beg for their lives if the come across a wild Millim ready for battle. Him standing up to Millim in order to protect his subordinates is a feat in itself if you think about it. Oh and if you're thinking well.. his subordinates tried to fight millim. Well they're just dumb ok. They're just willing to sacrifice their live for Rimuru that was it. 

Another thing was how many characters were not very memorable. Well that's true in a way. There are so many cast member that it its difficult to keep track of them all. But can you blame them? By the end of the anime series, Rimuru had became the master and king of over 150 000 monsters. Don't forget other characters that are not affiliated or included in that 150k.

In the manga, character development of the casts were slow. But so was the pace of the plot. It was never meant to be fast. You were supposed to discover each cast personalities through the interactions they show between one another and with Rimuru. The story slowly but surely helps us peel off each layer of skin in a pace where, we didn't even notice the character development until you realize how much you've grown fond of a certain character. Maybe the anime didn't do a very good job at doing this, but hey I gave my argument earlier right. Of another thing I noticed with the anime adaptation, is that they change the dialog a bit.. You know what? Scratch that, they change a lot of the dialog. I mean, the adding entire lines to what the characters are saying in a particular scene. Well, I didn't read the Light Novels so I don't know whether I am wrong about this.. but at least in the manga there was far less irrelevant dialog.

Now the enemies are a bit of a pushover yes. Seeing as Rimuru practically solo's most of them (except Millim technically but eh). The thing is in this part of the story at least Rimuru wasn't meant to fight impossible like villains yet. This is a section where we were given an idea of the power balance in the world currently (like the demon lord keeping each other in check for example), Rimuru's overall character and him realizing that he couldn't save everyone despite being all powerful and trying to work slowly into this albeit vague goal of his by slowly learning how to be a proper leader, the personalities of the other characters, etc.

Well there are more arguments I'd like to give but they're a bit out there so lets just leave it at that. Basically:

1. the anime is giving out waay too much fan service when compared to the manga. This is very sad for me because I feel that it would do so much better without them.

2. The dialog were changed to accommodate the fan servicing model, and unfortunately not for the better. I honestly don't think the anime studio understands the characters properly when adding new dialog and/or choosing dubbers. Maybe its just me, but when I'm reading the manga, the voice I have inside my head that represent each cast, isn't found on this anime adaptation.

3. I think why many anime only watchers dislikes Rimuru as a character is well.. he seems perverted. Like your typical harem main protagonist. I'm not saying he's not, but the anime seems to exaggerates i feel like. It's not that he's perverted, more like normal(?) He has his urges and is interested in women in general. Despite this, he seems.. normal for a guy i feel. In the anime for example, back to the Millim Nava vs Rimuru scene as an example. Rimuru mentions about Millim being flat, while checking her body out. This isn't found on the manga (idk about the Light Novel). You know they add things like this. And there are many scenes where the female kijins holds Rimuru underneath their breast right. And as he speaks the kijin's plot would jiggles. At least in the anime adaptation. While reading the manga, I do notice him having plots resting on his body, but never did it seem perverted? IDK how to explain this properly but I hope you get my point.

4. The plot is meant to be slow and steady, thus requiring more screen time for each scene and/or character. The overall addition of the new dialog and fan service does not help.

5. Finally, I'm giving the adaptation a 6.5/10 since I am disappointed at the adaptation, but on the other hand i kinda expected this. So to all of you that didn't like the anime, please i implore you to try reading the manga at least. To me at least, the manga is faaar more enjoyable to go through.

Anyway, thats it for my review y'all, thanks for reading such a long as essay.

Pretty fun! I'll admit that I was apprehensive at first, since the first few episodes appeared to repeat the same loop of Rimuru coming across a situation and handling it easily, and while I can't say the show ever stops doing that, they manage to twist the formula in interesting ways so the experience is never boring. I think this show might have some of the best sound design I've ever heard in an anime, as well. Every sound effect is delivered with a weight and emotion appropriate for the situation, be it the Great Sage's electronic processing, the thunderous crack of Rimuru's black lightning, orsimply the calming ambience of the Jura Forest. It all packs an appropriate punch, as does the music which supplies tracks for both goofy hijinks and moments of extreme hype. It sounds like a typical action-comedy anime soundtrack, but by implementing some synth sounds, it manages to stand apart from its contemporaries.

If I had to pinpoint my major issue with this season, it would have to be the apparent absence of real stakes. Of course, there's plenty of incomprehensibly huge beasts that threaten the world as we know it to contend with, but more often than not, these antagonists are swiftly dealt with by Rimuru. Having an overpowered protagonist is fine of course - many other anime follow this same trope to great effect - but it doesn't always feel like Rimuru faces any other kind of challenges that pose a serious threat to him. I'm not talking about being in physical danger, however. Rather, if Rimuru is supposed to be this insane, unbeatable force, then I'd also enjoy seeing him tackle some interesting ethical issues, perhaps by presenting him with a few difficult choices to make as both the leader of a nation and in an internal sense. I'd love to see Rimuru mess up somehow by making a bad call, and then seriously interrogate his way of thinking. I don't necessarily expect anything heart-wrenching or whatever, since I know this show is aiming for a more chilled-out tone. As it stands, Rimuru is able to solve every problem presented to him, be it physical or psychological, and he's always rewarded with constant praise and adoration from his subordinates. That's fine, but a little unengaging, and I hope this changes in the future somewhat.

Let's be honest, getting reincarnated in a fantasy RPG world is a played out and severely overused theme in Anime. It's completely uncreative at this point, yet, studios keep going back to the SAO well because it's hard to come up with fresh new ideas in anime and as long as something is popular among audiences, they're going to ride it until the wheels fall off. And so, we are introduced to yet another anime of this ilk in Tensura. If you've seen any anime in this genre at all before, SAO, Log Horizon, Konosuba, etc... Then you've seen Tensura. AndTensura brings all of the things that make those animes likable: Good action, a good comedy (Although Konosuba is far funnier) and an interesting and large crew.  

However, Tensura has made its crew too large, too quickly, and so most characters are kind of just "there".  Even ones with really good potential to be epic characters like the Ogres, Gobuta and Millim.  The crew is so big, that outside of a handful of characters, most don't get any significant lines to really build themselves up after their particular arcs are over.  It's kind of frustrating, because I really like a lot of these characters.  

The whole pace of the anime just moves too quickly for the viewer to become invested in anything as they should, so the anime feels like there's nothing at stake.  Especially since Rimuru is basically Saitama in terms of being OP.  Pretty much one move, three at most, and any threat is finished.   

This anime has a really good foundation, and the introduction of Kuro seems like Rimuru may finally have a real challenge, but going into future seasons, Tensura would benefit greatly from slowing the pace down and building up some emotional investment from arc to arc.  It would also benefit from giving more time to the cast that it continues to introduce and integrate into Rimuru's city.  Allow the viewer to get to know one group of characters for a while, before introducing more and pushing them to the back burner.  Characters like Benimaru, Souei, Millim and Gobuta could benefit from more screen time, before you introduce Chloe, Kuro and the Queen of Spirits.  

Still, Tensura is a fun anime to watch.  Smooth fight animations, some nice comedic moments, an entertaining cast, etc...  It's a not a bad anime at all.  It could just be better with more investment in the cast and introducing some kind of overarching serious threat that creates some kind of suspense in the anime.  As it stands now, no matter what Charbydis type create shows up, it'll be handled with ease and no sacrifice.  That drags the anime down.   

Hopefully it will improve going forward in these regards.

There's a very specific kind of enjoyment which you can get from Reincarnated as a Slime, and the best comparison I can make - which might explain that enjoyment - is to time-loop movies. Movies like The Edge of Tomorrow or Source Code focus on an initially-incompetent protagonist being repeatedly put through the same sequence of events in the same place and trying to achieve some kind of goal. At the beginning, the protagonist repeatedly fails or dies because they don't know what's coming next. But eventually, they begin to map out the possibilities and anticipate the events in their reality, and figures out thebest way to get through the obstacles, or the right thing to do at the right time, in order to succeed. And at the point that the protagonist has finally managed to git gud, you get a vicarious sense of enjoyment from watching them.

That's pretty much what Slime is like, except, crucially, without the first part - which is to say, the part where the protagonist actually struggles. This basically turns the anime into a weirdly fun, oddly amusing journey through a fairly stereotypical isekai setting where the protagonist constantly makes the right choices, level-grinds (so to speak) in order to get all the powerful abilities he needs to consistently destroy his opponents, makes the right alliances to build up his kingdom, etc. If he was some kind of stereotypically handsome cool guy, this would probably be really annoying, but he's a literal slime, so it just becomes oddly funny to watch him take over a goblin village and turn it into a built-up town which is home to a multi-species coalition, or to befriend a legendary storm dragon just by being around and not being scared to talk to him. 

If this sounds undistinguished and like it might be kind of boring, that's because it probably would be, which is why I decided to be fair and give it 5 out of 10. Certainly, after the entertaining early parts where Rimuru the Slime consistently wrecks every opponent he faces and becomes the founder of a new nation, there's a deeply shitty final arc where he has to babysit a bunch of annoying kids, which sucks. However, if you have nothing else to do and find isekai kind of annoying, it might be fun to watch a show where a super-powerful slime basically rampages through an isekai setting just by being smart, having a bunch of rare abilities, and using his common sense.

That Time I Reincarnated as a Slime (Slime) was the show I was not expecting anything out of and then it surprised me by being pleasantly good only to slowly burn all that goodwill away leaving me with what I expected at the start another generic isekia (a genre where the protagonist is whisked away to another world) show. Slime starts with how a lot of these shows do as an overworked salaryman is stabbed and murdered when he tries to defend a co-worker from a thief ( huh I guess Truck-kun must have been out sick for the day). He is then given the optionto reincarnate in another world and given some advantages that give him quite the edge against most of the denizens of his new world. After meeting with a mighty dragon named Valdora, they become friends and to free him from his imprisonment Rimaru ( the protagonist who is now a slime)absorbs him. This causes Valdora to disappear and creates a power vacuum in the forest where Rimaru has spawned. Rimaru comes upon some goblins and decides to help them.

From this point, the show turns into a lite kingdom building show. Which let me tell you if done right is one of my favorite genre's. But therein lies the problem. I much enjoyed much of the start where Rimeru starts a village, and it becomes more powerful and prosperous, but at the same time, it felt like the whole show was rushing to get through some story beats. This is problematic as a good kingdom building story needs a decent amount of time to explore the minutia of the process of starting a state. Slime is also the rare case where I have read the source material( keeping in mind I dropped it a ways back as I had caught up to the current issue of the light novel, but it never was enjoyable enough to go back and catch up) to know that they were skipping a lot of crucial details.  

As for the cast, Rimeru is a nice guy who tries to settle things amicably first in most scenarios. He was a reasonably exciting character to follow — the rest though not so much. No one was awful, but in that same vein, no one stuck out either. It has only been one day, and I have forgotten about most of them. I am sure I could tell you a detail or two but nothing that would make them memorable.

Animation wise Slime was nothing to write home about. In the sound department, it was the same nothing stuck out. The OP was good, but that was about all. 

All in all, Slime is going to be the show I forget about two weeks from now unremarkable in many ways. It is alright, but I would not recommend watching this show.

This show has two main parts: The combat + powerup stuff, and the dialogue sequences between characters. I don't think either of those parts work particularly well, although there's a slight upward trend in quality as the seasons go on (this review covers the first 3 seasons). The combat falls into the trap that many other anime fall into, namely that it devolves to characters taunting each other at length and announcing how powerful they are rather than actually clashing. Then, one side will attack and will either do no damage at all, or will instantly win the fight. If no damage was done, theother party will say something like "hahahaha didn't you know I have an everything-proof shield! Now it's my turn to attack!" Sometimes this goes on for several more rounds with each side using new abilities before one side can't pull out any more hidden moves and thus loses by default. I *hate* this style of anime action. There's no tension whatsoever, and it can't even be that stylish since the pacing keeps grinding to a halt. What's more, there are several "battles" where the good guys only want to "incapacitate" their enemies like it's a Saturday morning cartoon where they're bonking the enemy goons on the head to "knock them unconscious". These bits are so unrealistic and goofy that they always make my eyes roll. There's one exception to the boring/silly fights in the Megiddo episode where the protagonist Rimuru does a mass-execution and it's like "OK, are we actually doing something now?" but sadly it was a one-off. 

Rimuru is very overpowered which can be entertaining in and of itself if done correctly, like how Solo Leveling makes its MC's dominance feel genuinely satisfying and how it showcases flashy combat sequences. But this show doesn't do either of those consistently, and Rimuru himself actually only occasionally fights outside of the first half of S1. 

That leaves the dialogue, which is a mishmash of comedy bits, slice-of-life, and nation-building. The comedy is bad like it is in almost every anime, with far too much emphasis on characters simply overreacting to things, as if that's somehow a punchline by itself. Rimuru also uses a lot of millennial slang like "OMG that was totes awesome!" and "you're the bomb dot com!" that are painfully cringeworthy. The slice-of-life stuff is average at best -- this sort of thing really comes down to how much you like the characters, and this show spreads itself far too thin on that front. There's a nearly overwhelming deluge of side characters that creates a similar problem to S2 of Code Geass. There's just too many of them kicking around which leads to the vast majority of them being one-note. I kept getting the details of them mixed up and thinking to myself "What nation is this person from? Why are they upset?" Japan's comparative advantage in media has always been cute anime girls, and while this series has Milim and Shuna, they both get very little screentime since they're crammed in with the rest of the overcrowded cast. 

The nation-building stuff is fairly unique for an anime, with Rimuru's goal being to create a kingdom from the ground-up. In the first season this is pretty bad -- there's almost no internal pushback, all the implied racism between humans and monsters is instantly solved with no effort, and enemies are transformed into permanently loyal allies after 5 minutes of interacting with the MC. It all feels fake, like Rimuru's playing CK3 with all the cheat codes turned on. It improves moderately in S2 as other nations start plotting against the MC, and the show becomes a series of meetings as both sides try to outmaneuver each other. And this is a good thing! I've seen some people deride the show's choice to become meeting after meeting after meeting, but I think that's much more interesting than having a bunch of silly fight sequences. I would still prefer if there had been more internal pushback on Rimuru's plans, and the meetings themselves aren't nearly up to the level of, say, Game of Thrones' Small Council scenes, but they're still decent at least. Unfortunately it dips a bit towards the end, as the second half of S3 is just 4 and a half hours of the characters planning a big party. I presume this is meant to showcase how the economy of the nation will function, but it's done through slice-of-life scenes and meetings with no internal pushback again. 

As of now, this show is mediocre. If season 4 comes around and has more fights like Megiddo along with somewhat more compelling political machinations, then it could turn into something special.

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken -The one day a Slime started playing Sims- Another Isekai, this time the -Weak to Strong Route-, even if it is quickly skipped. In its approach, this Isekai probably contains all sorts of clichés from A to Z. Even the transition to the main topic felt like a comedy. In that regard, you couldn't even take the protagonist's death seriously. The joke was at least entertaining, the definition of "Please delete my browser history memes" I have to admit, however, that this Isekai is somewhat different from the others, in terms of characters and sympathetic implementation. Most of the characters are practically lovableand charismatic. And the world has been given a satisfactory world-building, with a great many personal approaches and some systems. Tbh, one of the few fantasy titles that actually went into more detail on the subject of "healing potions", which I found quite interesting in terms of logic, among other things.

However, the anime lost some of its tension and quality between episodes 12-24. The first 12 episodes were reasonably better than the later 12.

The plot of the story is extremely linear and completely simple, practically the same line runs from episodes 5-30. After the protagonist has left hell and appears in the forest, he begins to create his own empire. This of course includes expanding and educating the people and looking for allies. This is a review of the first 3 seasons, first movie, and the spinoff show "Slime Diaries" I think I can finally definitively say that I just don't like isekai/"RPG-like" anime. So the main character is basically invincible from episode 1 and can win every battle and bring everyone back to life at any time, so there's absolutely zero consequence or tension in any of the battle sequences. And the scenes in-between battles range from boring as heck medieval politics talk to "i want to touch the booby" nonsense. A lot of the development of the world and its characters just sorta happens off screen whileRimuru just narrates what happened in a rapid-fire montage. I feel like there was little to no reason for him to be reincarnated from another world, other than for him to say "my dude" over and over. The third season was... ridiculously boring. I swear that half the season just took place in the meeting room while everyone just sat completely still and talked about what they were GOING to do, rather than actually DOING anything. The spinoff show, Slime Diaries, is entirely sketch comedy/slice of life, which was more entertaining. But there's just SO many characters and no actual development for them during the main show that its hard to get attached. I feel like this was solely made to be eye candy for people who are just REALLY into phantasy creatures and RPG monsters... and boobies... lots of boobies... I honestly can't fathom why this show has been going on for so long. I also can't fathom why there have been a seemingly endless number of isekai anime in the past decade. They all look and sound more or less exactly the same. I chose this one to watch simply because it looked slightly more visually interesting than the dozens of other medieval phantasy RPG isekai shows with an overpowered protagonist and an obnoxiously long show title out there. Perhaps I chose poorly. Or perhaps there was never a good option in the first place.

Tensei shittara slime datta ken (or that time i got reincarnated as a slime) is another Isekai, in the way that follows the same tropes as other titles of the genre. This also means falling in the typical clichés of these type of stories, but it does with a lightheartedness that ends up helping the pace of the series making it a bit more enjoyable. These characteristic shows in the beggining of the show, with its informal and laid back start with Rimuru, our protagonist, getting reincarnated in this phantasy RPG styled world after dying in the present day Japan. After taking in the fact thathe died and is now in, what appears to be, a huge cave in a strange land with the body of a slime our main character set out to explore the place. While making his way through the dungeon the show explains some of the mechanics of the world as the protagonist figures them out, as well as the implications for the situation he's in, like skills and the likeky adavantages he can get through them.All this in a easy going atmosphere.

This marks the tone for the rest of the series, giving it a light pacing while the story progresses. As Rimuru gets stronger and get's allies, sorting out hurdles while gaining something in the process to overcome them this gives the viewer a feeling of fullfilment similar to watching your character develop in a MMO in the sense that every obstacle is there to reward you in some way for conquering it.
This element is there to add but also to take from the expirience, on one hand it adds to the enjoyment by watching the characters grow as the events unfold on the other it takes from the sense of struggle. Even when the protagonist runs into a sad situation doesn't really change the optimistic overall tone of the story, the same goes for danger as there's always a solution be that for the resourcefulness of the main or his over the top strength and his allie's, there is never a sense of dread.

Concluding, one could find it off putting that it is an isekai, a harem isekai at that and with overpowered characters in the main character's gang but besides that it is enjoyable overall. So if you like the genre or just are in the mood to sit down and watch an entertaining fantasy action packed animu and chill it's a good option.

Slime-Isekai is a hot steaming pile of nothing sugar coated by a good studio with very pleasing art and sound. And even though the studio carries the anime heavily, they also made some major mistakes which became apparent immediately on the first watch. And besides those mistakes the anime constantly breaks its own rules and sometimes even acknowledge this rule-breaking by its own characters, making the whole world completely inconsistent. To give a simple example of the first episode. After being reincarnated as a slime, the protagonist gains an ability "Magic Sense" to perceive magic matter in the vicinity. The very first thing he does after acquiringthat ability is to look into the reflection of the water, while still not having a visual sense. This is a an anime-only mistake, but still pulls the viewer completely out of the potential immersion.
The world in general borders so hard on MMORPG tropes that it almost physically hurts by watching it. It already starts with the concept of "unique names" and "titles" as people (and especially monsters) gain more power (whatever that means) as they receive names and titles from others. And while humans gain give names to their children without any problem, it seems to be a problem for monsters, for some reason. Apparently they spent magic to name things, but, as demonstrated by the protagonist, they recover that magic, making the convention of not naming things very illogical.

The isekai world also seems to be connected to the earth, but not really as there seems to be 2 different kind of earthlings in that world. Being reincarnated seems to be rarer as most earthlings get summoned but 30 mages over 10 days. Of course as this was explained it also was disproven a few episodes later when a mage solo-summons a young girl. However in both cases earthlings seem to get an affinity for magic while traversing.
The other possibility would be that magic can be learned by anyone, which is also likely because self-designated Rogue/Thief/Fighter classes can also use barrier-like spells, recontextualising the whole world as it only shows non-magic users in the regular daily life doing mundane things which could be trivialised with magic.

All in all, the world seems full of inconsistencies and unexplained behaviour in text and art, creating a superficial generic world out of a textbook. There are barely any thought out topics, story threads or derivative meanings behind anything shown to the viewer.

In a very similar fashion acts, or better "non-acts", the protagonist, later known as Rimuru. After being stabbed to death by a passer-by, he accidentally wishes to be reborn into a slime with devouring powers, elemental resistance and an analysing AI, which effectively only exists as an explaining tool.
He gets transported very close to one of the most powerful beings in that world. But that being is held in stasis. Naturally he devours the being and the stasis spell, obtaining some of its capabilities.
From there he falls from one situation into the next, making him a leader revered as a saint among the monsters of that region. Most notably are three things here.
First, Rimuru never acts but only reacts. Everything that happens to him and the village he inhabits happen because someone else initiated an action. Rimuru eats the powerful being. Then, the wolfs attack the goblin village. Then, he needs artisans for the village. Then, another earthlings visits the village. Then, Ogres attack the village. Then, Orcs attack the village. Then, Demon Lords attack the village. Then, an cataclysmic being attacks the village. Then, the earthling from before's plea gets answered. Everything happens because of something else. Never because Rimuru acts out of his own interests. He even admits that all he wants is a peaceful life and would like nothing more than that. And with that lack of motivation someone else has to do something so that anything can happen.
Secondly, everything is resolved instantly. There is barely any time for tension and any space to breath. Something happens and is, at most, resolved in three episodes. This creates a lot of mini-stories where only the characters are the same to 30%, and 70% new additions. There isn't any sign of a over-arcing story to follow. And the same is with the fights. Every single fight is resolved in a single strike. The only exception is a cataclysm whereas another one delivers the one-punch. On that note, this anime almost feels like it took the wrong things from One-Punch-Man and tried to apply this on an Isekai format. The greatness of OPM lies in the tension the non-protagonists create and the struggle they live through, and by the catharsis the finishing blow provides to the existing ordeal. Slime-Isekai fails miserably in all of those.
Thridly, because of the fact that everything is short-lived and Rimuru doesn't act but only reacts, there isn't much of a character. And this goes for most of the cast. Almost all of them are one-dimensional stereotypes, mostly serving a single purpose or for a joke. The best counterexample for this would be the Dwarf-King.
As he trials the main cast he ignores most of the proceedings in that trial as he sees a flawed system, eagerly prosecuting some of his most loyal people with no chance of defending themself. The anime-studio did a great job of showing his disgust as this process while also maintaining his royal aura to the tertiary cast. He later reappears to be one of the first to acknowledge the city as a federation within the continental system (although it appears more like an island the size and shape of Japan).

Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken is an anime that tries so hard to ride the Isekai wave, that it fails at almost everything the genre needs to have. An empty non-consequential world where the rules get broken all the time. Characters which fail to be more than one-dimensional, even the protagonist. A story with absent tension where everything resolves instantly and always in favour of the main cast. And the initiative hinges on the whim of shadowy figures.

It was fun whilst it lasted. And that included only for the first few episodes of the anime. And after that, it was kinda a reboot of the original overpowered SAO, along with its bullshit pointlessness. 'That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime' (I'll refer it shortened as Slime since the show basically turned out the same by its end) had an interesting start. The character dies and finds himself in an isekai (yeah, I know this part is cliché), and turns out to have reincarnated a slime (and thus the title eponym, and yeah, a rip off idea from Dragon Quest). Anyway, the initialinteraction between the dragon Veldora and the protagonist Rimuru seemed pretty enjoyable. If it was an isekai anime based on new ideas and interesting conversations, I'm all eyes and ears, but sadly the whole potential dropped out once Rimuru left that cave.

Except for a few instances within the Shizu episodes, it has been a pretty stale and predictable show ever since. A one-sided storyline, with Rimuru overwhelming every obstacle with ease. The plot pretty much went on a repetitive cycle - Rimuru finds a new race -> Helps them out -> They swear allegiance -> Rimuru moves on ahead, whilst the rest becomes characters on a wallpaper. That's basically it. The characters were poor in development. Hell, the main character is the prime example of poor and lazy writing. Lame jokes, sarcastic remarks, and the worst of all, they are all cycled later one way or the other.

I guess there's nothing much to say about the usual isekai anime. The background animation is one of the few things that can be praised, which is obvious to be better due to the development of computer and animation technology. Sadly, the brains of most of these isekai writers are stuck to the legacy of the older original games, but never coming close to the greatness of the former. These are lazy writers putting together all the previous elements that were successful into a personal ego-feeding story that turns out to be a shit sandwich with no cognizant meaning. And that's how Slime turned out after the first half-dozen episodes.

Breakdown

Story - 4/10 - I would have given a 2 or lesser, but I kinda enjoyed the initial arc of the show. At the least, there was a beginning and inevitable need for story development.

Art - 6/10 - Only for the background and CG animation. The character designs were nothing special.

Sound - 5/10 - The typical/usual isekai music, I guess.

Character - 2/10 - Kirito is one of the worst isekai characters to date, believe me, and Rimuru isn't much better. If you can't get a decent protagonist, how can you expect from the rest?

Enjoyment - 5/10 - It was a good past time if nothing else. But it indeed became hard to keep going but the later arcs, as the cringe, pointlessness, and rancidity of the show became ever prevalent.

Overall - 4.4/10 - There needs to be something special to show when an anime or TV series is being released. There was none for Slime. As for ideas in this series, everything is pretty much taken from previous fiction - JRPGs, Tolkien's universe. If you want a good fiction simply watch Lord of the Rings and play the old Final Fantasies, it's worth more the time.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime is an anime series that fails to leave a lasting impression on its viewers. While it has some interesting concepts, the execution falls short, and the show ultimately feels lackluster. One of the biggest issues with the series is its main character, Rimuru. As a slime, Rimuru lacks any discernible personality, making it difficult for viewers to connect with him. While he does gain new abilities and powers as the series progresses, there is no real sense of character development, leaving the viewer feeling detached and uninterested in his journey. Another problem with the show is its pacing. Theplot moves at a glacial pace, with very little happening in each episode. While this might work in some shows, it does not work here, as it makes the show feel stagnant and dull. Additionally, the conflicts and challenges that Rimuru faces feel contrived and lack any real stakes or tension.

The animation is also lackluster, with many scenes feeling static and lifeless. The fight scenes lack any real excitement, and the character designs are forgettable at best.

Overall, That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime is a forgettable anime series that fails to leave any lasting impact. The lack of character development, slow pacing, and mediocre animation all contribute to a show that feels uninspired and uninteresting.

tl;dr promising start devolves into repetitive, fragmented story interspersed with harem collection This will contain spoilers. I rewatched this anime recently after investigating the high rating I gave it and I find that I must change my opinion. While certainly better than most isekais, and likely one of the best overpowered MC isekai, there is a clear drop in quality after episode 7 and 14, so much so that the overall rating must fall. What Tensei Shitara does initially that other similar anime fail to do is to give its MC challenges that are not simply pushovers, a backstory development and worldbuilding, and eventually, enemies that cannot bedefeated by main force. The attention to detail is similar to what the anime version of Shield Hero pulls off, though indeed Shield Hero follows a difference premise and archetype.

However, the reason Tensei Shitara cannot be considered far above average is in its latter half, as the formula of "encounter, conflict, subjugate" with ever-stronger enemies becomes monotonous and it quickly becomes another harem collection feel-good anime.

It seems the creators felt that no stronger enemy could easily materialize, and thus rapidly changed tacks, but the jump between the Charybdis arc and the training of the students arc was abrupt and ill-explained; the students should've been included in the second season instead.

Don't get me wrong; I'll certainly watch a second season, but I wouldn't watch this anime if you were looking for a truly unique show.
